items.sum: Report of the Aylesbury Youths Relay on 7th February, where Belgrave's A team was second to Southgate Harriers by 16 seconds.
items.s: AYLESBURY YOUTHS RELAY Report of the Aylesbury Youths Relay on 7th February, where Belgrave's A team was second to Southgate Harriers by 16 seconds. This Relay was held on 7th February, and we entered four teams for this event and actually fielded three full teams. Our "A" side ran well to beat their winning time of last year, and yet were beaten by 16 seconds for first place. A. C. McLean ran the first leg and handed over in 4th place, then Gerry Lines took us up into second position. Ron Linstead did the third fastest time of the afternoon to take us into the lead, but J. B. Edgar, running in place of Frank Wright, who was down with 'flu, could not hold his opponent over the final stage. Our "B" team ran well to finish 8th, while our "C" side were placed 13th out of an entry of 28 teams, which proves how popular this form of racing is with the clubs. The winners were Southgate Harriers, who are very strong in both Youths and Juniors, and in third place were the R.A.F., Halton, boys, and their Sports Officer is none other than our own member, Eddie Short. Times of our lads were as under :— "A"—McLean, 18.33; Lines, 18.37; Linstead, 18.09; Edgar, 18.40. "B"—Hooper, 19.13; Mitchell, 18.53; Boreham, 19.06; W. Bird, 18.59. items.s: SOUTHERN R.W.A. GARNET CHAMPIONSHIP, 7th February, 1953, at Woodford Report and results of the Southern R.W.A. Garnet Championship walk at Woodford, where Belgrave's A team finished second to Essex Beagles; the text gives Burns 15th and Kemp 17th while the table gives 16th and 18th. This was held on a very cold day and on a rather hard three-lap course, with plenty of hills, but the teams really exceeded expectations. As a well-known walker reported : “We were unfancied for a scoring place,” but whatever the day or course, the lads walked extremely well. From roughly fifth place at half-way, they fought through to finish a comfortable second, the scoring lads being G. Warr 11th, B. Burns 15th, R. Kemp 17th, and G. Beecham 21st. The other lads of the two teams were always backing up, and it was a real credit to the Club to see such a fine effort from them all. Congratulations to every one of them, especially to Bobby Burns and Ron Kemp, who had travelled up from Eastleigh for this event. Percy Wright, who keeps a benevolent eye on these lads down there for the Club, must have been very pleased himself with the result. One hundred and seventeen finished. Position Name Time 1 R. H. items.sum: Report and handicap results of the annual Banstead walking match against Surrey Walking Club in snow at South Croydon, lost 148 points to 152.
items.s: ANNUAL BANSTEAD MATCH WITH S.W.C., 14th February, 1953, at South Croydon Report and handicap results of the annual Banstead walking match against Surrey Walking Club in snow at South Croydon, lost 148 points to 152. What a day ! Thick snow about and temperature near freezing, but 17 lads arrived at Croydon for this event. We were pleased to welcome our old friend, Jack Rutland, out again. Hope this will lead to many more. All the lads were content to take things easy to the turn, and coming home positions changed a little, but Syd James was first man home for us, followed closely by Hugh McGreechan and G. Checkley. Alan Robins, who is beginning to find his old form, won the handicap for our members ; he walked strongly the whole way and thoroughly deserved his win. We lost a very enjoyable match by a small margin of four points, scoring 12 aside, and congratulate Surrey W. Club on their win ; also they won their match with the M.P.A.A. The walk was followed by an enjoyable Social Evening at the Blue Anchor, Croydon. Many thanks, Surrey Walking Club. Match result, 12 a side—S.W.C., 148 pts.; Belgrave, 152 pts. Pos. items.s: SOUTHERN C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and Belgrave placings from the Southern Cross-Country Championships at Aylesford Paper Mills, with the seniors third, juniors fifth and youths sixth as teams. These were held at the Aylesford Paper Mills on 21st February and the venue left nothing to be desired both from the competitors' and the spectators' point of view. The Youths race was first on the programme and round the lap of the starting field Frank Wright was in the lead, but once they had gone out into the country, his lack of training, due to a bout of the 'flu, revealed itself, and Frank dropped back fast on the homeward run. Even so, his position of 17th, was quite good, as also was Gerry Lines' placing of 19th, but we then dropped a bit due to the absence of Ron Linstead, who was out with leg trouble. J. B. Edgar also lost both his shoes and thus found his running impeded, but on the whole our 6th placing in the team race out of an entry of 39 teams, was quite good. In the Senior race over 10 miles there was a field of 371 starters and after the usual fast start, Gordon Pirie and Frank Sando were out on their own, with Dennis Holden also in complete isolation in third place. Jack Brown was running quite well and was only beaten by the three above mentioned, plus Jim Peters and R. P. Ll. Morgan, the S.L.H. and Oxford University runner, and Jack's time was 55.41. Then came Denis Brickwood 30th, and as Denis was placed 22nd in the 1939 race, we think it a remarkable achievement for him to drop only eight places after a lapse of 14 years, and just shows what can be done with properly applied training methods. Eddie Short and John Burr also ran quite well, and our scoring team was completed by Chas. Walker and Mick Porter. To be placed third after our team had suffered so many setbacks was indeed a good performance and we doubt that even at full strength whether we should have beaten Thames Valley H., the winners of the team title, who gave a great display of sound team running. For the first time for a very long while we were unable to field a full team of 12 men, and so lost our hold on the “ Oddling-Smee ” Cup, which was won by Herne Hill. H. In the Junior race, Ray Tooby ran well to get 5th, as owing to foot trouble, he has not been able to train as hard as Bert Shaw would have liked him to. Brian Trower was 37th, with Mike Stearman 40th, and Mike was another just getting over the 'flu, and then came Don McLean, 65. We were pleased to see Geoff Goode out once again, and he looked short of training and has also put on quite a bit of weight in the Army. Here again we managed to be placed 5th out of an entry of 37 Clubs, and to get all our teams in the first six of each race can be looked upon as a good sign of our all-round strength, but we do need a few more chaps who are willing to “ slog ” it out, as did the Footer-Penny schools in the old days. items.sum: Report and Belgrave placings from the English Cross-Country Championships at Caversham Park, Reading, where the seniors were sixth team and Jack Brown won the Harry Parker Trophy.
items.s: ENGLISH C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and Belgrave placings from the English Cross-Country Championships at Caversham Park, Reading, where the seniors were sixth team and Jack Brown won the Harry Parker Trophy. These were held at Caversham Park, Reading, on 7th March, and a large crowd saw some good and exciting racing in fine weather . In the Youths' race there was an entry of 71 teams, but owing to the 2 p.m. start, which was strictly adhered to, many of the lads missed the race owing to their late arrival. Our team were all present and Frank Wright ran well to finish 8th and he beat B. G. Stone of Blackheath, who had won the Southern Youths race. We were placed 10th in the team placings, but were the 4th Southern team to finish and were only just behind Ilford A.C., the Southern champions. In the Junior race there were 68 teams entered, and our first man home was Mike Stearman, 26th, with Ray Tooby, 30th, and the latter had a bad time owing to an attack of stitch. With better support we may have been placed in the team race, but had to be content with 10th place, which, however, was an improvement on our last year's placing. The Senior race was the big event of the day and here there was an entry of 66 teams, plus 57 individual entries and a huge field faced the starter. Jack Brown was our first man home, 34th, and so won the Harry Parker Trophy, and he was closely followed by John Bromley, 39th, and John showed a welcome return to his old form once again. Denis Brickwood ran well to finish 55th, with Eddie Short 75th, and Eddie only ran in order that we should field a full team of nine men, as he has been troubled with an ankle injury. Chas. Walker was 85th and, seeing that he was running in borrowed “togs,” owing to leaving his running kit on a bus on his way to catch the Club coach at Tooting, he can be said to have run reasonably well. Eric Herbert, 87th, was our sixth scoring man, and Eric has also been troubled by injuries and has not been able to train as often as he would have wished for a race of this description. John Burr, 99th, Alan Bishop, 219th, and Len Bishop 247th, completed our team, and but for the backward position of the latter two, we should have stood a good chance of once again winning the “ Charles Otway ” Cup, which is awarded to the first club finishing its complete team, outside the three placed clubs. In fairness to the Bishop brothers we must point out that Alan only came into our team at the last moment owing to the non-arrival of Mick Porter, while Len was spiked early in the race, and this must have affected his running. We were placed 6th in the team championship and were the second Southern club to finish, and we turned the tables on Aylesford Paper Mills, who beat us in the Southern race. items.s: R.W.A. NATIONAL 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP, 14th March Report and Belgrave placings from the R.W.A. National 10 Miles walking championship at Cheltenham, won by R. Hardy of Sheffield, with Belgrave "A" seventh team. A coach party of 25 walkers and supporters travelled to Cheltenham for the Senior 10 miles Championship, and although both teams were unplaced, they very much appreciated the backing of those who made the journey to give them support and encouragement. Unfortunately, we were minus one or two of our top scorers owing to various reasons, which gives all the more credit to those who upheld the “ Claret and gold.” A one-lap course of 10 miles favoured the very fast men, and after getting away to a good start, Hardy, of Sheffield, stayed in the lead the whole journey, followed by his clubmate, R. Holland, with Brian Hawkins and George Coleman in close attendance. At 6½ miles, the two Georges, Oliver and Beecham, after their excellent County performances, were in 29th and 31st positions, with Hugh McGreechan 33rd, Garry Warr 38th, George Checkley 43rd, Percy Wright 44th, Harry Kemp 58th, Bob Readman 72nd, and Bernard Eglington 77th. Sheffield made no doubt about the result of the team race, but there was a keen struggle for the second and third positions between Highgate, Woodford, Cambridge Harriers and Met. W.C. At about 8 miles George Beecham had an attack of cramp and fell back considerably. He recovered again at about 9 miles and finished strongly, bettering his county time by 20 seconds. Bad luck came when Hugh McGreechan was “ pulled ” about 200 yards from the finish. The remainder of our walkers all made valiant efforts to put the team amongst the places and improved their individual positions considerably, but not quite enough. There was no lack of “ Belgrave spirit,” and to all we say, “ Well walked.” Owing to a delayed result, the party was split up on the return journey, but some of us met at the “ local ” in Stokenchurch and a merry time was had by all, to the scent of pickled onions, and the debate between “ The baron ” and “ Sir Harry ” on his next dramatic performance. items.s: ANNUAL DINNER AND DANCE Notice of the Club Annual Dinner and Dance at Strand Corner House on 21st November, with tickets at 17s. 6d. payable by instalments. The Club Annual Dinner and Dance, the great social event of the year, is to be held at STRAND CORNER HOUSE (not Coventry Street, as last year) on Saturday, November 21st. It is regretted that owing to the continual rise in catering costs, it is necessary to charge 17s. 6d. for tickets, but to encourage as many members as possible to be present, the Social Hon. Secretary, Dave Martin-Shepherd, is arranging for tickets to be paid for by instalments, with the aid of payment cards, and he hopes that you will start paying NOW. If for any reason you are unable to attend, any money you have paid will, of course, be refunded. The date of the dinner this year has been specially arranged so as not to clash too much with the London-Brighton Relay, and the payment system can also be used by those who are hoping to join the coach party for this race. The months will soon fly by, so don't waste any time. Get your payment cards and start saving NOW for these two important functions. Dave Martin-Shepherd Dave Martin-Shepherd Social Hon. items.sum: Announcement of a new Junior 5 miles walking championship for Tommy Green's trophy, first held on 18th April, with a prize from Syd. Roberts for a first-time walker.
items.s: NEW CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP Announcement of a new Junior 5 miles walking championship for Tommy Green's trophy, first held on 18th April, with a prize from Syd. Roberts for a first-time walker. A few years ago Tommy Green presented to the Club a very fine trophy, which was allocated to a Junior 5 miles Walking Championship. Unfortunately, owing to the shortage of Junior walkers, it has not been possible to hold a championship race until this year. It has now been decided to hold the first race for this trophy on Saturday, 18th April, the same day as the Club 20 miles Championship. So far there are about six Club walkers eligible, i.e., under 21 years of age on 1st October, 1952. Some of our foremost walkers in the past have started as runners and we now invite any member of the Club who is eligible by age and feels he would like to swell the entry, to take part in the race. This may attract some of our young members who are not quite making the grade at cross country, and who may be potential walking champions. As an added incentive, our Hon. Treasurer, Syd. Roberts, has offered to present a prize for the first competitor to finish who has not previously competed in a walking race. Why not have a go and see what you can do ? Make a note of the date NOW : Saturday, 18th April. Tommy Green Tommy Green presented trophy for Junior 5 miles Walking Championship Syd. Roberts Syd. Roberts Hon. items.sum: Preview of Belgrave's summer 1953 track and walking fixtures in Coronation Year, naming Len Marchant as new track captain and E. A. Duffett as the contact for entries.
items.s: THE SUMMER SEASON Preview of Belgrave's summer 1953 track and walking fixtures in Coronation Year, naming Len Marchant as new track captain and E. A. Duffett as the contact for entries. This is Coronation Year, and we can expect the usual crop of additional meetings due to this fact. We have already been invited to take part in meetings on Coronation Day itself, but do not think our members would appreciate having to turn out on such a day. Our first Club meeting will be at Battersea Park, on Saturday, 2nd May, and the Surrey County 7-mile track walk will be included in the programme. On Wednesday, 6th May, we visit Paddington Track for a match with Queens Park Harriers ; start at 6.30 p.m. Then on 9th May, at Battersea Park, will be held the Surrey County Youths Track Championships, with the 6 miles run and Pentathlon also at this meeting. 16th May, at the new Wimbledon Park Track, is the date fixed for the Brockman Trophy meeting, and on the same day we are holding our open 20-mile road run from Belgrave Hall, start at 3 p.m., and we are hoping for a good entry. On Monday, 18th May, we have a Club meeting at Tooting Bec, and have a Senior and Junior match against the Polytechnic H. and South London H. ; start at 7 p.m. Whitsun Saturday and Monday we see the C.A.U. and British Games meeting at the White City, and there are also the usual number of “ open ” meetings on this day. 30th May is the day fixed for the Surrey County Senior Track Championships at Motspur Park, with the Junior and Youth Relays, also the Junior Hammer Throw. On the same day we have accepted an invitation to compete in a Coronation Sports meeting at Aylesbury, with the usual generous six prizes in each event given by the Hazells Club. 6th June sees more County Championships, also a glut of Coronation meetings, and we have promised to support a meeting at the newly-opened track at Carshalton, and also to visit Walton A.C., at the Stompond Lane ground for an inter-club match. On Wednesday, 10th June we have a Club meeting at Battersea Park, start at 7 p.m., and hope to put on our annual Schools Relay at this meeting. Saturday, 13th June, is “ Kinnaird ” Trophy day, with our Club marathon championship being decided in conjunction with the Poly. race from Windsor to Chiswick. Tuesday, 16th June, we have a match with Sutton and Cheam H., at the Sutton Stadium, and this is in the nature of a “ B ” team fixture. 17th June is the date of the L.A.C. Inter-Club Relay meeting at the White City, and it is to be hoped that our members will give full support to the various events. Saturday, 20th June, is the day of the Southern Senior Track Championships, due to be held at the White City, and owing to the past large entries it may be necessary to introduce some qualifying conditions for this year's meeting. Wednesday, 24th June, we have another Club meeting at Tooting Bec Track, start at 7 p.m., and if it is decided to include any handicap events we trust they will be better supported than in the past by our members. 27th June is the day of the Surrey County Junior Track Championships at Wimbledon Park, and the Senior relays will also be held at this meeting. Also on this day there are “ open ” meetings at Weybridge and Broomfield Park, Southgate, which should attract good support. Wednesday, 1st July, we have a match at Victoria Park against the local club and the United Hospitals A.C. On Saturday, 4th July, we have the “ Heathfield ” Trophy meeting at Stompond Lane, Walton-on-Thames, and we are the joint holders of this trophy. Also on this day will be held the Southern Area Junior Championships, the venue for which has not yet been decided upon. Wednesday, 8th July, is the date fixed for our open Inter-Club Walking Competition at Battersea Park Track, where the accent is on competing for one's club, with no awards given. 10th-11th July we have the A.A.A. General Championships at the White City and tickets for the Club stands will be available from Frank Webb, as in past years. On 18th July there is the “ Waddilove ” Trophy meeting at Birmingham and we have also promised to send a team to Guildford on the same day, which should give a chance to all our members. Wednesday, 22nd July, we have a Club meeting at Tooting Bec Track, and hope to include some members' handicap events on the programme. The A.A.A. Junior Championships, also the Marathon and Relay Championships are due to be held on 25th July at Maindy Park, Cardiff, and the question of fares will come into what support our members can give this meeting. Saturday, 1st August, is Club Championship day at Battersea Park. See summer fixture card for list of events, and we hope our members will support the various events, for which standard medals are awarded. August Monday we have the “ Hazell ” Trophy meeting at Aylesbury and, seeing that our members did so well last year, I am sure that we shall not lack support for this fixture. Wednesday, 5th August, we have a Senior and Junior match at Charlton Park Track against Cambridge Harriers, and although this is the holiday season, we hope our members will endeavour to turn up for these matches. Monday, 10th August, we have a Club meeting at Tooting Bec Track, and as the evenings are drawing in at this time of the year, we shall only have a small number of events at this meeting. Saturday, 15th August, we visit Alperton for a match against Thames Valley H. and Mitcham A.C., and our Committee have agreed to the “ Doris ” Shield being put up for competition once again. There will also be a Junior match at the same meeting and as we have several members in this area this should give them a chance to represent the Club. 22nd August is the date of our final Club meeting, due to take place at Battersea Park Track, and we have arranged a Senior and Junior match with Cambridge Harriers, and it is likely that the Club 3 miles track championship will be decided at this meeting. On Saturday, 5th September, we visit Imber Court for a match against the Metropolitan Police A.C., and this will more or less wind up the track season, except for the evening floodlit meetings at the White City and the L.C.C. Championship finals, which are due to be held at Battersea Park on 12th September. We have a new track captain in Len Marchant, who most of our members will remember as a half-miler of near international class and, together with vice-captain, Dicky Bartlett, they will do their best to make sure that every member is given a chance to show what he can do. It is to be hoped that members will avail themselves of the opportunities offered them by the Club, and if any new member is in any doubt as to the method of approach, I shall be only too pleased to advise him in this direction. All entries for Club events should be sent to me at least ten days in advance of the meeting date. A card will do, and any handicap fees can be paid on the day of the meeting. Any enquiries can be sent to : E. A. Duffett, 57, Harcourt Road, Thornton Heath. Frank Webb Frank Webb Club stand tickets for A.A.A. items.sum: Club news notes on members' successes in other races, National Service postings, rugby, committee elections and club comings and goings.
items.s: HERE AND THERE Club news notes on members' successes in other races, National Service postings, rugby, committee elections and club comings and goings. Archie Bedford was first home in the British Workers' 5 miles c.c. championship, with Ron Mitchell in second place. John Burr won the L.B.H. Novices c.c. race, and Eric Bishop was second in the Inter-Banks Junior event. Brian Trower finished third in the Portsmouth A.C. open 5 miles road handicap race, with a start of 3 min. 10 secs., and has also been running with the R.A.F., Sopley. E. T. Paterson is another doing his National Service training and has been running for the R.A.F., Yatesbury, team. Another member to do well in R.A.F. events is P. N. G. Gilbert, and he captured the course record at Hednesford and also broke the R.A.F., Padgate, record. He has also twice run second to Sgt. McMinnis, the R.A.F. champion, and as he is still a junior, he should do well in future events. P. J. Rossiter is now in the R.A.F J. Hills finished second in the R.A.S.C. c.c. championship, but has now been posted to the Middle East. R. D. Knights also writes to say that he has been posted overseas with the R.E.M.E., and sends best wishes to Alf Taylor and S. Jefferson. Geoff Goode is now with the Royal Signals at Catterick, and ran in the Northern Command championships and finished 8th, and as K. L. Norris, of T.V.H., was 4th, it was evidently quite a hot field. Brian Rice, who is at Cambridge University, was reserve in the 4 x 880 for the Inter-Varsity Relays in December last, and Alan Sexton ran for Cambridge in the 4 x 110 yds., 4 x 220 yds., and the 4 x 440 yds., and led his team to victory in the latter event. A. J. Snoad was sixth in the London University c.c. race, and it is a pity that studies have prevented him from turning out for the Club, but he hopes to remedy this for next season. P. R. Bagnall was first home in an Inter-College race when running for S. Mark & S. John, and he beat several well-known runners, and should be an asset to our teams on the road and over the country. Congratulations to George Oliver on winning the Civil Service Road Walking championship, and he beat R. Carpenter, the holder, with A. H. Cotton, the Olympic walker, in third place. Syd James was second in the L.B.H. 7 miles road walk at Wembley Park, with Harry Churcher, the holder, a non-starter. We were pleased to see that B. C. Michez and M. A. Phillips, two of our youngsters from the Raynes Park County School, were selected to represent Surrey Schools XV. While on the subject of Rugby, we see that Basil Walden and D. R. Childs are playing for the very successful Streatham R.F.C., and J. Powell-Jones has now joined this club, while Alan Sexton recently turned out for his Old Boys' side There is a rumour that L. N. Bailey, the Streatham club's full-back and Surrey County player, is going to join the Club, as he wishes to go in for half-miling on the track. We send our best wishes to Vernon Blowfield, who, now that he has permanently moved down to Oxford, has resigned from the Club, and has joined the local Oxford City A.C., of which club Derrick Burfitt is also a member. We extend congratulations to Chas. Walker on once again being selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties c.c. race, also to Bob Belmore, who is a second-claim member, and to Jack Brown, who was a scoring member of the Kent team, who were third in the team championship. Also hearty congratulations to Les Cohen on heading the poll for the 20 elected members for the Southern A.A.A. Committee, and to Alf Harley, who was fourth in the voting list. At the Inter-Varsity Sports Meeting at the White City on 14th March, Alan Sexton, our quarter-mile champion, was second in the 440 yards to A. Dick, the Olympic runner. Ted Smith recently won the London Transport 7 miles walking championship. Geoff Gregory, who decided a short time ago to turn to running, has now given up the idea and is training hard for walking again. He made a good start by easily winning the Tobacco Trades 7 miles Championship in London in March and is looking forward to a successful season on the track. items.sum: Editorial announcing the Jimmy Belchamber Memorial Trophy and the Frank Thomson Cup, bringing the club's trophies to about 35.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial announcing the Jimmy Belchamber Memorial Trophy and the Frank Thomson Cup, bringing the club's trophies to about 35. Dear Fellow Belgravians, The " Jimmy Belchamber Memorial Trophy " Fund has now been closed, and a fitting trophy to perpetuate the memory of Jimmy will shortly be purchased and awarded for an event to be decided by the Committee. At the same time we place on record our gratefulness to Mrs. Smith, daughter of the late Frank Thomson for the presentation of a very beautiful cup, which will keep Frank's name for ever connected with the Club he so ably and unselfishly served, and which will also be awarded for an event to be decided by the Committee. With the addition of these two trophies our total of Club Cups and Shields will be brought up to the splendid total of some 35, and now cover every event in our curriculum of Athletics. It should be noted by all members, especially the newer members, that these trophies bear the names of illustrious Belgravians, some of them happily still with us and, we hope, for many years to come. We ask you, when admiring your trophies, to give a moment of thought to the donors who are still with us, and a reverent thought for those who have passed from us. These gentlemen and their colleagues of yore are those who pioneered so steadfastly to give you the Belgrave Club, to which you must surely be proud to be a member. The inscription on The Frank Thomson Cup reads : " Life Member for 60 years.—President, 1940-1942.—Presented as a token of life-long service to Athletics." It is truly so, and let it be an incentive to you—you for whom he did so much, many of whom he never knew. Let it never be said you knew not of him or his contemporaries or of what they did. YOUR EDITORS. items.label: No. 118
items.sum: Article by Vice-Captain Denis Brickwood on poor cross-country support, the 1953-54 fixtures, the Captain's responsibilities and training methods.
items.s: CROSS COUNTRY SEASON, 1953-54 Article by Vice-Captain Denis Brickwood on poor cross-country support, the 1953-54 fixtures, the Captain's responsibilities and training methods. I think that the main reason for poorish support during the last few seasons has been that members have been a little uncertain of what was expected of them. At the same time I believe that the Section's activities have not been broadcast nearly enough to start off on the right foot. Before I go any further I would add that my mandate for these remarks is that I am a Vice-Captain of the 1952 vintage, still in office until the A.G.M., and partly responsible for next season's activities. No matter what is organised, it will not go well if members do not give support, but I am hopeful that the programme and organisation this year will warrant this support. Firstly, the opening run will be Saturday, September 19th, earlier, of course, than usual. It is fully realised that some will not be present owing to track commitments, but there are still a lot available, and although they may not be first team men, they will be wanted for fixtures during the season. The fixtures this year are much nearer home and there should be no cry about the distance being too far. There are Home and Away fixtures, for example, with Surrey A.C. and Herne Hill Harriers ; and just another word about support—these fixtures are intended for all, and not just " A " Team men. These matters have had to be dealt with, but it will be up to the new Captain and Vice-Captains to put them into practice. Whilst on the subject of these officials, it might be a good plan to outline the responsibilities of the Captain. Firstly, he LEADS the Section, not follows it. He is responsible for implementing the season's training, i.e., he handles the tactics of his teams ; he organises the training of the packs and has the final say in their composition. He selects teams with the assistance of his Vice-Captains. He warrants your support if you give him the job. And now a word on training. I hope that the Captain and Vice-Captains, Senior and Junior, will do what they can to stamp out " Fast and slow " training and in its place can we have " Fast and medium " training. Probably the majority intend their training to be fast and medium, but I have noticed that quite often the fast is so fast that it is almost impossible to continue afterwards. Cross country running is three-dimensional—it brings in the additional element of rough ground and the resultant breaking up of rhythm. Many cross country runners indulge during the winter in track running, but whilst track running is beneficial for speed, which should have been acquired in the main during the track season anyway, it is very necessary to acquire many other manners of movement over different types of ground. Speed running takes its place amongst them and fast runners obviously make the most of good fast going. Cross country is a rugged business and it demands every quality, both physical and mental, and it has yet to be proved that it upsets track runners, particularly if they train like Pirie. Anyway, we have some very good examples in Jack Brown and Bob Taylor. What most young Belgravians seem to lack is pace and judgment, and I should like to see some concentration on them. They are first principles. Those who run with me last year will understand more easily what I am getting at ; they will remember the change of pacemakers and the resultant fluctuations in the pace of the pack. These changes were made to produce concrete examples of lack of judgment and an opportunity to get to grips with the problem. Another thing I should like to see is all the runners going out in the official packs, and coaches directing their changes in this way. Without any enlargement, the Country is a team game and the Club should learn to run as a team. Finally, I hope I shall see members running in their proper packs and conforming with the pack leader's instructions and ready to go out sharp at 3 o'clock. In these few notes on training, I realise that more justice could have been done to them, given time. They are essentially my ideas and can be wrong. Even in the twilight of a fairy athletic life, I am still learning. DENIS BRICKWOOD. items.sum: Field Events Section report on a good season, plaque wins by G. T. Gaworski and P. Luxon, the juniors' coaching and a new 120yds. Hurdles cup from Mr. J. Fell.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS Field Events Section report on a good season, plaque wins by G. T. Gaworski and P. Luxon, the juniors' coaching and a new 120yds. Hurdles cup from Mr. J. Fell. Let us begin by saying, most definitely, that the Field Events Section is having a good season and certainly an improved one up to the time of writing this report. We have done well in the Sward, Brockman, Kinnaird and Heathfield Trophies so far, which gives me considerable encouragement to look to the future. Two of our new Plaques have been won this season, viz., G. T. Gaworski winning the Discuss with a throw of 135ft. 7ins. at Walton, and P. Luxon winning the Javelin with a throw of 178ft. 7ins. at the Kinnaird Meeting. Porter is doing very well with the Hammer, and we are expecting something very good from him before the end of the season. Van Sukavachana is Pole Vaulting very well and should encourage more Club members to compete against him, when we hope to see an improvement in this branch of our Field Events. Here I would like to say that I am very pleased with the Juniors, who are turning out very regularly and getting in plenty of training and making full use of the coaching of F. Stamfl and Frank Simmons. Finally, we have to thank our Starter, Mr. J. Fell, for presenting us with a Cup in memory of his father, who was Club Starter before him for many years, for our new 120yds. Hurdles Championship, which will be held at Battersea Park on August 22nd. We hope to get a good entry for this new Championship and I want you to send your entries to me early. Please me and help yourselves and the Club by keeping up the good work. JACK CHAPPELL. Jack Chappell JACK CHAPPELL G. T. Gaworski G. T. items.s: 15 MILE MATCH v. LONDON VIDS. AND SURREY A.C., AT MITCHAM, MARCH 21st, 1953 15 mile walking match at Mitcham won by Belgrave from Surrey A.C. and London Vidarians, with Fred Rolfe winning the handicap. Owing to clashing of fixtures we were minus some of our Police members. Twenty-four started, 12 being Belgrave lads, although two represented London Vidarians for purpose of this match. George Oliver, carrying on his good form, held third place the whole way, and Harry Shields, who came along during the latter half, just managed to hold Fred Rolfe out of 4th place, but Fred's fine walk won him the handicap. Alan Robins finished very well, just in tront of Bernard Eglington, who travelled up from Salisbury and, although suffering from a sprained ankle, completed the course well. We were pleased to have our second claim members, W. Wesson and C. Gittins, with us, and although most of us got rather cold towards the end, we enjoyed the season's first fifteen, and our thanks go to London Vidarians for a good afternoon's sport. items.sum: First track fixture of 1953 at Charlton Park, won by Belgrave on points, with new track records by Bob Taylor, Ray Tooby and Jack Brown.
items.s: MATCH AT CHARLTON PARK First track fixture of 1953 at Charlton Park, won by Belgrave on points, with new track records by Bob Taylor, Ray Tooby and Jack Brown. This was the first track fixture of the 1953 season, and although most people may think that March 28th was a bit early to make a start, it did give some of our lads who were in training a chance of a run. In the 100 metres 1st string our sprinter from British Guiana, Ivan Mayers, showed a clean pair of heels to his rivals to record 11.2 secs. In the 2nd string race Ron Morrell finished third, with P. Cornish in second place. The 300 yards 1st string event was won by Dicky Bartlett in 35.4 secs., and John Benstead won the second race in 34.5. Ian Badiali was first home in the 1st string 660 yards in 87.4 secs., and Bob Taylor recorded 86.5, to set up a new track record in the second race over this distance. In the ¾-mile event Ray Tooby was first, with Frank Wright in second place, and Ray's time of 3 mins. 15.9 secs. was also a new track record. Jack Brown won the 1½ miles in another new track record time of 6 mins. 58.2 secs., while in the 3 mile event we had Bob Belmore 4th and Don Maclean 5th. The medley relay saw Alan Bishop give us the lead over the half-mile stage, but Essex Beagles beat us into 2nd place in 3 mins. 54 secs. P. C. Luxon scored a good double by winning the Long Jump with 19ft. 11½ ins., with D. B. Ansell third, and Luxon threw 137ft. 6ins. to win the Javelin Throw. T. J. Gaworski did 40ft. 0½in. to win the Weight, and the final points placings were : 1, Belgrave H., 71 ; 2, Essex Beagles, 56 ; 3, W. J. O'Bree's Team, 39 ; 4, Peckham Police, 23 ; 5, Deptford Park A.C., 8. Also included in the programme was a 2 mile Walk, which was won by Eric Hall, with our new member, Demmon, in second place. It was pleasing to see such a good turn-out by our lads, and we hope that they keep up the good work throughout the season. items.sum: Stage-by-stage report on the News of the World "National" Road Relay of April 11th, won by Thames Valley with Belgrave 4th in 3.53.44, with Belgrave stage times; the team placings print South London H. 3rd in 3.52.19, faster than 2nd-placed Birchfield's 3.52.42.
items.s: THE " NATIONAL " ROAD RELAY Stage-by-stage report on the News of the World "National" Road Relay of April 11th, won by Thames Valley with Belgrave 4th in 3.53.44, with Belgrave stage times; the team placings print South London H. 3rd in 3.52.19, faster than 2nd-placed Birchfield's 3.52.42. The third race for this trophy, promoted by the " News of the World," was held on April 11th, and although it was a fine day there was a head-wind against the runners and it looked unlikely that any records would be broken. On the first stage to Purley we had Jack Brown, and he ran well to hand over in second place behind Frank Sando, of Aylesford, in 28 mins. 22 secs. We then had Peter Bagnall, who was making his first appearance in this race. He caught the leader, but was himself passed by Don McMillan, the Australian Olympic runner, who was representing the Polytechnic H. Len Herbert went off on the third stage, which includes the stiff climb through Redhill. Len ran well to maintain our 2nd position, and his time of 22.46 was the third fastest. At this point the Poly. were leading us by 32 seconds, while we were 56 seconds in front of T.V.H., 1 min. 23 secs. in front of Birchfield, and 2 mins. 28 secs. in front of S.L.H. When selecting our team we had thought to consolidate our position over the 4th and 5th stages, but it did not work out that way. Chas. Walker did 27.01 for 5th fastest time on the 4th stage, which was well behind Arthur Bruce's record for this leg, and his time was beaten by Dalton, of Birchfield, to set up a new record. We then had Ray Tooby, who holds the record for the 5th stage, but Ray did 24.44 for the 4th fastest time, and was also well behind his record run of last October. Our position was still 2nd, behind the Poly., but the other teams were closing up and although Bob Taylor caught the Poly. runner to give us the lead, it was evident that this was not going to be as big a margin as we had hoped for. John Bromley went off with the lead over the long 7th stage, but with Pirie and Olney running stride for stride, they soon overhauled him and went well away into the lead. John endeavoured to hold on to Bobbie Reid of Birchfield and Jimmy Wood of the Poly., but was troubled with stomach cramp over the last mile and was forced to give ground so that we were now 5th. Bill Lucas ran the 8th stage for us. He did the fastest time on this leg and although gaining ground he could not catch any of his rivals. We then had Archie Bedford on the 9th stage and he ran well to record the 2nd fastest time and almost caught the Poly. runner, who was now in 4th place. Mike Stearman, also making his first appearance in this event, was doing the 10th and final stage, and as he lives in Brighton he was running over familiar ground. Mike ran well to catch Ward of the Poly. and so took us into 4th place, and his time of 18.15 was the 2nd fastest for this leg. It was interesting to note that Nankeville only did 18.43. Our total time of 3.53.44 would have won the race on previous occasions, so it was not a question of our chaps failing, but of the other clubs improving. We congratulate Thames Valley on their win, but here again they only had faster times than our lads on stages 2-5 and 7. From our point of view it was a similar race to the one in 1950, which was only won by T.V.H., with ourselves in 4th place, and in all the races held since 1932 we have never once been outside the first four places, which is a pretty good record. items.s: CLUB 20 MILES WALKING CHAMPIONSHIP Report and placings of the club 20 miles walking championship, won by Hugh McGreechan from George Checkley, with George Beecham third in his first 20. The race opened with George Oliver going into the lead, followed by George Beecham, who was tackling his first 20, Hugh McGreechan, out to hold his title, and George Checkley, all together. After the first few miles, Mac and George Checkley took over the lead and they walked together until the second time at Roehampton, when Mac had a small lead. George Beecham was showing great form on his first 20 in third position, followed by Harry Shields, Norman Guilmant and Bernard Eglington, with the others coming along steadily. Back at Lauriston Road for the last time but one, with only the hills to do, one wondered whether Mac would hold his lead, but finding some reserve, he held off George Checkley's challenge and at the same time Harry Shields was challenging George Beecham for third place, but the gap proved too great and George Beecham, in his first Club 20, took third medal. items.s: 5 MILES JUNIOR WALKING CHAMPIONSHIP, APRIL 18th The first club 5 miles junior walking championship for the "Olympic" Cup, won by Johnny Haynes after Eric Hall developed foot trouble. Preceding the 20 miles, the new 5 miles Championship for the "Olympic" Cup, presented by Tommy Green, was set on its way. Unfortunately, the field was small and a new member, who had travelled all the way from Devizes, arrived just too late to take part in the race, which promised to be a duel between Johnny Haynes and Eric Hall. Eric led round the hills, but, unfortunately, developed foot trouble on the Common and finished minus his shoes, with very badly cut feet. This gave Johnny the chance to go in front and so he holds the magnificent trophy for the first time. Len Denman, who was short of training, finished 3rd, with John Griggs, another new member, 4th. items.sum: Colchester to Ipswich open walk, where Hugh McGreechan dropped back with stomach trouble, George Beecham was 3rd and Belgrave finished 3rd team.
items.s: COLCHESTER TO IPSWICH OPEN WALK, APRIL 25th Colchester to Ipswich open walk, where Hugh McGreechan dropped back with stomach trouble, George Beecham was 3rd and Belgrave finished 3rd team. This seems an unlucky race for Hugh McGreechan. Last year he had foot trouble, and this year developed stomach trouble. From being in leading position, we lost a number of places and seemed out of the race. There was, however,a ray of sunshine. Geo Beecham Following his splendid performance in the Club 20, he was in 2nd position until about a quarter of a mile from the finish. Mac eventually recovered and made up a number of places and, backed by George Checkley and Harry Shields, we managed to finish 3rd team. items.s: MATCH v. HERCULES A.C. Report of the triangular track match with Hercules A.C. and Mitcham A.C. at Tooting, with Belgrave second in both the junior and senior points. This was our second track fixture and took place on April 29th at Tooting Track, as a triangular match between Hercules A.C., Mitcham A.C., and ourselves. Boreham second in the 1 mile in 4 mins. 46.8 secs., while our team was second to Hercules A.C. in the 4 x 110 yds. items.sum: Report of the first home track meeting at Battersea Park, a Captain's v. Vice-Captain's match for seniors and juniors.
items.s: CLUB TRACK MEETING Report of the first home track meeting at Battersea Park, a Captain's v. Vice-Captain's match for seniors and juniors. Our first home meeting was held at Battersea Park on Saturday, May 2nd, when we had a Captain's v. Vice-Captain's match for both Seniors and Juniors. In the Junior match events we saw C. R. Jones win the 100 yards, with Bellenger in second place, and these two were also first home in the 220 yards. E. Cronk won the 660 yards Junior Race, with R. D. Baines second, and in the 1,320 yards we saw A. C. McLean score a good win from S. G. Boreham and J. F. Mitchell. In the Senior events we saw Ron Holtum win the first 100 yards, with Ivan Mayers winning the second race, and Mayers also won his 220 yards race, with Dicky Bartlett winning the other 220 yards. We also had two races in the 440 yards Senior, and Bob Wolton won the first race, with "Jock" Cameron taking the second race. Wolton beat both Bob Taylor and Ian Badiali and is showing great improvement this season. In the Senior 880 yards we saw John Bromley score rather a surprise win in the good time of 2 mins. 0.8 sec., with Ian Badiali second and Chas. Walker in third place. The 1½ miles run saw "Lofty" Holden in the field as a "guest" runner, and he won in 6 mins. 54 secs. from Archie Bedford, with John Burr third. Our 1 mile Novices' run wcs won by F. H. Turner in 4 mins. 54 secs., and the 1 mile walk for Novices was won by G. Davidson. Final scores in the match events saw a tie in the Senior match at 24 points each, with the Vice-Captain's team winning the Junior match with 14 pts. to 12. C. R. Jones C. R. items.s: R.W.A. NATIONAL 20 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP, MAY 9th R.W.A. National 20 miles championship, where Belgrave lost their team title but finished 2nd to Woodford Green, with Hugh McGreechan 3rd. One of the best organised championships for years, with excellent dressing accommodation and general facilities calls for congratulations to the organisers. For ourselves, we were defending the title we won last year, and although we lost it, we certainly created a surprise by finishing 2nd. At 12 miles we were second to Woodford by the margin of 2 points. At 15 miles we had dropped to third place behind Poly. Over the last five miles, however, we gained a number of positions and finished with a total of 41 points, 14 points in front of Poly. Hugh McGreechan walked extremely well to finish in 3rd position, and George Beecham, by finishing 8th, qualified for his Club Honours Badge. They were supported by Percy Wright, 13th, and Norman Guilmant, still improving, 17th. Our thanks are due to Jack Goswell, who nearly lost his bike, Bill True and C. items.s: MATCH AT PADDINGTON Report of a triangular track match at Paddington against Queens Park H. and Ealing H., in which Belgrave finished second on points. This was a triangular match, with Queens Park H., Ealing H., and ourselves, and in the 100 yards Senior we had J. Benstead 1st with D. Gorden 2nd. D. B. Ansell was 3rd in the Junior 100 yards, and in the High Jump we had S. R. Day 1st with P. C. Luxon 2nd. Ray Tooby won the 660 yards Senior, with Jim Heathfield in 2nd place, and Bob Wolton won the Senior 300 yards, with Ron Morrell in 4th place. We also won the 2 mile team race and had the first man home in Don Maclean, and he ran really well to record the good time of 9 mins. 34.7 secs. P. C. Luxon and K. C. Key did well in the Long Jump, with D. Butler scoring points for us in the Weight. Ray Tooby turned out again in the Senior ¾-mile race and, although taking things steady, he managed to finish in 3rd place. The final event was a 8 x 220 yards relay and after a good race, D. items.s: " BROCKMAN " TROPHY MEETING Report of the "Brockman" Trophy meeting at the new Wimbledon Park Track, where Belgrave lost the trophy to Herne Hill H. by one point. This was held at the new Wimbledon Park Track, and we put up our best performance to date, only losing the Trophy by the narrow margin of 1 point. Basil Walden qualified for the 100 final, but could only finish 6th in a close race, and Denis Merrett was 2nd in the 220 final, being beaten by Clay Gibbs, of Herne Hill H. Bob Taylor ran a fine race to win the 880 yds. in 1 min. 59.6 secs, with Ian Badiali in 4th place. V. Suvachana was 4th in the Pole Vault and T. J. Gaworski won the Weight with 40ft. 11 ins., and was 3rd in the Discus with 117ft. 10½ins. Alan Law was 6th in the Weight, with D. R. Childs gaining 5th place in the Javelin, and P. C. Luxon was 2nd in the Triple Jump with a leap of 42ft. 6½ins. E. M. Bare won the High JJump with 5ft. 10ins. and, as can be seen, our field event men did very well indeed and it was not their fault that we failed to win the Trophy. Our weakness was in the 1 mile and 3 miles, and it is indeed a feature of our present strength that we have difficulty in turning out teams at these distances. items.s: SOUTHERN SENIOR RELAY Belgrave won the Southern Senior 4 x 110 yds. relay championship for the first time, at the "Brockman" Trophy meeting on May 16th. For the first time in the Club's history we managed to win the Southern Senior 4 x 110 yds. relay championship, which was held at the "Brockman" Trophy meeting on May 16th. Our team was Ron Holtum, Denis Merrett, Dicky Bartlett and Ivan Mayers, and although the latter was troubled by a foot injury, the whole team ran extremely well to beat Thames Valley H., with Cambridge H. third. The success of our sprinters speaks well for the good work that Frank Simmons and Cecil Brodie, an old Club sprint champion, are putting in at Battersea Park on training nights, also on Sunday mornings. items.s: MEETING AT AYLESBURY Report of the special "Coronation" meeting at Aylesbury, where Belgrave won the six-club match, Ron Holtum beat McDonald Bailey in the 100 yds. and Arthur Wint won the 440. This was a special "Coronation" meeting, put on by the local Mayor, who was none other than our old friend, Pat Sage, organiser of the well-known Aylesbury meeting on August Bank Holiday. The six competing clubs were: Polytechnic H., Aylesford Paper Mills, Thames Valley H., Achilles, Wycombe Phœnix H., and ourselves. In the 1 mile, John Burr ran well to finish 2nd to Eddie Ellis, of T.V.H., while in the 880 yds. Bob Taylor was also 2nd to Don McMillan, the Australian Olympic runner. Dicky Bartlett ran 3rd in the 220 yds., which was won by Brian Shenton, and then came the sensation of the meeting, McDonald Bailey could only finish 3rd in the 100 yds. and was beaten by Ruddy of A.P.M., and our own Ron Holtum in 10.1 secs. He had travelled down with the other Poly. runners by car from the White City, where they had been competing in the Caledonian Games meeting and we were hoping that Jack Brown would come down with them in order to run for us in the 2 miles event. Jack did not put in an appearance, however, and we were forced to run John Burr again, and he did well to gain 3rd place, behind Sando of A.P.M., and Norris of T.V.H. The 440 yds. saw Arthur Wint "strolling" round the track to record 50.4 secs and "Jock" Cameron ran well to gain 2nd place for us. In the final event, the 1 mile medley relay, our team of Bob Taylor, Bartlett, Holtum and Bob Wolton finished 3rd behind the Poly. and Achilles in 3 mins. 35 secs. The final match points were:—Belgrave H., 39; Polytechnic H., 36; Thames Valley H., 32; Aylesford P.M., 29; Wycombe P.H., 25; Achilles, 19. items.s: SURREY SENIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS Belgrave successes at the Surrey Senior Championships at Motspur Park, led by Alan Sexton's 440 yds. win and John Bromley's record 2 miles steeplechase. These were held at Motspur Park on Saturday, May 30th, and we had several successes, the highlights being Alan Sexton's win in the 440 yds. ,in 49.1 secs., and John Bromley's win in the 2 miles steeplechase in a new record time of 10 mins. 24.8 secs. T. J. Gaworski also did well with 2nd place in the Weight, 3rd in the Discus, and 2nd place in the Hammer Throw, which made for a busy afternoon's work. Denis Merrett was 2nd in the 220 yds. final, and Ian Badiali was 3rd in the 880 yds. R. McMullen was 3rd in the 2 mile walk and Dennis Fleming was placed 3rd in the Javelin Throw. Basil Walden, Pete Cornish and Alan Law all qualified for the 100 yds. final, but could not get placed in the first three, and Jim Heathfield also reached the 440 final. Also on the programme were the County Youths' 4 x 110 yds. relay championship, and our team of R. E. Bale, M. Booker, P. Bellenger, and R. B. Tobin took 3rd place in the final of this event. We could not field a team in the Junior 4 x 110 yds. owing to some of our lads being unable to obtain leave from their Service Units, but in the Junior Medley Relay our team of Frank Wright, J. H. On June 3rd we sent a team to Morden for a 4 x 176 yds. relay, and on a rough track our team of Ron Holtum, John Benstead, Ron Morrell and Dudley Gordon ran out winners of a close race. items.s: MEETING AT CARSHALTON Report of the "Coronation" meeting on the new Carshalton track, where Belgrave tied with S.L.H. for first in the 5-sided match. This was another "Coronation" meeting, and was held at the newly-opened track at Carshalton, opposite St. Helier Hospital. There was a 5-sided match on the programme, together with other events, also a local 100 yds. handicap, which Basil Walden won from the scratch mark in 10.4 secs. John Powell-Jones won the Weight with 40ft. 7ins., and as he was competing against Seniors, this was a very good performance and heralds well for the future. In the 100 yds. Inter-Club, Basil Walden and John Benstead both qualified for the final, in which Basil was 1st and John 3rd, which put us well ahead on points. B. F. Windley competed for us in the Long Jump, but could only finish 4th with a leap of 17ft. 10ins. J. S. Tranter ran in the 440 yds. match and was 3rd in a close run race. Ian Badiali won an Invitation 600 yds. scratch race, and he beat A. A. Martin, who beat him in the Surrey half-mile. Ian was too tired to compete again in the 880 yds., and so our runner was Len Bishop, who could only finish 4th in a slow run race. Also in the 1 mile team race we only had the Bishop brothers, plus Eddie Short, and although Eddie was 5th, our other runners brought up the rear and so we were placed 5th. In the final event, the 4 x 110 yds. relay, our team of Benstead, Gordon, Robinson and Walden, were 3rd to S.L.H. and Mitcham, and the final points in the match were :—1, Belgrave H. and S.L.H., 25 each ; Mitcham A.C., 24 ; Sutton and Cheam H., 16, and Polytechnic H., 15. items.s: " KINNIARD " TROPHY MEETING Report of the "Kinniard" Trophy meeting at Chiswick, where Belgrave were 5th in the senior match but won the Inter-Club junior match. Held at Chiswick on the 13th June and we had hoped to improve on our last year's placing of 4th, but it was not to be, and we were actually 5th, with one point less than last year. Basil Walden qualified for the final of the 100 yds., and was 5th, with Holtum unplaced in his heat. Walden and Banstead both failed to get through their heats in the 220 yds., and we missed Denis Merrett in this event. A. H. Cameron ran a fine race to get 2nd in the 440 yds. final with Dicky Bartlett running unplaced in his heat. Bob Taylor was our "highlight" of the meeting, when he did 1 min. 55.8 secs. to finish 2nd in the 880 yds., and Ian Badiali was unlucky not to qualify in his heat. Peter Bagnall also ran well to be 5th in the 1 mile, and he clocked 4 mins. 17 secs., with John Bromley an also-ran. In the 3 miles we had Chas. Walker and John Burr, and although Chas. took the lead early on, once Gordon Pirie had gone by him he dropped back to finish outside the first six. T. J. Gaworski gained his first "big" success by winning the Weight with 43ft. 8½ins., a Club best performance, and Percy Luxon threw the Javelin 178ft. 7ins., to be placed 5th. Cobden being second in the 440, while Frank Wright won the 880 in 1 min. 59.5 secs. A. C. items.sum: Eye-witness account of the Poly. Marathon, in which Geoff Pearson took 2nd in the Club Championship ahead of Arthur Whitehead, with Belgrave finishing positions and times.
items.s: THE POLY. MARATHON, JUNE 13th Eye-witness account of the Poly. Marathon, in which Geoff Pearson took 2nd in the Club Championship ahead of Arthur Whitehead, with Belgrave finishing positions and times. As an eye-witness to the Poly. Marathon from start to finish I am able to give a short account of the performance of our lads. Owing to the State Drive to Windsor by H.M. The Queen, we, the non-runners, were unable to witness the actual start. However, in ideal Marathon weather a good field got away sharp on time. At 4½ miles Denis Brickwood was nicely placed 29th and running strongly but steadily. Arthur Whitehead, Jock McDonald and Bill Wortley were close behind, while the rest of our lads were among the 100s. At 10 miles Denis' time was 61 minutes. On to 15 miles, when the race was beginning to sort itself out, Denis was having leg trouble. His time at this stage was 1 hr. 31 mins. 30 secs. Arthur Whitehead was running very strongly and seemed to be catching him, but Mac was obviously feeling the pace. The rest of the Belgrave boys were doing well. At 20 miles Whitehead was running very strongly to clock 2 hrs. 2 mins., and had passed Brickwood. Mac and Denis were very tired indeed, and at 21½ miles Denis was forced to walk. Arthur Whitehead kept going well until about 23½ miles when he began to tire and then Geoff Pearson, who had run a good steady race, came through very strongly to catch Arthur on the track and to beat him into 2nd place in the Club Championship. Mac ran in with his usual strong finish, although a very tired man, to secure 3rd place. To the rest of our lads who finished let me say most heartily "Well done." There were 142 starters and our boys finished as follows :— The actual race was won by Jim Peters in the amazing time of 2hrs. 40.2secs., and in the Southern Team Race we were 6th, and also 6th in the "Sam Ferris Cup." items.s: MATCHES AT SUTTON Report of two matches at Sutton, a Saturday match lost to Sutton and Cheam H. and a Tuesday match also including Mitcham A.C. We had one fixed for June 16th and at the last minute another one was arranged for June 13th. At the Saturday fixture we were pleased to see Dave Marshall, our old Junior sprint champion, make a welcome reappearance, and he won the 100 yds., with T. Moxon in 4th place. Marshall was also 3rd in the 220 yds., and Bob Wolton won the 440 in 53 secs., and was also 3rd in the 880 yds. J. W. Kennedy was 3rd, with Archie Bedford 4th in the 1 mile, and B. F. Windley won the Long Jump with 19ft. 5½ins. Windley was also 2nd in the Weight, with R. S. Glenn 3rd, and Dave Marshall was 3rd in the Discus, with Glenn 4th. We were beaten in the 4 x 110 yds. relay, and the final match points were : Sutton and Cheam H., 61 ; Belgrave H., 43. In the match on Tuesday, Mitcham A.C. were also present and, owing to shortage of numbers, we scored no points in both sprint races. A new member, G. E. Daniels, was 2nd in the 440 yds. and Jim Heathfield ran well to win the 880 in 2 mins. 4 secs. In the 2 miles team race we had Bill Lucas, Stan Davies, and I. S. Edmonds, and although Bill managed to get 3rd we were behind both Mitcham and Sutton in the team result. D. R. Childs was 2nd in both the Weight and Discus events, and the final points were : Mitcham A.C., 56 ; Sutton and Cheam H., 39 ; Belgrave H., 18. Although we were short of numbers for both these matches, the home club thanked us for an enjoyable match, and we hope that for any future fixtures on this ground that we have a few more put in an appearance. items.s: COMBINED MEETING WITH L.O.A.C. Report of a combined club meeting with L.O.A.C. at Battersea Park on June 15th, with club handicap races and walking events. This was held at Battersea Park on June 15th, and although it had rained hard during the afternoon, with the result that the track was almost flooded in places, it was decided to carry on with the meeting. In our Club 880 yds. handicap we saw our young member, E. Cronk, off 70 yds., score a good win in the fast time of 1 min. 54.7 secs. J. W. Kennedy (65) was second, with K. T. Rowland (50) a very close third, and the latter looks a very promising addition to our ranks. The Club 300 yds. handicap saw three heats, and Basil Walden (5) won the final, with C. W. Coxon (17) just beating P. Cornish (14) for second place. In the 2 miles run handicap the long markers had matters all their own way, and the winner was J. B. Edgar (320), with E. J. Gebbett (380) second and P. M. Childs (420) third. We had three walking events on the programme, the first being a 1 mile walk open to Schools, which was won by the lads from Stanley Technical. The next was the L.O.A.C. 1 Mile Championship, and this was won by S. Jennings, who is a daughter of one of our old Club members, and the form (?) shown by the first three in this race was certainly an eye-opener to our lads. In the Club 2 mile walk handicap we saw a new young member, R. Middleton, make good use of his long start to come home an easy winner from Eric Hall, with George Oliver third. E. Cronk E. Inter-Club Relays at the White City on June 17th, where Belgrave were 3rd in the 4 x 440 and the Victory Trophy 4 x 1 mile and finished 4th on points. Held at the White City on June 17th. All the events are in relay form, with the field events being taken on the aggregate of two members from each club. In the High Jump we had E. M. Bare, who cleared 5ft. 8ins., and S. R. Day, 5ft. 4ins., and this placed us 4th in the team result. We were also 4th in the Javelin Throw, with Dennis Fleming and D. Maddicks, but with K. C. Key straining his leg we had to call on a reserve for the Long Jump and so were not placed in this event. The Weight Put saw T. J. Gaworski doing the 2nd best putt of the evening with 42ft. 1½ins., and Percy Loxon came in to do 30ft., which gave us 5th placing. We could not field a team for the 4 x 120 yds. Hurdles event, but managed to get into the final of the 4 x 110 yds. relay. Our team of Holtum, Marshall, Walden and Mayers were drawn on the outside and with Marshall being short of training we could only finish in 6th place. The 4 x 440 yds. saw Badiali, Wolton, Taylor and Cameron all run well to finish 3rd in their heat and so qualify for the final. In this we were again 3rd to Poly. and Woodford Green, and our time of 3 mins. 25.6 secs. would have won this event in previous years. The race of the evening was the 4 x 1 mile event for the "Victory Trophy," and on the first leg we saw Jack Brown give us the lead. Chas. Walker ran well to retain this after dropping back at one stage and we then had John Burr doing the third leg. John made the pace for the first two laps, but once the leaders had gone by him he dropped back to hand over in 4th place to Peter Bagnall. Peter soon passed Walton A.C., but could not catch the Poly. and Blackheath runners, and so we finished 3rd, and it was interesting to note that the winner's time of 17 mins. 31.2 secs. was 5 seconds slower than our time of last year. In the 4 x 2 laps steeplechase we had no recognised performers in this event, and our team of Len Bishop, Don Maclean, A. C. McLean and Joe Tranter could not get placed. We hope that Joe did not suffer too much when he crashed into, or should it be through, one of the hurdles. items.sum: Report of Belgrave performances at the Southern Senior Championships at the White City.
items.s: SOUTHERN SENIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of Belgrave performances at the Southern Senior Championships at the White City. These were held at the White City before a rather poor attendance and our members who competed did quite well and worthily upheld the Club name. P. L. Porter was placed 5th in the Hammer Throw and gained Southern standard with a throw of 142ft. 3ins. T. J. Gaworski was 2nd in the Weight with 43ft. 1½ins., and so gained his Club Honours Badge, and was also 4th in the Discus with a throw of 130ft. 11ins. In the 880 yds. both Jack Brown and Bob Taylor qualified for the final, and we were the only Club with two runners in this. Although Bob ran well he could only get 4th in 1 min. 55.7 secs., while Jack Brown did 1 min. 59 secs. Ian Badiali did 1 min. 58.6 secs. in his heat, but did not qualify, and it may well be that a better method would be to take times rather than placings. Basil Walden, who was the holder of the 100 yds. title, got into the 2nd round of this event, but could not progress further, and he does not seem to be running with the same dash as he displayed last season. E. M. Bare was unlucky in the High Jump, as although he cleared 5ft. 9ins., which was the height which gained 2nd place, owing to the larger number of failures, he was eventually placed 6th. Dennis Fleming was 5th in the Javelin with a throw of 164ft. 6ins., and G. T. Olding, who is a second-claim member, ran well to finish 3rd in the 1 mile final. It was a sad reflection on our present distance strength to note that we had no entries in either the 1 or 3 mile events. In the 2 miles steeplechase, John Bromley set a fast pace and with D. G. Ross, of S.L.H., they soon dropped the rest of the field. At the bell Ross jumped away from John, who seemed suddenly to "crack," with the result that he was passed for 2nd place, and Eddie Short almost caught him down the straight for 3rd position. We had three runners pass on to the 2nd round of the 220 yds. in Denis Merrett, Ivan Mayers and Basil Walden, but only Merrett progressed further and he was eventually 4th in the final of this event. Gerry Warr was our sole entry in the 2 miles walk and he finished 7th in 15 mins. 27.6 secs. P. L. Porter P. L. Porter 5th Hammer, 142ft. 3ins., Southern standard T. J. Gaworski T. J. items.s: CLUB 20 MILES ROAD RUN Report of the second annual Club 20 miles road race at Wimbledon on June 27th, won by Geoff Iden, with Belgrave placings and times. The second annual race was held at Wimbledon on June 27th, and we had received a good entry, which comprised most of the leading road men, with the exception of Jim Peters and Stan Cox. The Mayor of Wimbledon very kindly started the race, with our own President giving him support, and the field of about 80 runners set off on their long journey. At the end of the first of the three laps, Dave Fotheringham, of T.V.H., was leading from Geoff Iden, of Victoria Park H., with Tom Richards, of S.L.H., in third place. Next time round Iden had taken the lead and Harry Dennis, of T.V.H., was fast overtaking Richards. At the finish, at the top of Lauriston Road, which was marked by a banner in Belgrave colours stretched right across the road, above the heads of the runners, we saw Geoff Iden run in a good winner in the fast time of 1 hr. 53 mins. 27 secs., which was about 3 minutes better than last year's time. Fotheringham, who was the winner last year, ran in 2nd, with Dennis close behind, then came Goodsell, of Walton A.C., Hefford, of Woodford Green, and Tom Richards in 6th place. First man home in our colours was actually R. G. Plummer, who finished 13th, but he is not yet qualified to represent us in open team races. This made J. McDonald, who was 26th, winning the award for first Club man home, and he was closely followed by Lou Bush and Frank Mitchell. All the competitors expressed their appreciation of the way the race was organised and their comfort attended to, a thing that is overlooked in some promotions, and we can be sure of good support for next year's race. We must thank all those who gave a hand at the sponging points, also for working out the result, etc., and a Roneod sheet was available to all competitors a short time after the finish of the race. Placings and times of our runners were :— 13, R. G. Plummer, 2.06.14; 26, J. McDonald, 2.18.14; 27, L. Bush, 2.19.26; 28, F. Mitchell, 2.20.08; 34, G. R. Chantler, 2.25.41; 37, A. T. items.s: CLUB MEETING AT TOOTING Report of a Senior and Junior match at Tooting on June 24th against Herne Hill H. and Mitcham A.C.; Belgrave won the senior match and were second in the junior. Held on June 24th as a Senior and Junior match with Herne Hill H. and Mitcham A.C. as our opponents. In the Junior events we saw Frank Wright win the 880 yds. in 2 mins. 0.9 secs., with A. C. McLean in second place, while J. B. Edgar was 2nd in the 1 mile. Alan Law won the Weight, and H. Powell, the son of our old champion, George Powell, followed in his father's footsteps by winning the Javelin Throw. S. R. Day won the High Jump with a leap of 5ft. 6ins., and the final match points were : Herne Hill H., 50 ; Belgrave H., 40 ; Mitcham A.C., 7. In the Senior events Ron Holtum won the 100 yds. and was 2nd in the 220, while Bob Wolton was 2nd in the 440 yds. Ian Badiali won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 59.1 secs., but nearly lost the race by easing at the tape, and Chas. Walker ran well to win the 1 mile in the good time of 4 mins. 22 secs. Bob Belmore turned out for us in the 2 mile run and was 3rd, with Maynard, of H.H.H., doing 9 mins. 23.5 secs. T. J. Gaworski won the Weight and was 2nd in the Discus, and P. C. Luxon was 3rd in the Long Jump. We were 3rd in the 4 x 110 yds. relay and it looked as if some baton-changing practice would not come amiss to our lads. What about it, Frank ? items.s: SURREY JUNIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the Surrey Junior Championships at Wimbledon Park on June 27th, with C. R. Jones winning the 100 yds., and Belgrave unable to field sprint relay teams in the Surrey Senior Relays. These were held at Wimbledon Park on June 27th, and also on the programme were the Surrey Senior Relays. In the Junior events we saw C. R. Jones score a good win in the 100 yds. final and his time of 10.4 secs. was a tribute to Frank Simmon's coaching. Frank has now had three Surrey Junior champions through his hands, the other two being Alan Sexton and Dave Marshall. Ron Linstead was 4th in the 1 mile and C. R. Jones also finished 3rd in the Hop, Step and Jump. Owing to Basil Walden and Denis Merrett being picked to run for the A.A.A. in Wales on this day, we were left short of sprinters and so could not field a team in the Senior 4 x 110 yds. relay championship. Ian Badiali and Pete Cornish were also the only two present for the 1 mile medley relay, and so we also had to scratch from this. A poor showing, some might say, but not one entirely of our own making, as Jim Heathfield was also away on holiday,. and it must be remembered that quite a number of our lads have Middlesex qualifications and so cannot run for us in Surrey County events. There were six clubs competing for the Shield, of which we were the joint-holders. Ron Holtum was 4th in the 100 yds. final, and won a Lamp and Shade, while "Jock" Cameron won the 440 yds. final, and so got himself a fine canvass Holdall, and we are asking the promoters to put up a Track Suit for next year's race ! items.sum: Report of the Belgrave Harriers Inter-Club Walking Contest at Battersea, won by Metropolitan W.C. with Belgrave third after Johnny Haynes was disqualified.
items.s: BELGRAVE HARRIERS INTER-CLUB WALKING CONTEST, BATTERSEA TRACK, JULY 8th Report of the Belgrave Harriers Inter-Club Walking Contest at Battersea, won by Metropolitan W.C. with Belgrave third after Johnny Haynes was disqualified. This year we really deserved our placing in this contest. After last year's poor effort, we redeemed ourselves and were within an ace of winning until the last 20 yards of the last race, when Johnny Haynes unfortunately came under the judges' disapproval and was disqualified. This meeting continues to be as popular as ever and is obviously looked forward to by London Clubs, judging by the way they give it their full support. For close on 90 walkers to turn out on a mid-week evening shows there is no lack of enthusiasm in the walking world, particularly for a meeting where there are no prizes at stake. Disqualifications were very few and 84 walkers were timed in over the four races. Lack of space prevents us from publishing a full result, but the contest resulted in a win for Metropolitan W.C. with 156 points, Woodford Green 2nd with 144 points, and Belgrave 3rd with 143 points. items.sum: Report of Belgrave performances at the A.A.A. Championships at the White City on July 10th-11th.
items.s: A.A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of Belgrave performances at the A.A.A. Championships at the White City on July 10th-11th. Held at the White City on July 10th-11th, and on the Friday we saw the heats of the 100 yards, and we had Holtum, Mayers and Walden competing, but without success. E. M. Bare cleared 5ft. 10ins. in the High Jump, but the qualifying height was 6ft., and it is interesting to note that there were seven competitors who cleared this. In the 880 yds. we had Ian Badiali and Bob Taylor, but with the slowest of the four heats being 1 min. 55.4 secs., neither of our runners could qualify for the final. Our only competitor in the 440 was A. H. Cameron, and he retired owing to a damaged leg in his heat and it was a great pity that Alan Sexton was not available for this event. In the 220 yds. we saw Denis Merrett doing 22.3 secs. in his heat, which was won by McDonald Bailey in 21.3 secs., and he thus qualified for the semi-finals. With the first three in each going through to the final we saw Denis just pipped for third place. T. J. Gaworski did 43ft. 8ins. in the Weight to gain 5th place and so gain a standard medal. In the 1 mile we had our big thrill of the evening when Jack Brown won his heat, beating Bill Nankeville in the fast time of 4 mins. 12 secs., a personal best performance. Peter Bagnall and Chas. Walker also competed, but here again, with the slowest heat showing 4 mins. 17.8 secs., neither of them could gain a place in the final. We had no runner in the 6 miles race, which was won by Gordon Pirie in the new world record time of 28 mins. 19.4 secs. On the Saturday we saw our Junior 4 x 110 yds. relay team of Moxon, J. Smith, C. R. Jones and Ansell score a good win in their heat to qualify for the final. In this the Poly. lads were the winners in the good time of 43.9 secs., which was much too fast for our boys. The 1 mile final was won by Roger Bannister in 4 mins. 5.2 secs., a new championship record, and Jack Brown was 6th. We saw Charlie Smart, home from Germany, running in the 3 miles event, but he found the pace too fast for him and this was another win for Gordon Pirie in 13 mins. 43.4 secs. We had two runners in the 2 mile steeplechase in John Bromley and Eddie Short, and in the early stages John was running well in 4th place. He came a cropper at the water-jump and was carried off with a damaged ankle, which was certainly very bad luck, and we trust he will soon recover from his injury. Eddie Short had now moved up and eventually finished 5th in 10 mins. 28.4 secs., which is quite good going. From the Club point of view we did not have any successes, but think our lads performed creditably in view of the ever-increasing standard in both the running and field events. items.sum: Report of a "Coronation" Cup inter-club meeting at Guildford, where four Belgrave men took the club to third place.
items.s: GUILDFORD MEETING Report of a "Coronation" Cup inter-club meeting at Guildford, where four Belgrave men took the club to third place. This was a "Coronation" Cup affair, with six clubs taking part, and there were five track events, with one field event. We only had four men turn up and D. Gordon was 3rd in the 100 yds. and 4th in the 220. G. E. Daniels was 4th in the 880, with Len Bishop being 3rd in the 440 and he also won the 1 mile in 4 mins. 32 secs. D. E. Childs was third in the Javelin and the final points were : Dorking St. Pauls A.C., 21 ; Polytechnic H., 14 ; Belgrave H., 13 ; South London H., 8 ; Walton A.C., 7 ; Herne Hill H., 3. It was a pity that we did not have more members present to run on this fine grass track, but as they intend to make this trophy an annual affair, we hope for a better turn-out next time. D. Gordon D. items.sum: Report of the "Waddilove" Trophy meeting at Birmingham on July 18th, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 2nd, and the accompanying Junior match for the "Grenville" Cup.
items.s: "WADDILOVE" TROPHY MEETING Report of the "Waddilove" Trophy meeting at Birmingham on July 18th, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 2nd, and the accompanying Junior match for the "Grenville" Cup. Held at Birmingham on July 18th and, owing to holidays and injuries, our team was much depleted. Denis Merrett won the 100 yds. in 10.3 secs., but we had no finalist in the 440, and although Peter Bagnall qualified for the final of the 880 yds., he found the effort too much for him and failed to finish. Owing to Len Herbert crying off with a leg injury, plus the fact that the Civil Service meeting took away Jack Brown, Bob Taylor and Chas. Walker, and Ray Tooby was competing at the Inter-Banks, we were unable to field a team in the 2 miles team race. In the 1 mile medley relay our team of Jim Heathfield, Bob Wolton, Merrett and Key finished 4th, and so scored three points. It was in the field events that we scored best and our men are to be congratulated on their fine showing. T. J. Gaworski won the Discus with 132ft., while Dennis Fleming was third in the Javelin with 157ft. 5ins., and Percy Luxon was 4th in the Hop, Step and Jump, and K. C. Key was 5th in the Long Jump. Our Siamese member, V. Suvakachana, went to compete in the Pole Vault, but was unlucky to fall heavily when making his initial effort and so had to retire. Final match points were : 1, London A.C., 50 ; 2, Belgrave H., 24 ; 3, Birchfield H., 22 ; 4, Herne Hill H., 18 ; 5, Walton A.C. and Polytechnic H., 17 each. Also at this meeting was a Junior match for the "Grenville" Cup, of which we were the joint-holders, but owing to National Service calls our team was also short of numbers. C. R. Jones, the Surrey Junior champion, won his heat in the 80 yds., but was unlucky to be disqualified in the final for two false starts. J. H. Cobden ran well to gain 3rd place in the 880 yds., and we missed Frank Wright, who had to report at Kingston for service with the East Surrey Regt. Our team in the 4 x 110 yds. relay could only finish 4th in their heat, while we only had two runners in the 1 mile team race, but J. B. Edgar ran well to finish in 4th place. D. Maddicks competed in the Javelin event but his effort was ruled "no throw." Denis Merrett Denis Merrett won 100 yds. in 10.3 secs.
