items.s: CLUB MEETING AT TOOTING, JULY 22nd Report of a rain-hit club meeting at Tooting on July 22nd, planned as a Captain's v. Vice-Captain's match, including the Club 3 mile track championship won by Jack Brown and field event handicaps. A heavy downpour of rain just before the meeting started kept down the spectators and also accounted for our shortage of numbers present. It was intended to make this another Captain's v. Vice-Captain's match, but we could not hold a full list of events, and the points total on those held was 18 each. In the 100 yds. Basil Walden just beat Ron Holtum, with Pete Cornish in third place. The 880 yds. Junior was a good race, with Steve Boreham just pipping D. Pettican, with J. Palmer third. In the 880 yds. Senior race we saw Len Bishop score a good win, with Joe Tranter second and a new member, Shackleford, in third position. The 2 miles walk handicap was won by Eric Hall, with George Oliver second and L. Demmon third, and the back-markers did not seem to have much chance of catching their field. Alan Picton, making a reappearance, won the 220 yds. with Cornish second and Bob Wolton third. In the 440 yds. we saw Dicky Bartlett beat Bob Taylor, with Jim Heathfield in third place. The " big " event of the meeting was the Club 3 mile track championship, and the holder, Jack Brown, retained his title in 14 mins. 31.4 secs. Chas. Walker, who had made the pace in the early stages of the race, was second, with Bill Lucas, still retired, in third place. Then came Ray Tooby, John Bromley, Bob Belmore, Ron Linstead, G. Davidson, George Stace, S. Gawler, John Burr, Peter Courtney, Eric Gebbett, and " Spud " Abbott, and all these were inside the 1st-class standard time of 15 mins. 45secs. We also held a couple of field event handicaps, and with Jack Chappell and Bert Ellsey away on holiday, these were looked after by Mr. O'Hara, who made a very good job of it. In the Hop, Step and Jump we saw K. C. Key win the handicap, with Percy Luxon second and Dennis Fleming third. The Discus Throw handicap was won by Dave Ansell, with D. R. items.sum: Report of Belgrave performances at the A.A.A. Junior Championships at Cardiff on July 25th, which also included the Senior relays and the Marathon championship.
items.s: A.A.A. JUNIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of Belgrave performances at the A.A.A. Junior Championships at Cardiff on July 25th, which also included the Senior relays and the Marathon championship. These were held at Cardiff on July 25th, and included in the programme were the two Senior relays and the Marathon championship. In the latter we had R. G. Plummer, who finished 8th in the good time of 2 hrs. 39 mins. 12 secs., and he will be a great help to our road teams when he is qualified. Our only success in the Junior events was the 2nd place in the Weight by John Powell-Jones, who did 49ft. 0½ins., which was only beaten by the winner with his final effort. S. R. Day did well to gain a standard medal in the High Jump by clearing 5ft. 7ins. C. R. Jones in the 100 and J. Smith in the 220 yds. both failed to get through their heats, as did J. H. Cobden in the 440 yds. R. D. Baines also failed in his heat of the 880 yds., but Frank Wright qualified for the final of this event by being placed 2nd in his heat. Whether it was due to his Army training, the fact remains that Frank could not get a place in the final and so vanished our last hope of a winner's medal. In the senior 4 x 110 yds., our team of Basil Walden, Ron Holtum, Denis Merrett and Ivan Mayers won their heat in 44.1 secs., the same time as the Polytechnic H., who were the eventual winners. On the heat form we should have been a good second to them, but in the final Ivan Mayers pulled a leg muscle when running the last 110 yds. and so we were out of the race. The 4 x 440 yds. saw only six teams competing and so this event was run as a final and we finished 5th, and at least our team of Bob Wolton, Jim Heathfield, Bob Taylor and " Jock " Cameron had the satisfaction of beating the Midland champions, Coventry Godiva H. We sadly missed Alan Sexton, still out in Canada, while Ian Badiali was away on holiday and " Jock " was just getting over his leg trouble, so we hope for better luck next year. R. G. Plummer R. G. items.s: CLUB TRACK CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the Belgrave Club Track Championships at Battersea Park on August 1st, with several new championship bests, a list of standard medal winners and members' children's races. Our Club Championship Meeting, held at Battersea Park on Saturday, August 1st, was witnessed by a good crowd of spectators, who saw several new championship records set up. In the 100 yds., Basil Walden just beat Denis Merrett in 10.2 secs., which equalled the previous best time, with Ron Holtum in third place. The 100 yds. Junior saw C. R. Jones beat J. Smith in 10.7 secs., with T. Moxon third. Dennis Trower, the third brother of this family to join the Club, won the 100 yds. Boys' race in 11.5 secs., with P. Heywood second and B. Pritchard third. In the 220 yds. Denis Merrett reversed the short sprint result by beating Basil Walden, with J. D. Benstead third, and the time of 22.7 secs. also equalled the previous best time. A similar reversal of placings was seen in the 220 yds. Junior, with J. Smith beating C. R. Jones, with T. Moxon again third. The 440 yds. saw A. H. Cameron score a good win from Bob Wolton in 51.6 secs., with Ian Badiali in third place. In the 440 yds. Junior J. H. Cobden won easily in 54.4 secs., with E. Cronk second and G. Flower third. Bob Taylor won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 58.3 secs., which is a new championship record, and Len Bishop was second, with Jim Heathfield in third place. K. Rowland ran well to finish 4th, and should do well with further racing experience. The 880 yds. Junior was won by the holder, Frank Wright, in 1 min. 59.6 secs., with J. H. Cobden second a few yards behind, and a new member in H. B. Foster in third place. Jack Brown came over from the White City where he had been running for the Great Britain " B " team in the attack on the 4 x 1 mile world's record, and he successfully defended his 1 mile title, beating Chas. Walker in 4 mins., 25.6 secs., and Len Bishop again ran well to gain third place. The 1 mile Junior saw a surprise win with R. D. Baines beating J. B. Edgar in 4 mins. 39.8 secs., with Frank Wright third, and quite a number of the competitors gained a standard award in this event, which is a good sign for the future. R. McMullen won the 2 miles Walk, after a long string of second places, and his time of 15 mins. 5.4 secs. was quite good after his lay-off during the winter season. G. Oliver was second, with Syd James in third place. In the Field Events we saw some good performances, pride of place going to T. J. Gaworski, who set up new best figures in both the Weight and Discus. In the former he did 42ft. 10ins., with Alan Law second and P. C. Luxon third, beating D. R. Childs by a quarter of an inch. The Discus Throw saw Gaworski do 129ft. 2½ins., with D. R. Childs second and a new member in T. H. Strang in third place. Dennis Fleming won the Javelin Throw with 161ft. 10ins., another new championship best, and P. C. Luxon was second with D. Maddicks third, and the latter is actually a junior but seems to do better with the senior implement. E. M. Bare won the High Jump with a leap of 6ft. 1in., to set up a new championship best, and S. R. Day was second, with P. C. Luxon in third place. S. R. Day also set up new figures for the Junior High Jump with 5ft. 8ins., and C. R. Jones was second with, a new member, T. Upperdine, in third position. In the Long Jump we saw P. C. Luxon retain his title with a jump of 21ft. 10½ ins., and D. B. Ansell was second with 21ft. 2ins., and K. C. Key in third place with 20ft. 7ins., all very good performances. Standard medals were gained by the following:— 220 yds., Senior.—D. Gordon, P. Cornish, R. Holtum. 440 yds., Senior.—R. Bartlett, J. Heathfield. 880 yds., Senior.—K. Rowland, A. Bishop, J. Masters. 1 Mile, Senior.—J. Bromley, J. E. Burr, S. Gawlor, P. Courtney. 1 Mile, Junior.—R. Linstead, S. Bor[illegible]ham, W. Bird, P. Childs, M. Courtney, H. Powell. 2 Mile Walk, 2nd class.—E. Hall, H. McGreechan, J. Haynes, G. Beecham. Javelin.—C. Melchior, D. Childs, G. Powell, H. Powell. High Jump.—K. C. Key, R. Holtum, T. H. Strang. Discus.—D. Fleming, A. G. Law, P. C. Luxon, C. Melchior, P. Porter. Weight.—D. Childs, C. Melchior. Also on the programme were some members' children's races, and in these we had the names of several well-known Club personalities, with Diana and Frances Cohen, Elizabeth and Valerie Cook, Jean Chantler, David Bradnum, Michael Stimpson, Peter Marchant and Clifford Redgrave. The awards were presented by our President's wife, and all present agreed that it had been a very successful meeting, for which we wish to thank those competitors who turned out, also the many officials who gave a hand. items.s: CLUB RECORDS Additions and amendments to the Club records lists by Colin Collis, followed by Gordon Doubleday's recollection of Arthur Penny's run in the 1936 A.A.A. 6 miles Championship. Here are some more additions and amendments to previously published lists of Club records. I should like to thank all those who have helped me with the information about their own and others' performances. Track, Senior—Amendments— 440 yards—A. D. Sexton, May, 1953, 48.2 secs. 6 miles—J. C. Smart, April, 1953, 30 mins. 16 secs. 1 mile—J. Brown, July, 1953, 4 mins. 12 secs. Track, Junior— 1 mile walk—J. Rutland, May, 1936, 7 mins. 31 secs. Field Events, Junior— 120 yds. hurdles—P. J. Briggs, July, 1946, 16.6 secs Field Events, Senior—Amendment— 2 miles Steplechase—J. Bromley, May, 1953, 10 mins. 19 secs. Shot Put—T. Gaworski, June, 1953, 43ft. 8½ins. N.B.—I am awaiting definite news of Alan Sexton's recent brilliant quarter miling in America. COLIN COLLIS. In addition to the above, we have just received the following from Gordon Doubleday :— " Glancing through the Club records has recalled the A.A.A. 6 miles Championship of 1936, the year of the Berlin Olympic Games. In this race Arthur Penny finished 5th. The winner Noji (Poland) set up a new British record of 29 mins. 43.4 secs., whilst runner-up A. Burns, Elswick Harriers, set new figures for the native British record. Arthur's time was 29 mins. 57 secs., and he still has his lap times carefully recorded. items.s: THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW Club notices on the Jimmy Belchamber Memorial Trophy Fund, tickets for the London v. Stockholm floodlit meeting, the Southern Garnet Cup award, the A.G.M., subscriptions, the Treasurer's change of address and the annual dinner. As announced in our Editorial, the " Jimmy Belchamber Memorial Trophy Fund " has now been closed. Our Secretary, Alf Harley, who has been responsible for the recipt of donations for the Fund, is prepared, however, to receive any late donations prior to the purchase of a suitable trophy to commemorate the memory of Jimmy Belchamber. FLOODLIT INTER-CITY MATCH It is brought to your notice that tickets for the Floodlit Meeting, London v. Stockholm, at the White City on Wednesday, September 23rd, 1953, may be obtained from Frank Webb. Your wholehearted support should be given to this meeting, and it is interesting to know that the Club will have some part of the proceeds. Apart from this, a really fine evening's sport is assured and it is advisable to book your tickets, preferably with cash, with Frank at an early date. The Southern Garnet Cup (10 miles Walking Championship) has now been awarded to Belgrave Harriers. The actual winning team included an ineligible man in their team and as a result Belgrave Harriers (originally second) now become holders of this title and trophy. ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING Be sure to book in your diaries—THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8th—which is the date of the Belgrave Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall. Your attendance is particularly requested, and apart from the fact that you should be interested in the general management of your Club, and the election of those who will officiate in various capacities, you will find our A.G.M. most interesting, informative and possibly entertaining. The Club financial year ends on September 15th. Syd Roberts, our Treasurer, is most anxious to close his books with all subscriptions paid up. You elected Syd to be your Treasurer last October. It is only fair to help him to present his first Balance Sheet with a record paid up subscription item. If your subscription is still unpaid, will you please make a special note of sending it before September 15th to S. C. Roberts, 35, Perrymead Street, Fulham, S.W.6 (Please note next paragraph.) SPECIAL NOTICE—CHANGE OF ADDRESS From August 29th, 1953, our Hon. Treasurer's address will be :— 4, DERWENT AVENUE, EDMONTON, N.18. Please make a note of this in your diaries, etc. (just in case you wish to send him something.) THE DINNER Tickets for the highlight of the social side of the Club are now obtainable from Dave Martin-Sheppard. A really good night is assured. Book the date—Saturday, November 21st, and your ticket, price 17s. 6d. items.sum: Club news column covering injuries, members' performances at summer meetings, Alan Sexton's running in America and Canada, Charlie Smart's racing in Germany, new member R. G. Plummer, and members in the Services.
items.s: HERE AND THERE Club news column covering injuries, members' performances at summer meetings, Alan Sexton's running in America and Canada, Charlie Smart's racing in Germany, new member R. G. Plummer, and members in the Services. Near the end of the winter season, Eddie Short was in hospital suffering from a kick in the back, sustained while playing for the camp Rugby team, and who should be in the same R.A.F. ward but E. G. Read, our old sprint champion. Ted was very badly knocked about in a plane crash, but is progressing after several operations, with the prospect of more to come and we wish him a full recovery from his serious injuries. At the London v. Paris Schools meeting at the Wimbledon Park Track, Alan Law won the weight with a put of 44ft. 11¼ins., and at the same meeting our Junior team won the 1 mile medley relay open to clubs. Our team was: Frank Wright 880, T. Adams 220, J. Smith 220, J. H. Cobden 440. Charlie Smart ran well in the Southern 6 miles track championship and in finishing 4th he recorded 30.16, which is very good running. At the Leyton Floodlit meeting we fielded a team in the " A " section of the medley relay race and were placed 3rd to the Polytechnic H. and Achilles. We could not field a team in the 3 miles team race, but Alan Sexton was 3rd in the 440 yds., John Bromley was 2nd to Disley in the 3,000 metres steeplechase and Frank Wright won the 1 mile Junior race in 4 mins. 29.4 secs. Our members did well at the Charlotteville " open " meeting on Whit-Monday, and Ivan Mayers and Ian Forrester were 1st and 2nd in both the 100 and 220 yds. handicaps. We also had first two in the 880 yds., and Jim Heathfield just "pipped" Bob Wolton for 1st place. Our team of Ian Badiali, Ron Morrell, Bob Wolton and " Jock " Cameron also won the 1 mile scratch relay in the good time of 3 mins. 36.8 secs. At the " Sward " Trophy meeting at Chiswick we had entered a team for the 2 miles team race, but only Chas. Walker put in an appearance, and he ran as an individual and was second to P. B. Driver in 9 mins. 28.8 secs. In the Croydon v. Arnhem sports meeting we had several Club members competing, and Bill Lucas was 3rd in the 3 miles event, while Dick Savage was present as a Timekeeper. Alan Sexton has gone to America with the Combined Universities team and won the 440 yds. in 49.9 secs., and was 3rd in the 100 yds. against the American team. He is then going on to Canada to compete in their championships and does not expect to be back in this country until the end of August. This means that he will miss our Club Championships and will be unable to assist us in the A.A.A. 4 x 440 yds. relay, but we wish him the best of luck in his travels. More of our Junior members continue to go into the Services, and D. G. Hooper and T. Adams are both stationed at Hednesford in the R.A.F. Frank Kemp is now out in the Middle East with the R.A.F., and sends best wishes to all his Club-mates. He has a brother of Basil Walden stationed with him and says he has done 10.1 for the 100 and 22.5 for the 220, so keep up the good work, Frank ! We sent a team over to the W. H. Smith & Son sports for an open 2 mile team race, and Chas. Walker was first home in 9 mins. 38 secs., with John Burr 3rd and Bill Lucas 5th, and they won the team event, beating Finchley and the Poly. H. At the Vickers' meeting at Weybridge we again won the " Viking " Trophy, presented to the winning team in the 2 mile team race. John Bromley ran well to finish 3rd, with Jack Brown 5th, Chas. Walker 7th and Bill Lucas was our non-scoring runner. Another success at this meeting was Ron Holtum's win in the 100 yds. open handicap event. We are pleased to welcome R. G. Plummer, late of Oxford City A.C., to our ranks. He is a well-known long-distance runner and should strengthen our road teams once he is qualified to represent us in open competition. Alan Sexton is now being quoted as Britain's fastest-ever runner over 440 yards. He was beaten by a yard in the Canadian National quarter-mile race by Jack Carroll, the Canadian Olympic runner, in the fast time of 47 secs. His time was given as 47.2 secs., which is 2/5ths faster than Godfrey Brown's best-ever British performance at the White City in 1938. The Press state that Alan only took up quarter-miling last autumn at Cambridge, apparently overlooking the fact that Alan won our 440 yds. Club championship last season. At the Insurance A.A. championships, Percy Luxon won the High Jump with a leap of 5ft. 9ins., thus beating the best championship performance, which was put up in 1934. Charlie Smart writes from Germany to say that he has had ten races over 5,000 metres so far this season (four of them at International meetings), and has won nine and been second to Mimoun, the French Olympic runner, in the other. His last two races were in the B.A.O.R. Championship, which he won in 14.55 (a new record), and at an International meeting near Saarbrucken also in 14.55, which is a new Saarland record. These times for 5,000 metres are equivalent to 14.23 for 3 miles, and Charlie says that the standard of German distance running cannot compare with present U.K. times. We offer our sincere congratulations to Eric Bishop on his recent marriage. Eric does a very good job of work in getting the prizes and medals for the various Club races. Our Pole Vaulter, Van Sukavachana, competed in an invitation event at the Heathfield meeting, and although he cleared the same height as the winner, he was placed 3rd on the number of failures. Congratulations to Hugh McGreechan on winning the Surrey W.C. 14 miles Keston race on March 21st, and also winning the Police Long Distance Championship—Barking to Southend—for the third time. Harry Shields won the London Transport 10 miles Championship, with Bill Wesson 2nd, on April 7th. Gerry Warr was 2nd in the University one mile at Motspur Park on May 7th. Charlie Speechley—like Johnny Walker—still going strong, won the handicap in the Veterans' match at Parliament Hill on May 20th. Percy Wright was 2nd and Gerry Warr 3rd in the Hampshire County 2 miles Championship. Ted Smith took second place in the Business Houses 2 miles Track Walk on July 15th in 15 mins. 24 secs. George Oliver won the Civil Service 2 miles Track Championship on July 18th. Gerry Warr has now gone into the R.A.F. for his National Service. At the National Schools Championships at Uxbridge, John Powell-Jones was competing for Surrey in the Senior Weight, and he won with a putt of 45ft. 1½ins. P. L. Porter won the Essex Hammer Throw and is improving each time out. We have heard that Don Maclean and Geoff Goode are now both out in Korea, while Ian Forrester is also serving in the Far East, and we hope that these lads will still retain their interest in running once their enforced absence is at an end. At the Civil Service championships, Jack Brown won the 1 mile, beating Len Eyre, while Bob Taylor won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 56.9 secs. At the newly-opened Croydon Track was held an Inter-County match and we had four winners at this meeting, as follows : Bob Taylor (Middx.), 880 ; Jack Brown (Kent), 1 mile ; T. J. Gaworski (Surrey), Weight ; K. C. Key (Middx.), Long Jump. John Bromley won the Army steeplechase title in a new record time, and was 3rd in the Inter-Services event, with Eddie Short (R.A.F.) in second place. Peter Casselton, our Junior 440 yds. champion, is now in Germany with the B.A.O.R., and ran in the championships out there, but found that Army life is not good training for running. The Wandsworth Council promoted a 14 miles road run in connection with their Coronation celebrations, and Geoff Pearson finished 3rd, with Len Rolls 8th and Bert Smith 15th. E. M. Bare, our high jumper, competed for an A.A.A. team at Eastbourne in a match against a combined Sussex and Kent side, and was second in the high jump with a leap of 6ft. R. J. Harris, our former Discus champion, is now in Singapore with the R.A.F., and at a recent Inter-Services meeting he did 40ft. 9ins. with the Shot, and over 125ft. in the Discus, and he should be an asset to the growing strength of our field event section on his return to civvy street. items.sum: Editorial mourning the death of club president Frank Elson and announcing that the magazine will become a quarterly costing 2/- a year.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial mourning the death of club president Frank Elson and announcing that the magazine will become a quarterly costing 2/- a year. Dear Fellow Belgravians, Since our last issue of the Club Magazine, a major tragedy has befallen the Club in the loss of our President, Frank Elson. It is difficult to realise how great a loss the Club has sustained as Frank was something more than an ordinary Club member. As my Co-editor, I shall miss his very great assistance and I am sure the magazine will suffer to a degree without his help and co-operation. Any further tribute I will leave to the pen of Alf Harley who has known him considerably longer than I have but I know you will all join in a few moments of silent tribute to the memory of a great sportsman, a first class club man and a gentleman. The long illness of our late President has been partly responsible for the delay in coming to a decision over the future of the Magazine and you now have before you the first issue of the Belgravian in its new form. After much consideration and bearing in mind the suggestions put forward at the last Annual General Meeting, your committee have arrived at the following conclusions: 1.That there is a general desire for a Club Magazine. 2.That such a magazine should be published at least once a quarter. 3.That the cost of four issues a year would be too great to be met wholly out of club funds. It was therefore decided to publish a first issue for circulation to every member and thereafter to introduce a charge of 2/- a year for four issues, the second and subsequent issues being sent only to those who indicated their desire to be associated with the scheme by completing and returning the form which is enclosed. It must of course be made quite clear that the proposed charge of 2/- a year would only meet part of the cost of production and distribution the balance being borne by Club Funds. Your response will really show if you want a club magazine and it is hoped that every member will support this new venture and thus ensure its success. The yearly charge will also apply to members who are engaged on their compulsory period of National Service and are not called upon for ordinary subscriptions. If you wish to receive the next issue,please don't put the enclosed form away and forget about it. Complete it now and forward it with P.O. for 2/- to the Hon. Treasurer: S.C. Roberts, 4, Derwent Avenue, London,N.18. The future of the Belgravian depends on you. Your Editor will do the utmost to provide you with an interesting and topical magazine. Owing to the lapse of time since our last issue and the fact that space is restricted, it is not possible to give as full results of some of the races as we would wish, but I hope that with a regular quarterly issue in the future,I shall not have to resort to any cutting of copy sent to me Your Editor. Frank Elson Frank Elson late President; Co-editor of the magazine Alf Harley Alf Harley S.C. Roberts S.C. Roberts Hon. Treasurer London

items.sum: Obituary of club president Frank H. Elson, a walker who joined in 1927 and died aged 47, with an extract from his will and a note on his funeral.
items.s: FRANK H. ELSON Obituary of club president Frank H. Elson, a walker who joined in 1927 and died aged 47, with an extract from his will and a note on his funeral. We mourn the loss of our President who passed away on 26th April at the early age of 47 years and extend our heartfelt sympathies to Mrs. Elson and daughter June. We congratulate ourselves on having had Frank as an enthusiastic member for 27 years but we are profoundly sorry that he has not been spared to see the fruition of much that he worked for within the Club and to give us the continuing benefits of his wise guidance, his courageous and pleasing personality and enthusiastic zeal for anything to do with Belgrave. His great work for our Building Fund will ever be remembered. Frank joined the Club in October 1927, and quickly endeared himself to all members. In a very short time he started showing the most promising form in Walking events, and in his first "Open" road event finished 29th and was a member of our team which won the handicap. In his second open race he was again a member of the winning team and for several years was a first class performer both on road and track. On scores of occasions Frank figured in our winning and placed teams and special mention must be made of his second place in the R.W.A. National Junior Championship of 1930 at Enfield when he led our team to victory. He served the Club at various times as Captain, Walking Hon. Secretary, Hon. Handicapper and Joint Hon. Editor and his hard work for the Club had deservedly gained him Life Membership. He became our President last October, and many will recall his courageous and inspiring speech at our Dinner a few weeks later. For 27 years, Frank gave of his enthusiastic best for the Club - a sustained and ever zealous effort throughout - and his pleasing personality and devotion to Belgrave's interest over so many years can well be an inspiration to all. R. I. P. A.A.H. The following is an extract from Frank's will:- "My very deep appreciation of the many happy hours spent in the company of very fine fellows. The Club has always been one of the greatest things of my life and my feelings towards the Club and those who have been and still are true Belgravians are those of sincere pride and gratitude". ........ Well over twenty members and friends paid their last respect to our President and there were numerous messages of condolence and floral tributes from other Athletic Clubs and Associations. Frank H. Elson FRANK H. ELSON President; died 26th April aged 47; joined October 1927; walker, 2nd R.W.A. National Junior Championship 1930 at Enfield; Life Member Mrs. Elson Mrs. Elson A.A.H. A.A.H. R.W.A. items.s: INTRODUCING YOUR NEW TRACK CAPTAIN The new track captain introduces himself after Len Marchant's resignation and sets out his approach for the summer season. Due to the enforced resignation of Len Marchant owing to domestic difficulties (house hunting), I was persuaded by your Committee to accept the post of Track Captain. In taking on this position I realise what a tremendous job I have, but I am determined to try and make a success of it. I can if you will all give me your unstinted support throughout the Summer Season. We have a full programme as you will see by your Fixture List, and everybody has a chance of running or partaking in the various field events to enable them to enjoy their athletics. There will be no "Closed shop" as has been alleged in the past. Everybody has the same opportunity to run in the big events but they must show that they are worthy.. There is ample proof of the talent in the Club and I, for one, want to see the younger members making our first teams. Teams will be picked on current merit and not on past reputations and reserves must always remember to bring their kit with them, even although they may not get a run. Remember too that it will make my job much easier if all turn up at the correct time and not an hour after the majority. I can then say "My team is here, let's get to town Belgrave". We have had a lot of glamour on the country and on the road, now lets get some on the track. My sincere thanks to Bill Lucas and Tom Carter for their promised assistance when needed. One last word. I should be most happy if more of you, especially the half and the one milers who cannot go to Albert Shaw, would make more use of Franz Stampfl. He is most anxious to help you and his advice is given wholeheartedly,with great charming and understanding, but with the accent on hard work. Good luck, good racing and Up the "Bels". Frank Simmons. items.sum: Belgrave members' performances at the Leyton floodlight meeting, highlighted by a win in the mile medley relay.
items.s: LEYTON FLOODLIGHT MEETING Belgrave members' performances at the Leyton floodlight meeting, highlighted by a win in the mile medley relay. A cold blustery evening on May 5th saw a grand crowd of club members at this meeting, the first big attraction of the season. Those who were not competing, were cheering the club members on. Dennis Merrett ran in the 100 yards, but it was very evident that he had not recovered from an attack of the flu. Ted Gaworski gave a good account of himself in the Shot and was most unlucky not to gain a place. His put was 42" 8". Some of you could take a lesson from Ted in Clubmanship. J. Butterfield was also in the shot put and managed over 40', good performances on such an evening. John Bromley was lying third in the 3000 metres steeplechase when he gave his ankle a nasty bang on a hurdle and had to retire. He however ran again in the two mile team race so that we could field a full team, another example of good Belgrave spirit, although we did not fare too well in this event. R.Taylor ran an excellent half mile considering he was the victim of a lot of unnecessary rough tactics on the first bend. The highlight of the evening for us was the mile medley relay. Bob Wolton's 660 yards cannot be praised too much and the magnificent way in which the rest of the team rose to the occasion to give us a handsome win in the time of 3mins. 26.3secs was terrific. The team was R. Wolton, D. Merrett, R. Holtum, Ian Mayers and Jock Cameron. Jock Cameron paid our bus fares back to the railway station and everybody was extremely happy about the evening. Bystander. items.label: No. 119
items.h: LONDON TO BRIGHTON NATIONAL RELAY RACE
items.sum: Stage-by-stage account of the London to Brighton National Relay of 10 April 1954, run again from Westminster, in which Belgrave finished second to South London Harriers.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON NATIONAL RELAY RACE Stage-by-stage account of the London to Brighton National Relay of 10 April 1954, run again from Westminster, in which Belgrave finished second to South London Harriers. SATURDAY APRIL 10TH 1954 By Olympian. This Classic race promoted by the "News of the World" has come to be recognised as one of the major events in the Athletic Calendar and on this occasion history was again made when the course from Westminster to Brighton as instituted in 1924 when the race was originally staged was once more experimentally adopted for the first time since 19[illegible]. In the intervening years the start has been from Mitcham but it is hoped that by the restriction of supporters coaches that the full distance of 54¾ miles can be reinstated as the recognised route for future races. The race started at 10am. precisely by the first stroke of Big Ben and after the twenty runners had sorted themselves out from the conglomeration of press cameramen, who had formed an almost impassable barrier in the first twenty yards, the battle was on in earnest. A fast start along the embankment to Chelsea Bridge soon strung out the field which was led by Wood of Sheffield United Harriers who had recently performed creditably in the International Cross Country closely followed by Parmenter of Birchfield and Wood of Surrey A.C. Our own Bill Lucas was not far away in 10th position The three leading teams remained unchanged to Clapham Common where we were seventh, some fifty seconds behind the Sheffield Club with all but Birchfield of the favoured clubs behind us. John Bromley on the second leg to Mitcham maintained the position with a steady run but Blackheath and Essex Beagles had come more into the picture and Sheffield were over a minute ahead with Bolton also prominent. Jack Brown on his favourite stage from Mitcham to Purley produced another of his excellent performances on this leg and with a well judged effort took Belgrave into a very valuable lead of twenty one seconds from Surrey A.C. and Sheffield. The lead was held by Archie Bedford on the fourth stage to Merstham at which point we had 16 seconds over Essex Beagles and 28 over South London who had been slowly moving through the field. The remainder of the teams had begun to fall away - Birchfield had not maintained their earlier promise and Thames Valley, a well fancied team, had not made up for their poor start. Our Cross Country Captain Dennis Brickwood, who in 1937 had started Mitcham A.C. on a winning sequence in this event by an inches decision over our own Arthur Allum, was performing for the first time in this race in Belgrave colours and although chased by two very promising runners in the shape of Douglas of Essex Beagles and Lyne of S.L.H. retained our lead by a small margin over the latter club. Another veteran, Len Herbert, who is now 40 years of age took over at Earlswood with the Beagles and South London Harriers breathing down his neck, but with a nicely judged effort and one of his well renowned sprint finishes opened up a few seconds gap from those clubs. Now began one of the crucial stages of the race the newly arranged leg of well over six miles which constituted the combined Nos. 5 and 6 stages of the old course. Charlie Smart who at the age of 44 is running better than ever set off with the Belgrave baton with Gordon Pirie of S.L.H. some 15 seconds behind. As one would expect it was not long before Gordon caught Charlie ,but it was not without a fight that he eventually got away. In fact Charles actually repassed Pirie twice before having to relinquish his lead and by finishing only a minute behind at Handcross,can be said to have put up an excellent performance. The Beagles were still in third place but had lost a little ground. The next stage was another vital long leg over which many battles have been fought in the past. S.L.H. had given it to Peter Driver another of their young but very talented members and he set up for them what proved to be an unassailable lead with a time of 28.52 which beat by 17 seconds the October effort of Pirie and Olney which it will be remembered was considered to be an almost fantastic effort. However even Driver's time was not unbeatable, for first Jim Peters lowered it by 10 seconds and in doing so passed Charlie Walker and took Essex Beagles into 2nd place, and later by Alec Olney who reduced it by another 7 seconds without bringing his club T.V.H. anywhere near the front. The race by this time had definitely resolved itself into a battle between the leading three clubs with S. L. H. almost certain winners. Bob Taylor set about reducing the lead and with the fastest time of the day on his leg gained 43secs. on the Beagles but made only a small impression on S.L.H. who were still some 2½ minutes ahead. Stan Gawler carried on the good work and also returned the fastest time of the day on his stage and in so doing he brought us back to second place. S.L.H. were still keeping up the pace and with only the last leg to be run had over two minutes to spare. Dave Baulch a newcomer to Belgrave and on his first Brighton run put up a creditable performance which kept us in second place and also gave him the second fastest time for the stage.This member has definitely come to stay and should be an asset to our teams for some time to come Although we had to be content with only second place on this occasion the team performance was extremely good and it will take an exceptionally fast team to defeat S.L.H. in this type of race over the next few years. Providing Belgrave can produce two runners to undertake the vital 7th and 8th stages which now more than ever are the crucial points of the race, I feel that we can match South London's strength. In Jack Brown we have one of those runners but at present it is difficult to see who else can bear this mantle to combat S.L.H.'s Pirie and Driver. It is time our younger runners trained hard enough to keep our ageing athletes out of the team - this is not a race for the over 35's, yet in this year's team we had five in that group and without doubt were the oldest team on the road. We cannot much longer depend on these runners who have carried the long distance, track and road running on their shoulders since the war ended. In passing it should be mentioned that the old record for the full course which had stood since 1932 was beaten by no less than 8 minutes by S.L.H. and six by Belgrave and the Mitcham/Brighton time made by Mitcham A.C. in 1938 by approximately two minutes by both clubs. items.sum: Report of the National cross-country championships at Arrowe Park, Birkenhead, where Belgrave youths were eighth, seniors ninth and juniors sixteenth, with team placings.
items.s: NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the National cross-country championships at Arrowe Park, Birkenhead, where Belgrave youths were eighth, seniors ninth and juniors sixteenth, with team placings. This year Arrowe Park, Birkenhead was the venue for the Championships which were held on March 13th. The course which everyone had expected to be easy, turned out to be quite sticky. The first event was the Youths' race over 3 Miles. There, our lads expected to do well, bearing in mind their surprise 2nd place in the "Southern". This was not to be however, for Ron Linstead and Jim Edgar never seemed to get going and, finishing together in 30th and 31st places, were a minute down on the winner. D. Pettican did not seem at home on the sticky ground and was 85th G. Flanagan, 99th failed to produce his Southern form but nevertheless ran well for an athlete of only three months experience. When the team positions had been worked out it was found that we had come eighth. The Senior Race over a course of just under 10 miles was the next on. Our team was weakened by Jack Brown's absence and it is interesting to note that G. Olding, our Second Claim member, who was beaten by Jack in the Club "7", finished 19th. Although we did not expect anything brilliant from our runners, they did not run too badly and certainly bettered their "Southern" performance In coming 31st, Chas Walker certainly pulled one out of the bag and so becomes holder of the "Harry Parker" Memorial Trophy, for the ensuing year. Not far behind Chas. was "[illegible]umbo" Masters in 41st place, a good performance especially in view of his recent foot injury. Dennis Brickwood running in his usual steady manner, was our next man to finish coming 73rd. Doug Briggs came in 20 places later. Our next two home were Stan Gawler 98th, and Eddie Short 128th.Both these runners were further back than expected, although in fairness to Eddie Short it must be stated that his training has been interrupted this winter. Lastly came the Juniors who once more had to perform on a course churned up by nearly a thousand others. Here we came only 16th, but Dave Baulch's 21st place was especially encouraging for it was only his sixth race since he joined us in November. Peter Courtney ran well and finishe 38th. We had to go back to 125th position for our next scorer, B. Trower, who was ten places in front of Frank Wright whose running seems to have been upset by an Army P.T.I. Course he is on at present. And finally a word about our supporters. There is no doubt the efforts of our runners were matched by the few Club supporters who turned up. Particular mention must be made of Charlie Poulter and his two lads who carried a vast quantity of tea from London to Arrowe Park, where he was soon relieved of it by three teams of thirsty and grateful runners. Arthur Whitehead and Mickey Pyer did what was expected of them as Team Managers and Recorders, but found a flaw in the Northern Officials organisation. Arthur is particularly suited however, to overcoming diplomatically other peoples' inefficiency. Finally Eric Bishop motor cycled all the way with his wife, and adquately made up for the very poor support our runners received from the Club generally. items.h: A FEW WORDS FROM THE HON. TREASURER
items.sum: The Hon. Treasurer thanks members who paid arrears and asks the rest to send their 2/- magazine and current-year subscriptions at once, with a note for members on National Service.
items.s: A FEW WORDS FROM THE HON. TREASURER The Hon. Treasurer thanks members who paid arrears and asks the rest to send their 2/- magazine and current-year subscriptions at once, with a note for members on National Service. I should like to thank all those who so promptly replied to the letters I sent out a few weeks ago regarding arrears of subscriptions, also those who paid without a reminder. Our rebuilding programme is now in progress, which means we shall be spending the whole of our funds, so I would once again, through the medium of the magazine, ask all those who have not done so, to send in their subscriptions for the current year AT ONCE. You have an excellent opportunity of killing two birds with one stone, by not only completing the enclosed form,that is assuming you want to get the next issue of the Belgravian, and returning it to me with the necessary 2/-, but also including in the same letter your subscription for the current year. If you are not sure whether you have paid, just glance at the back of your handbook and see if you have a receipt affixed for the current year. May I once again remind members who are engaged on the compulsory period of National Service that whilst we do not enforce payment of your subscriptions during that period, IT IS ESSENTIAL THAT YOU LET ME KNOW THAT YOU ARE SO ENGAGED. Will Service members also indicate on the form for the Belgravian, whether they would like it sent to their home or Service address. S.C.R. S.C.R. S.C.R.

items.sum: Jack Chappell's field events section notes on members' throwing and jumping form, the Sward and Brockman Trophy meetings and hopes for the Kinnaird.
items.s: WITH THE FIELD EVENTS MEN Jack Chappell's field events section notes on members' throwing and jumping form, the Sward and Brockman Trophy meetings and hopes for the Kinnaird. May I first say how pleased I am that we can once again write to all our members, particularly as far as I am concerned to those in the Field Events Section, through the medium of the Belgravian. This year, as we all know, the weather has not been too kind to us, but we have been able to train during the winter. I was surprised to see so many members turning up for training. It is quite encouraging to the Club and particularly to Frank Simmons and Percy Luxon. Up to the moment we have not had a very exciting time but one or two have started to come into form. Percy Potter's win in the Essex County Hammer Championshop with a throw of 146' 8" was a fine effort. He tells me he had a throw of 155' at Imber Court. Well done, Percy. J. Powell-Jones is giving a good account of himself. In addition to winning the Surrey County Junior Weight with 48' 10" - a County record - he is also putting the senior weight for London University at about 42'. Ted Gaworski is also coming back to form. At the Sward Trophy Meeting on 29th June he threw the discus 142', which I think is the best club performance. He is also putting the weight about 43' and the hammer 140'. A new member,Ron Liggins is also proving very useful with the javelin, his best distance to date being 178' 10" in the Middlesex County Championship which gave him 2nd place.. Percy Luxon and Ken Key are showing improvement in both the Long Jump and Triple Jump. Dennis Fleming had an operation on his arm during the winter but should soon be back in form. Young Day is jumping well and we are pleased to see him when on leave. Other new members are beginning to take their place in teams. We did not do too good at the Brockman Trophy Meeting, but in the Sward Meeting we were better than last year. We had a competitor in each event except the pole vault which certainly shows the growth of the section. Eddie Short was 3rd in the 3000 metres steeplechase. I am now looking forward to the Kinnaird and hope we shall again make a good show. Alan Law is at Oxford but recovering from a strained back. I wish him well as we can do with him. Finally, the most important thing is to keep hard at training and make full use of the coaches who are ready to help. Wishing you all many successes. Jack Chappell. items.s: THE COUNTY TRACK CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of Belgrave successes at the Surrey, Kent, Middlesex and Essex county track championships, including J. Powell-Jones's Surrey shot record. Our members met with many successes in the various County Championships which were held on Saturday, 22nd May, and in all gained 7 firsts, 7 seconds and 7 thirds, in addition to which a recently joined second claim member, J. Butterfield, won no fewer than three Kent titles, viz; shot, discus and hammer throw,the last with a new County record of 135' 2". At Motspur Park the most outstanding performance was undoubtedly that of our Junior, J. Powell-Jones who set up a new Surrey County record in the shot put with a put of 48' 10". Despite a recent injury, Alan Sexton won the 440yds in 49.4secs. with A. Picton 3rd. The sprinters did well with Basil Walden defeating the holder C. Gibbs, to win the 100 yards, with D Merrett 3rd and J. Benstead 5th. In the 220 yards Merrett was 2nd to Gibbs and Benstead again 5th. C. Walker was third in a fast race over three miles and T. Gaworski 2nd in the shot put with 41ft.2ins and third in the hammer with 137ft. 6ins. R. Phillips won the two miles walk in 14mins. 57.8 secs with Eric Hall 3rd and Syd James 5th The best junior performance was that of J.Powell-Jones who won the shot put with a new County record of 48ft.10ins. H. Powell wo was third in the javelin and B. Windley who cleared 20ft to finish 3rd in the long jump, both achieved Southern Standard. In the Middlesex Championships Bob Taylor was second in the 880 yards for the third year in succession. He equalled Arthur Wint's County record in his heat, but a slow first lap in the final prevented a fast time, and he was beaten by R. Day in 1 min. 57 secs. A. Cameron won the 440 yards and R. Wolton was third. In the 100 yards I Mayers was 2nd and R. Holtum 4th. P. Luxon missed 1st place in the long jump by three inches and was fifth in the hop step and jump with K. Key 4th. In the Kent Championships Jack Brown won the mile in 4 mins. 19.6secs and R. Liggins was 2nd in the javelin with 178ft. items.s: NEWS FROM ABROAD News of C.R. Jones's jumping and sprinting results in station, R.A.F. and Inter-Services sports while serving in Egypt. C.R. Jones, serving in H.M. Forces in Egypt send news of his activities in "Sphinxland". In the Station Sports he competed in the Long Jump, Triple Jump, 100 yards and 220 yards with the following results:- L.J. 19' 6", H.S.& J. 41'6"" (1st) 100 yards 10.3sec. (2nd) and 220 yards, 23.5secs. (2nd). In the R.A.F. Championships, he improved on this by gaining 1st in the two jumps, both with record distances, viz; Long Jump 20' 5", Triple Jump, 42' 7", and was second in the 100 yards in 10.2secs. Later in the Inter-Services Championships, he was 4th in the Long Jump with 19' 10", 1st in the Triple Jump with 41' 7", 2nd in the 100 yards in 10.4secs. and 2nd in the 220 yards in 23.2. He mentions that all the track events take place on a sand track and the run up for the jumps is bone hard bumpy mud. Contrary to what he understands is the opinion over here, the temperature and general conditions do not tend to make for faster times in fact he has it on the authority of a A.A.A. Coach that there is a difference of about .1 - .2 in the 100 yards and .3 in the 220 yards. Congratulations! Charles, we certainly hope your times were correctly recorded and we wish you more successes. C.R. Jones C.R. Jones serving in H.M. Forces in Egypt; won long and triple jump at R.A.F. items.sum: Dave Shepherd's social section notice on the Annual Dinner and Dance at Oxford Street Corner House on 25th September, coach seats for the Brighton Relay, and winter socials at the improved Belgrave Hall.
items.s: SOCIAL Dave Shepherd's social section notice on the Annual Dinner and Dance at Oxford Street Corner House on 25th September, coach seats for the Brighton Relay, and winter socials at the improved Belgrave Hall. The most important date in the Club's Social Section is the ANNUAL DINNER AND DANCE which will be held this year on 25th September, a date which you should make a note of straight away. As the attendance last year was not as great as was expected, it has been decided to hold this year's function at Oxford Street Corner House, (corner of Tottenham Court Road, where there is accommodation for not more than 200 so you are advised to book early to avoid disappointment. As the number is limited, all applications for tickets MUST be accompanied by the cash,(17/6d each)and although the tickets are not yet available, you can send your applications in as early as you please. Those who have attended during the past few years need no recommendation as it is really a first class night. So once again, don't leave it too late. Another important function, and one in which you will get full value for your money, is the Brighton Relay in October. Here again, if you would only realise the immense pleasure and excitement which can be gained from this day out, I am sure I should be inundated with applications for seats on the coaches. With the completion of the improvements at Belgrave Hall, the socials during the coming winter season, should be a great improvement on previous years. We need to recapture some of the pre-war enthusiasm for these very enjoyable socials and I hope that the improved amenities at our hall will have this effect. Look out for the dates in our next issue and come along and give your support. Dave Shepherd. items.sum: Jack Goswell's walking section notes on winter progress, the win in the National 20, all-day strolls, coaching at Battersea Track and hopes for the National 50 Kilos after the Northern 50 Kilos win.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Jack Goswell's walking section notes on winter progress, the win in the National 20, all-day strolls, coaching at Battersea Track and hopes for the National 50 Kilos after the Northern 50 Kilos win. This being the first issue of the Belgravian for some months, the activities of the Walking Section have had to be tightly compressed, so if I have inadvertently overlooked any of the unusually good performances, my humble apologies. We can be pleased with our progress,during the winter we made continued improvement in the "Open" sevens and some of our younger members began to show their paces. I hope it will continue during the track season. Our distance walkers are going from strength to strength. To gauge the spirit, one only needs to go on one of our trips away from home, a better days outing you could not wish for.The biggest triumph of all was, of course, our win in the National 20, a big surprise for many and a credit to the Club. Our all day strolls are thoroughly enjoyed by all who take part, even if "Big head" will argue with the Captain (alias Fog horn), over the birth and names of trees. Those who want to improve their knowledge of Natural History or English History would always be most welcome and would soon learn something about "Silent pools" "Good Queen Bess", "Old manors", etc. Last Whitsun we learnt that they feed the north on rhubarb - acres and acres of it, in fact the country outside Leeds is covered with it. There is a very good attendance at Battersea Track on Tuesday evenings and I am sure the lads will benefit from the advice and assistance of our coaches Len Fletcher and Don Brown.Unfortunately Len is now working quite a bit outside London and is not able to spend so much time at the track as last year and whilst we miss you Len,we are fortunate to have one of your pupils in Don Brown. We must endeavour to enrol more youngsters to keep our strength going and I should like to see a good field battling for the "Olympic" Cup next year. By the time this is being read, the Inter-Club meeting at Battersea will be over and I am sure we can look for a good result. The National 50 Kilos will also have been held at Sheffield and I hope will result in another National Win.The lads are all fighting fit, particularly after their win at Bradford in the Northern 50 Kilos on Whit Monday and I am sure we all wish them luck, and continued progress in the coming months. May the name of Belgrave be seen many times in our National papers. Yours sincerely Jack Goswell. items.label: No. 119
items.h: RACE WALKING NEWS SINCE THE LAST ISSUE
items.sum: Race walking news from August and September: Norman Guilmant's win in the Hastings to Brighton race and second in the London to Brighton Walk, his collapse at Milan, and the St. Dunstan's Hour Walks.
items.s: RACE WALKING NEWS SINCE THE LAST ISSUE Race walking news from August and September: Norman Guilmant's win in the Hastings to Brighton race and second in the London to Brighton Walk, his collapse at Milan, and the St. Dunstan's Hour Walks. Before starting on the winter season's results, some mention should be made of the efforts of our distance walkers during August and September last. In the Hastings to Brighton race on 15th August last Norman Guilmant put up a grand performance by winning the race in a new record time and to crown it, won the handicap also. The team were second in the team race, our best performance for many years. In the following month, Norman again excelled himself by gaining second place in the London to Brighton Walk and of course won the Club Long Distance Championship. Hugh McGreechan and Harry Shields walked their best distances to date, both being inside 8. 40. but unfortunately Fred Rolfe had shoe trouble and was obliged to fall out at Dale Hill. However Jack Wakeley who had only intended making it a stroll, being his first long walk following his operation, made a great effort to push through and finish as our fourth man to make us second in the team race, only five points behind the winners. Our other walkers, Bernard Eglington, Joe Wilson, Percy Wilson, all gave a good account of themselves. The usual enthusiastic support was in evidence and much appreciated by the walkers. Following Norman's fine performance in the Brighton Walk we were very pleased to hear that he had been selected to go to Milan for an International 100 kilometres race. After lying 6th at 80 kilometres, he suddenly collapsed and of course was out of the race. He was subsequently taken to hospital, and our old friend of Surrey Walking Club, Timber Woodcock, who was acting as manager, in order to stay with Norman, was obliged to become a casualty also, and be put to bed with "flu". Fortunately Norman has suffered no serious after effects and is now almost back to last year's form. Hard luck Norman and better luck next time. In the St. Dunstan's Hour Walks at Parliament Hill Fields, 23 of our lads competed, six of whom qualified for "Six mile" badges and no doubt they are all now striving for the "Seven". This was virtually the end of the summer season and we now go over to Wimbledon. items.s: BELGRAVE OPEN 7 - November 28th Report of the Belgrave Open 7 walk with a record 332 entries, Belgrave 3rd in the scratch team race and B and A teams 2nd and 3rd in the handicap. Our own Open created a record programme entry of no less than 332. 220 started and for the first time over 200 finished, 203 to be exact. It was a busy day and a hard one for the recorders and it is certain that the whole day reflected credit on the Club. The scratch team race developed into a neck and neck struggle, and it was very difficult to forecast who was going to come out winners until the very end, eventually 3 points separated the first 3 teams with us taking 3rd place.. Bob McMullen once again led the lads home in 5th position with George Checkley 8th, Hugh McGreechan 15th and E. Hall 16th. All the handicap team prizes stopped over our side of the water as Surrey W.C. took 1st place, our "B" team (Demmon, Middleton Wilson,Doubleday) were 2nd and the "A" Team (Hall,Checkley,Eglington McMullen) were 3rd. The result showed a decided improvement in all our walkers and hopes of greater successes in the future. In addition Len Demmon was third in the individual handicap. Bob McMullen Bob McMullen 5th George Checkley George Checkley 8th Hugh McGreechan Hugh McGreechan 15th E. Hall E. items.s: SOUTHERN GARNET CUP CHAMPIONSHIP - February 6th Report of the Southern Garnet Cup walking championship at Eltham, where Belgrave finished third after Bob Phillips was disqualified, behind winners Surrey Walking Club. This was held at Eltham on February 6th and we were unfortunately short of two of our qualified members, so that when Bob Phillips came under the judges' ban after the first mile our hopes of a place looked very slender. However this setback rather than deter the rest of the team, seemed to make them more enthusiastic, and so well did they walk, that we finished third in the Championship. Considering we had an entirely different team from last year when we won, this was an excellent performance and says much for the younger members. With all these walkers eligible for next year we have very high hopes of regaining the championship. Congratulations to Surrey Walking Club on their win. The team was led home by Eric Hall 12th, 84mins.4sec. 13th R. Newson 84.37, 24th J. Scamell 87.0[illegible], and 36th R. Garwood, 89.29. Surrey Walking Club scored 58 points to our 76. items.sum: Report of the club 20 miles walking championship for the Ricketts Shield on a new course, won by Hugh McGreechan for the third time, with the junior 5 miles Olympic Cup a walk-over for Ray Middleton.
items.s: CLUB 20 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP - April 17th Report of the club 20 miles walking championship for the Ricketts Shield on a new course, won by Hugh McGreechan for the third time, with the junior 5 miles Olympic Cup a walk-over for Ray Middleton. A new course was used for the race for the Ricketts Shield this year at the suggestion of the walkers themselves. Owing to traffic conditions at various crossings, and the opening of new blocks of flats adjacent to the course it was felt that the existing course was too dangerous for the walkers and the Committee therefore agreed to use the same course as that used for the 20 miles road run. This consists of three equal laps, turning left with traffic the whole way and with no crossings. After the race the general opinion of all the walkers was that the course was an improvement on the old one. Hugh McGreechan and George Beecham led the field for the first two laps at a very fast pace and one began to wonder who would be the first to crack. Eventually George began to drop back and soon lost a number of places. Hugh continued to hold the lead, but by this time George Checkley was storming ahead and making up a lot of ground but not quite sufficient to catch McGreechan who thus won for the third time running in the time of 2hrs. 57mins. 19secs. George Checkley was a good second in 2hrs. 58mins. 23secs., Bernard Eglington coming next nearly 7 minutes behind in 3hrs. 5mins. 14sec. Norman Guilmant, 4th, Bob Newson, 5th, George Beecham 6th and Fred Rolfe 7th all completed the course inside 3hrs. 15mins. Outstanding performance was that of Bob Newson on his first 20. He is certainly going to be one of our leading distance men in the near future. The handicap was deservedly won by George Checkley with Bob Newson 2nd, and Bernard Eglington 3rd. Our thanks are due to all the helpers, the ladies who manned a sponge and drink station at the bottom of the hill, to Ron Garwood, Arthur Skinner and their ladies at the top of Kingston Hill, the helpers at the top of Lauriston Road and all those who assisted with cars and enabled the judges to get round the course. As last year, we arranged to hold our Junior 5 miles race on the same day, for the "Olympic" Cup. Unfortunately Johnny Haynes was unable to get away from duty to defend his title and only Ray Middleton turned up and had a walk over for this very fine cup. This shows the necessity for enrolling some more junior members and thus ensure that next year we shall have a proper race. Hugh McGreechan Hugh McGreechan won Ricketts Shield for third time running, 2hrs. 57mins. 19secs. items.s: NATIONAL 20 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP - May 8th. Report of Belgrave's team win in the National 20 miles walking championship at Birmingham, with tables of the team's positions and team scores, near-miss for the Nimegen Shield and thanks to helpers. The Championship was held at Birmingham this year and what a grand day it turned out to be for the Club. Once again we are holders of a National title and it was grand to see in a weekly paper "Belgrave National Champions". It was quite a good field which faced the starter on a fair two lap course although there was fairly heavy traffic in many places. From the start the lads were content to settle down and the following table shows the positions of the team throughout the race. As one can see, not only did the lads consolidate their positions, but gradually improved on them, although Geogge Checkley did drop one place in the last stages. Sheffield made a dashing start and were only 29 points at 3 miles, whilst we were then 78 and thereafter at every check we were improving our position. The last few miles was a drive to strengthen our position and this we certainly did. The only real disappointment was that we did not win the Nimegen Shield, although we had seven men.in before Woodford's 5th man, but unfortunately Fred Rolfe developed a bad spell as will be seen from the table above between 9 and 14 miles otherwise we should certainly have scored the double, in fact we only missed it by one place, the shield going to the first team to close in their full team of 8. Our heartiest congratulations to all, particularly to George Checkley who celebrated his birthday by gaining his Honours badge. Bernard Eglington, 13th, missed his by one position. George Beecham gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan the Sydney Bayliss Cup and Bob Newson his first (2nd Class) National Standard medal. In fact the four members of the winning team were all inside first class standard and three out of the remaining founr were inside 2nd class. To Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday, Len Demmon and Billie True and the ladies who came along to give their help and support ,we say thank you very much. Needless to say the hard working Hon. Sec. Jack Goswell, covered quite 50 miles on his iron horse dashing from one end of the field to the other to attend to the wants of the men. items.s: ON THE TRACK Walking notes on the club two miles track handicaps, Johnny Haynes's resignation, members' news, the Police Barking to Southend Walk and the team's prizes in the Northern 50 Kilometres Walk at Bradford. Our two miles track handicaps held to date have been well supported. The first was won by "Pothunter" Harry Shields, with Eric Hall 2nd and Doub 3rd. The second was won by Maurice Nye who we had not seen since the early winter, but who must have been doing plenty of secret training. We look forward to seeing him more with the lads in the future. Doub improved on his first effort by coming 2nd and Percy Wilson was third, slowly getting back to fitness after a spell of ill health. We were also pleased to see Charlie Speechley having a go again after a period in hospital. One minute covered fourteen competitors in this race - good marks to the handicapper. News has just been received that Johnny Haynes has made up his mind to resign from the club as he is now permanently posted a long way away and is hoping to join another club nearer at hand. We can ill afford to lose our younger members but thank him for his help in the past and wish him well in the future. We understand the "Baron" has bought a nice big car. We have missed him out racing this past winter, but when he is qualified to drive we feel sure he will be out regularly particularly on the distance walks when he can be of great help. Gerry Warr has gone back to rejoin our Southampton-cum-Eastleigh contingent having taken up residence at Southampton, so we hope he will be seeing something of Percy Wright. For many years Belgrave Walkers have been trying to win the Police Barking to Southend Walk for four years in succession, and this year we hoped Hugh McGreechan would be the first to do it. Fred Rickards, Fred Bentley and Hugh have all won on three successive occasions and Hugh looked all set for it this year. However that very improved young walker, McFarlane of the Poly, who incidentally seems to spend more time with us than his own club, beat Mc.to it and so the battle for this honour still goes on. A piece of news concerning our long distance walkers has just come to hand and whilst we hope to give a fuller report of the race in the next issue, we feel that brief details should be included here. Four walkers and the usual hard working Jack Goswell went up to Bradford for the Northern 50 Kilometres Walk on Whit Monday and came away well loaded up with prizes. Hugh McGreechan was 3rd in the race, Norman Guilmant 5th, Bernard Eglington 9th and Harry Shields 10th, all inside 5 hours. In addition Harry took the second handicap prize and Norman the 3rd. It looks well for the R.W.A.50 Kilometres. items.label: No. 120
items.sum: Editorial on subscriptions to the magazine, the election of Tom Morrell as President, the completion of the Belgrave Hall rebuilding and the walkers' London to Brighton success.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial on subscriptions to the magazine, the election of Tom Morrell as President, the completion of the Belgrave Hall rebuilding and the walkers' London to Brighton success. Fellow Members, The response to the invitation to members to subscribe towards the cost of the Belgravian was not as great as I expected, but forms are still coming in and I feel sure that as time goes on, the majority of our members will become subscribers. This issue marks the beginning of a new Belgrave Year and judging by the enthusiasm displayed by members at the Annual General Meeting, there is every prospect of it proving a very successful one. The unanimous election of Tom Morrell as our new President will add in no small measure to our efforts to maintain our reputation as one of the leading clubs in the country. There is no doubt that Tom is fully deserving of the honour conferred on him and we offer our hearty congratulations to him on attaining his present office. For many years his work as Assistant Hon. Treasurer, in particular in dealing with the supplies of Club vests, etc., has brought him into close contact with almost every member, and his willingness to carry on with this work during his year of Presidency, is a typical example of his enthusiastic and generous disposition. Another landmark in the history of the Club has been reached in the completion of our rebuilding programme at Belgrave Hall. Much work has been put into this project by members over a long period of years to make Belgrave Hall one of the finest Club Headquarters in the country and it is up to every member to see that every possible care is taken of the new amenities which have been provided. Our long distance walkers rounded off a successful summer season by very decisively winning both the individual and team titles in the classic race of the year, the London to Brighton Walk, the team event being won in a new record low score of 16 points. Fuller details will be found elsewhere. As this event actually took place in the Club's new year, let us look on it as a good omen for the events which are to come. Your Editor. Tom Morrell Tom Morrell elected President; Assistant Hon. Treasurer London to Brighton Walk Belgrave Hall

items.label: No. 120
items.sum: Report of the Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall: tributes, the Hon. Secretary's and Treasurer's reports, election of Tom Morrell as President, presentations and proposed subscription increases.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING Report of the Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall: tributes, the Hon. Secretary's and Treasurer's reports, election of Tom Morrell as President, presentations and proposed subscription increases. Our Annual General Meeting, held at Belgrave Hall on Monday 20th September, gave members an opportunity to see the progress which is being made with the building programme and the attendance of over 100 was remarkably good. Harry Evans, the interim President, took the chair and after a few well chosen words, the assembly stood for a few moments as a token of respect to our late President Frank Elson, and a Life Member H. Goodfellow who had passed away since our last meeting. In presenting the Annual Report the Hon. Secretary, Alf Harley apologised for the omission of a paragraph referring to our second placings in the Brighton "Southern" and "National" Relays and it was unanimously agreed that it should be inserted. The Report, which included a vote of thanks to Ernie Duffett who was not seeking re-election as Running Hon. Secretary, having held that office for many years, was then adopted. The Hon. Treasurer then gave the financial report, starting by thanking the Assistant Hon. Treasurer, Tom Morrell, Eric Bishop, and A. Pyer for the help they had given him and Also Les Cohen for the work he had put in for the Supporters Club. He then compared the income and expenditure with the previous year pointing out the large decrease of £140 on the cost of printing which was mainly due to the fact that only one issue of the Belgravian had been made, and that, with the new photo-type process. The cost of social events was also considerably reduced and with a little more support for the Annual Dinner this could have been reduced further still. On the income side, subscriptions were down a little but donations from Life Members, Past Presidents, etc. was up. He informed the meeting that there were still a number of members in arrears and hoped they would promptly pay their dues. Handicap fees remained fairly steady but there was plenty of room for improvement by better support to club promotions. A 25% increase in entries would produce a much larger revenue from this source and would make for keener competition. The Inter-City Meeting at the White City last year resulted in our funds benefiting to the extent of £55 and provided a very good reason for our members giving it their support. The final item of income, which for many years has been the biggest, was the donation from the Supporters Club, and was actually less then the total subscriptions. With the exception of the first payment of £660 towards the rebuilding, there was nothing outstanding about the Building Fund Account, but the Hon. Treasurer pointed out that as the whole of our investments would be utilised on this project, we should be losing a valuable source of income of £140 or more per annum in interest. Before the report was adopted, Eric Bishop, one of our Hon. Auditors, expressed his satisfaction with the accounts. The meeting then proceeded to elect the officers for the year. Harry Evans proposed Tom Morrell as President. Alf Harley seconded and gave a short review of Tom's services to the Club over 27 years and his election was carried unanimously. It was then proposed, seconded and carried that the names of A. Readman and G.P. Powell be added to the list of Vice-Presidents. The principle officers, Hon. Secretary and Assistant, Hon. Treasurer and Assistant were re-elected and the election of Section Secretaries, Captains, Vice Captains, etc. began. It was agreed to split the office of Running Hon. Secretary Denis Brickwood being elected for Cross Country and Ron. Holtum for the track. A full list of the officers will be included in the new handbook which will probably have reached you by now. A number of presentations were then made. Harry Evans presented the new Jimmy Bellchamber Trophy (50 kilometres Walk) to the first holder Hugh McGreechan. Ted Gaworski presented a cup to Peter Porter for the best throwing performance of the year (156ft6in) with the hammer. The President presented a cup, from the Club, to Percy Luxon for the best jumping performance of the year (45ft 5ins. triple jump and 23ft. 2ins. long jump). The proposed new rules governing the Trustees and powers to borrow were moved by Alf Harley, seconded by Syd Roberts and carried. The Hon. Treasurer then proposed that subscriptions be increased to £1 for seniors, 10/- for juniors, 5/- for boys and 10/- for Hon. members. He outlined the future liabilities of the club which would include repaying money borrowed from the bank to complete our building programme and increased cost of maintaining the hall. The motion was seconded by the Hon. Secretary who gave a brief description of the new amenities at the hall. A number of members stated that they felt the new rates would still be giving good value and the amendment to the rules was carried unanimously. It was made apparent from the points raised both in the Hon. Treasurer's report and the facts put forward in proposing the amendment to rules that we must keep the money flowing in. This can be done by being up to date with subscriptions, supporting the subscription list for the "Belgravian", supporting club events, taking tickets in the Supporters Club and making voluntary donations similar to the old "halfpenny in a box" scheme or sixpence a week until our funds are built up again. Under any other business, a vote of thanks was given to Frank Webb for his work in connection with the disposal of tickets for the White City. Might I end by asking all members to study their handbooks well. Make yourselves acquainted with the Section Officers, keep in touch with them and above all GIVE THEM YOUR SUPPORT. G.S.D. items.sum: The Hon. Treasurer asks members to pay their subscriptions at the new rate early and invites donations towards the Building Fund debt.
items.s: HON. TREASURER'S NOTE The Hon. Treasurer asks members to pay their subscriptions at the new rate early and invites donations towards the Building Fund debt. Those of you who attended the Annual General Meeting will need no further enlightenment of the fact that the annual subscriptions have been advanced. Quite a number of conscientious members have already paid their subscriptions for the current year, but at the old rate, and I hope they will at the first opportunity, forward to me the balance. To the remainder I would say as I did at the A.G.M. - please pay your subscriptions EARLY. I shall endeavour to be at Wimbledon as often as possible, but it can be handed to Tom Morrell and of course there are such things as postal orders and 2½d stamps. Donations, large and small, will be welcomed from our Past Presidents and Life Members as the more money we can accumulate, the sooner we shall be able to pay off our debt on the Building Fund. Tom Morrell Tom Morrell Wimbledon

items.s: THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and results of the club track championships at Battersea Park on Saturday 7 August. The Club Championships, the highlight of the track season were held as usual at Battersea Park on Saturday, August 7th. The meeting opened up with fairly good weather and everyone was keeping their fingers crossed that it would continue throughout the afternoon. Unfortunately the rain arrived just before the childrens' races and somewhat affected the entries, but generally speaking the meeting went off very successfully. Entries were not quite so good as last year, notable non-appearances being from Alan Sextion, Bob Taylor who we regret to say is in hospital and J. Brown. It is also interesting to note that only 12 standards were gained as against 37 last year and one wonders whether the raising the standards since last year had any effect on the number of entries. items.sum: Report of Belgrave's first win in the AAA relay championships, the 4 x 110 yards in 42.6 sec at Birmingham, and John Powell-Jones's junior shot record.
items.s: A.A.A. RELAYS Report of Belgrave's first win in the AAA relay championships, the 4 x 110 yards in 42.6 sec at Birmingham, and John Powell-Jones's junior shot record. On 31st July we took two teams to Birmingham for the AAA. Relay Championships which were being held in conjunction with the Junior Championships. Our main hope was in the 4 x 110 yards relay, whilst we thought we had an outside chance in the 4 x 440 yards. I was quietly confident that we would pull off the short distance relay and my confidence was increased when our team won their heat in 42.9s The 4 x 440 team gave of their best and although they were knocked out in their heat, with a little more luck they would have been in the final. Meanwhile J. Powell Jones was performing in the Junior Shot put and was leading when the final of the short relay was announced. We had drawn lane No. 4 and our lads were prepared to do or die. At the start Dennis Merrett went away well, held his own and indeed gained a trifle to hand over to Ron Holtum who, although he had a bad cold, ran well to catch Ferguson of Notts. A.C. and the T.V.H. runner. Ron handed over to Basil Walden who put in a terrific challenge to hand over to Ivan Mayers about 1½ yards up. T.V.H. had Downs on the last leg and I thought he might rob us of our first win in this event but with 50 yards to go I saw Ivan's face break into a grin and I knew that it was ours. Ivan came away to win by four clear yards and we had registered our first win in the A.A.A. Team Championships in the creditable time of 42.6secs., the second fastest time by a British Team. After I had recovered my equilibrium, I whispered a quiet word in John Powell-Jones ear and he hurled the shot 53feet 1 inch to end a good day's work and establish a new Junior record. Needless to say we celebrated our win in the proper manner on our return to London. Heartiest congratulations must go to D. Merrett, R. Holtum, B. Walden, and I. Mayers. They worked very hard for a well deserved victory, also to Powell Jones who no doubt, took inspiration from their victory. J. Powell Jones J.
