items.sum: New Year editorial from the new editors welcoming President Tom Carter, noting the London County cross-country title and appealing for contributions.
items.s: Editorial New Year editorial from the new editors welcoming President Tom Carter, noting the London County cross-country title and appealing for contributions. Dear Fellow Members, A VERY HAPPY AND SUCCESSFUL NEW YEAR We are honoured to become your editors at the same time as the election of your new President Tom Carter, to whom we are indebted for his typically modest article. What greater pleasure could be given to this wonderful veteran of so many individual and team successes in Belgrave colours, than for us to regain our supremacy over the cross-country clubs of Britain? We are already London County Cross-Country Champions and we are pleased to see the great form of Jack Brown, Charlie Walker and Charlie Dabbs. Let us see how many more titles we can annexe during 1957. Owing to our inability to edit non-existent material, we were almost driven to publishing our personal memoirs. Whilst this would doubtless prove most indigestible reading, it does seriously show how much we depend on articles contributed by section leaders and in fact by any members. We welcome material from any source, sent to us within reasonable time of the event to which it refers. With your co-operation we hope to be able to maintain the high standard of editorship set by our predecessors. Your Editors. Tom Carter Tom Carter new President Jack Brown Jack Brown in great form Charlie Walker Charlie Walker in great form Charlie Dabbs Charlie Dabbs in great form London County Cross-Country Championships

items.label: No. 129
items.sum: The new President thanks members for electing him, urges teams to turn out in club vests, and congratulates the club's two Olympic representatives.
items.s: From Your President The new President thanks members for electing him, urges teams to turn out in club vests, and congratulates the club's two Olympic representatives. Dear Belgravians, Thank you all for the great honour which you have bestowed upon me in making me your President for this year. To me, this wonderful Club of ours has no equal, for what other club can point to so many successes in all branches of athletics. There is no need for me to remind any of you as to these achievements, all you have to do is to read about them in your winter handbook or ask any oldtimer (I know!) of Belgrave who would willingly devote a few weeks to telling you. I should like to draw members attention to our motto, "Semper Paratus" which means "Always Ready". To me this means always ready for anything for our Club; I hope that this means the same to you also. Something that I should like to see done, is that of the turning out of teams in club vests. When representing the Club, be proud of it, let rival club performers fear the sight of claret and gold vests and Persil-white shorts. I cannot close these few remarks without mentioning our two Olympic representatives; congratulations Eric and Vic. When you read these few words of them, you will know how well they have performed and have given of their best. Here's to a successful year and once again thank you for making me a very happy and proud Belgravian. C.T. CARTER. President. C.T. Carter C.T. CARTER President Olympic Games

items.label: No. 129
items.sum: The Track Captain reflects on a disappointing level of support in the 1956 track season and appeals for greater effort in 1957.
items.s: On the Track The Track Captain reflects on a disappointing level of support in the 1956 track season and appeals for greater effort in 1957. Once again I am accepting, with mental reservations, the unenviable job of Track Captain. I say reservations, because I am not really satisfied that the 1956 track season, though successful, has not been accompanied by the support which I expect of Belgravians; in fact I wondered at times whether it was worth the trouble trying to instil some enthusiasm into you. Perhaps my forthright approach to you was not the correct one, but like the leopard, I don't suppose I will change my spots. My one thought is to try to assist you on the track, to get you to enjoy ATHLETICS, to coerce you to run, throw or jump for the club. This of course, should be unnecessary, for it is always an honour to represent a club such as ours. We need more endeavour and fewer excuses, then we shall show all that Belgrave is the best club in the country. The talent is within our ranks, it only needs self-confidence and club spirit to bring out the best in all of you. Remember, you are the club, you Seniors, Juniors & Youths. Your officials do their best on your behalf, give them full support and their task will be lightened, for without that it is sheer hard work. I look forward to a more successful season in 1957, but we can only achieve this if all give their unstinted support, both in home and away fixtures and in major trophy competitions. Frank Simmons Frank Simmons Frank Simmons Track Captain

items.s: Match v. Q.P.H. Aug. 20th. Report of a track match against Q.P.H. lost through lack of support, with a call to re-learn team running. Lack of support lost us this match. It is beyond my comprehension why so many seem to avoid partaking in matches such as this, for here surely the better class athlete can help his clubmates with less ability, and at the same time have an enjoyable run without the need to ''bash it" to win. We must re-learn that lost art once typical of Belgrave, especially in the longer track events, namely "TEAM RUNNING". There were too many watchers and too few competitors, and if the entry for the 880yds. handicap was any criterion then the support does not warrant the inclusion of events such as these. Q.P.H.

Mal Ash won the pole vault, high jump and 120yds. hurdles and was placed in the triple jump- what an asset this boy is! items.s: Field Events Note that Bill Merryman has stepped down as Field Events Captain after winning the Sward Trophy, succeeded by Charlie Jones. Just when he had lifted the Field Events Section to the highest position it has held since its formation, Bill Merryman was obliged to relinquish his post as Captain of the section. His was the honour of seeing us win, under his captaincy, the coveted SWARD TROPHY. We are indebted to Bill for the devotion he gave to his task and we know that Charlie Jones his successor will continue to uphold our name in this increasingly popular branch of athletics. items.label: No. 129
items.sum: Report of the first inter-club floodlit meeting at Tooting Bec for the Melbourne Trophy, where Belgrave finished third overall after a mile medley relay win anchored by John Davies.
items.s: Floodlit Meeting - 24th. October Report of the first inter-club floodlit meeting at Tooting Bec for the Melbourne Trophy, where Belgrave finished third overall after a mile medley relay win anchored by John Davies. On a cold damp evening at Tooting Bec, the first inter-club "Floodlit Meeting" was held for the "Melbourne Trophy".We had entered three teams, Senior, Junior and Youths. Inability to turn out Junior and Youths sprinters weakened us, but those who ran in the longer events gave of their best, indeed, once again they demonstrated to our Seniors the art of Team running. It was a source of satisfaction to their advisers, and to me, to see our lads running as a team, as Belgrave used to run, our juniors packing in their one mile race 4th, 5th and 8th and the youths in their's, 5th, 7th and 8th, gaining minor team placings. This shows signs of better running when these boys have had more experience, they were the youngest teams running and it should be noted that they all wore their "Belgrave Vest" proudly. We were weakened again in the senior events, Ron Holtum having the flu and Jack Brown unable to be present. Bob Taylor tried to contact Charlie Walker but failed. However, after much persuasion Bill Bird made our three in the 3000 metres team race, but not being at his best he finished well down. Ray Tooby ran well to be placed third (How about that Club Vest Ray?) and George Davidson was fifth. We were third in the team race. In the absence of Holtum I decided on a gamble and ran Clive Ryan in our senior 4 x 110yds. team. This team of C.R. Jones, D. Carter, Ian Forrester and Clive ran well to finish second to the Poly, who had Shenton on the last leg, Clive hanging on for dear life for second place and gaining some valuable experience against top class sprinters. Our 4 x 220yds. team again finished second to the Poly, being beaten by 8yds. The forward running of D. Carter in both sprints and the running of Roy Glenn who is always ready to have a bash should give us hopes for next season. The tit-bit for us, was the mile medley relay. Dudley Gordon ran his best quarter ever. Not knowing who was in front of him, he just "went" and surprised us all with his determined running, handing over second to Dennis Butler for the first furlong. Dennis gave us the lead but Pat Fox, inexperienced as he was, lost ground and handed over to John Davies 40yds. down. John set about his task in workmanlike style, running in his usual relaxed way, he reduced the lead on the first lap and in the back straight of the final lap came away to give us a win. John's time was 1min.55.8secs, truly wonderful running on such a cold night. Our field events lads performed well, M. Ash and D. Ansell gained first team points in the long jump and Ash and C.R. Jones second points in the high jump. We finished third in the competition as a whole, points being added from matches. It was surprising the number of our members who always seem to appear just too late to be asked to run, or have the flimsiest excuses as to why they cannot, yet are always willing to "hold" a watch on somebody else and then criticise them when they were not willing to have a go themselves. Frank Simmons. items.label: No. 129
items.sum: Appeal to members who have drifted away from competition to resume training, citing Charlie Smart as an example of success past 40.
items.s: Do Not Despair Appeal to members who have drifted away from competition to resume training, citing Charlie Smart as an example of success past 40. During the last few years a considerable number of promising members have disappeared from competition long before age should have caught up with them. What is the cause? Is it married life, studies or just a spell of poor form, resulting in loss of interest. Perhaps they just felt they were too old. It need'nt be thought that because one has reached the age of 30 or even 40 one is necessarily past it. Indeed there are instances too numerous to mention of athletes well past 40 putting up class performances. Our own Charlie Smart being a good example. So don't despair those of you who think you are past it, try those shoes on again and take a few gentle training runs. What could be more enjoyable than a spin on Wimbledon Common on a Saturday afternoon? You will probably surprise yourself and a good many others too. Charlie Smart Charlie Smart example of an athlete performing well past 40 Wimbledon Common

items.s: S.L.H. 30miles road race. Report of the S.L.H. 30 miles road race at Old Coulsdon, where Collin Collis finished third and Belgrave were second team to Thames Valley. Saturday Sept.8th. saw us with a full team at Old Coulsdon for this classic event and we were greeted by that elusive body called the sun. The promoters very sportingly delayed the start to enable MacDonald, who had arrived late, to take part, and we finally got away at 2-45p.m. At the end of the first lap Collin Collis and Eric Gebbett were running with the leading bunch of men, with W. Wortley, A. Penstone and A. Bishop not far behind, while A. Byford and J. MacDonald were some way back. After 15miles Collin and Eric were still with the leaders in a time of 1h.29m.30s., but at 17miles Eric began to drop back and at the end of the third lap was some four minutes down. A. Bishop was now our third man and at this stage Wortley and Penstone dropped out, leaving us with five men still in the race. On the last lap Collin held on to third place to finish in the magnificent time of 3hrs.2m.33s., while Eric moved up from ninth to sixth. In spite of having two in the first six we could not prevent Thames Valley's powerful trio from winning the team race. A. Byford was most unfortunate to miss standard by a mere half minute. The actual winner was A. P. Keily of Derby & County A.C. in the record time of 2hrs. 59 mins. 8 secs. 56 started and 41 finished. Finishing positions and times of our men :- Team result :- 3rd. C. items.s: London to Brighton Running Race Report of the London to Brighton running race, in which A. Bishop, W. Wortley and J. MacDonald won the team event and the Len Hurst Belt for Belgrave for the first time. The team result prints Belgrave's score as 21 pts although the places given (12th, 14th, 15th) add to 41; kept as printed. Yet another resounding success was achieved by the Road Running Section when they won the team event in this classic race. The runners concerned were the indomitable trio of A. Bishop J. MacDonald and W. Wortley who had finished second last year. W. Wortley ran with the leaders for about 17 miles when he began to fall back. A. Bishop and J. MacDonald started more soberly and at 10 miles Bishop began to go ahead. Passing 20 miles in 2 hrs. 16 mins. he was 4 mins. behind Wortley, while MacDonald was 3 mins. further back. Wortley was by now beginning to have a rough time but was still under three hours at the marathon distance, and at 27 miles he was overtaken by Bishop. However, he continued to press on in true Belgrave fashion in spite of being reduced almost to a walk. Bishop although fading somewhat after 40 miles managed to hold on to 12th. place and so be our first man home. Wortley and MacDonald were never far apart after 35 miles and finished, in that order, with less than one minute between them; the latter improving on his last year's time by no less than 40 minutes! Our fourth runner A. Byford, did very well to complete the course in 30th. position but said afterwards that he had found it a very long journey. The winner was R.F. Hopcroft of Thames Valley in the very good time of 5 hrs. 36 mins. 26 secs. Finishing positions and times of our men :- Team result :- Having won the Len Hurst Belt for the first time, every effort should be made next year to retain it. So what about it, you marathon men, remember it's only twice the distance and an easy course at that! 12th H.A. Bishop 6 hrs. 39 mins. 26 secs. 14th W. Wortley 6 hrs. 48 mins. 8 secs. 15th J. items.s: Walton - 20th October, 1956. Report of the Walton meeting: Colin Collis's record-breaking second place in the three hours track race and Jack Brown's second place in the 10 miles road race, with Belgrave's positions. This was to prove a great day for Belgrave Harriers, in the two events which were so admirably organised by Walton A. G. and The Road Runners Club. It is impossible to speak too highly of the accurate timekeeping and attention to detail which is always evident in events promoted by these two organisations. THREE HOURS TRACK RACE Ten runners, including our own Colin Collis and Wally Wortley, lined up for this event which was to prove a succession of new English Native Records. 10 miles in 51m.48secs. by Jack Heywood with Colin then fifth in 58m.6secs. and Wally in 61m.4secs. was to lead to a new English Amateur Native Record for 15 miles in 1hr.17m.25secs. by Heywood who then retired. Colin, with his sights set on the full 3hr. run was progressing carefully to complete 15 miles in 1.26.44, 20 miles in 1.55.57, and 25 miles in 2.25.48, truly wonderful pace running. Wally had now retired. Eric Smith had also departed, with a new English Amateur Native Record to his credit for 25 miles of 2.21.19, leaving Colin in second place 3 mins. behind Arthur Keilly and himself leading Beale by the same margin. The testing time had come and Colin was putting everything that willowy frame of his possesses into his last 5 miles. For the first time he was to fall outside 6 minutes per mile but his work was done, for at 3 hours he had covered 30 miles 952 yards 2 feet, a truly magnificent performance having himself broken the then existing records for 25 miles, 30 miles and 3 hours. Arthur Keilly, the winner covered 31 miles 877 yards 11 ins. 10 MILES ROAD RACE As the Manchester Guardian stated "Jack Brown of Belgrave Harriers........made a startling entry into the ranks of short distance road runners when he took second place to O'Gorman in the Walton A.C. 10 miles event". Thus we had two individuals finishing second at Walton on the same day. Jack and O'Gorman left the field after 2 miles and a rare tussle between these two resulted in O'Gorman leading Jack home by only 8 seconds in a new record time of 50m.17secs. beating the previous best by 38 seconds. Charlie Walker and Eric Gebbett ran extremely well. to finish 12th and 13th - Charlie is returning to something like his best form. However, we had to go back to 30th position for our fourth scoring man, Dave Baulch, and consequently we were 3rd team with 47 points behind St. Albans A.C. 39 points and Walton A.C. 45 points. Considering that a field of 130 faced the starter, our lads performed extremely well. A special word of praise to Jim Heathfield, a newcomer to this distance on the roads who covered the course in 55m.55secs. Positions. 2 J. Brown 50m.25s. 35 J. Burr 56m.02s. 12 C. items.sum: Leg-by-leg report of the London to Brighton Relay (Southern Clubs), in which Belgrave finished third behind Thames Valley and Herne Hill, with individual times.
items.s: Road Relay Running Leg-by-leg report of the London to Brighton Relay (Southern Clubs), in which Belgrave finished third behind Thames Valley and Herne Hill, with individual times. LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY (SOUTHERN CLUBS) OCTOBER 13TH. The "Gods" again smiled on us and provided us with another fine day for the second of our bi-annual visits to that famed Regency resort,Brighton. The reporters in the Sunday newspaper organising these races,gave us no chance of winning (as always) which in itself automatically assured us of at least a place. The better-informed thought we might be second to T.V.H, but Herne Hill,now appearing near the front with alarming regularity, proved them wrong by a mere 16 secs.However,this is anticipating our story,so let us proceed. Len Bishop,in place of our regular first runner,P.Bagnall, who was injured,rose well above the form he had shown of late, giving us a reasonably good start finishing 6th behind Poly,H.H.H Aylesford, Hampstead,and St.Albans in that order. Eric Gebbett,more used to 15 and 20 miles than a mere 5,soon proved that he has a turn of speed,quickly passing St.Albans and Hampstead.Poly unfortunately lost their way at tha start of this leg,and dropped to 10th.At Wandsworth H.H.H led from Aylesford and Woodford with Eric not far away.An ominous cloud,in the form of Ken Norris of T.V.H was looming up,and not dismayed by their 10th position on the 1st. leg,he ripped through the field and headed the race before the take-over,as if the hounds of hell were at his heels. He established a lead of 89secs. and chopped 54secs.off the stage record.Eric was undeterred however,and ran steadily throughout to hand over 3rd.behind T.V.H and Woodford,having made up 3 places. Charlie Dabbs,on the long leg from Mitcham to Purley,had the misfortune to start only a few seconds ahead of Ken Caulder of Surrey, Sando, and Towl of H.H.H. Charlie wisely ran his own race,arriving in Purley in 6th. place,just over 2 minutes behind the leaders T.V.H Came George Davidson and hopes that some of the leeway would be made up as George had run so well in the recent road race. Although by no means disgracing himself,he could make no impression and was forced to give way to Thorpe of St.Albans.The experience should be invaluable to George in the future. Jumbo Masters,who we were glad to see out in the team again, set about the opposition through Redhill,passing St.Albans,now exhausted of their supply of good runners,and Surrey,handing over well within striking distance of all but T.V.H.Jumbo had put up the fastest time on hig leg. Ray Tooby,another of our experienced runners who had missed a few Brightons,took over on the flat 5mls.run to Lowfield Heath with three runners in sight.He ran steadily,but his effort lacked spirit,and we made no further headway.We were now 2½ mins down. On the longest leg of all,Jack Brown ran a "blinder",making up 2 places and 30secs on T.V.H.His time was surpassed only by St. Albans' O'Gorman,at that time well behind us.Jack gave Heywood of H.H.H a fright and was unlucky not to catch him before Handcross. The traffic here was exceptionally thick and a slight contretemps with a large car might well have proved serious to our runners. Pete Newall took over on the second longest leg from Hickstead, and although making good progress down Handcross Hill,later regretted this fast start,as many have before him.He quickly caught Ron Clarke, but experience soon prevailed,and Ron steadily pulled away.A game but very tired Newall handed his baton to Geoff Goode at "The Castle" 3mins behind T.V.H and 1¼mins behind H.H.H but still in 3rd position. Geoff was another newcomer to the Brighton trail,and after a good start seemed to be suffering badly on what is thought to be a fairly easy leg,but which is in fact a " snorter " as the writer, in company with other distinguished Club members can well vouch for. However,Geoff pulled himself together and moved well over the last mile in sight of the South Downs. At the foot of Dale Hill,Charlie Walker waited,as usual, wasting much energy asking all and sundry," what do you think?" Would Charlie pull one out of the bag and put us back in the running for 2nd place? By now the winners were almost a foregone conclusion. It was certainly Walker's day when, 97 secs.behind H.H.H., represented by promising J.Davis, he climbed Dale Hill like a champion, and with the aid of continuous encouragement from supporting occupants of cars, the most prominent being the President, he produced the fastest time of the day and took us to within 64 secs. of the "Hill". T.V.H. unfortunately, also had a good performer on this leg and only 6 secs. was pared from their lead, which mattered little as they were now over ½ mile ahead. Dave Baulch, whose running during the summer was a source of disappointment to many (including Mavis) set out to prove his fitness, and with a time of 17.40 on the last leg, a time beaten only by a few Belgravians, raised hopes of our finishing 2nd. Unfortunately the race could not be extended to Black Rock or we should certainly have pegged back those red and black hoops. As it was, a mere 100 yds. separated us from the 2nd team and Dave did the fastest of the day. We can be well satisfied with our effort. Experience has been given to newcomers to this event, which will help us next April, and now that S.L.H. have lost the great Gordon and we can improve on our team by the inclusion of Davies and Hallowell, it can be hoped that last year's 5th position in the National Relay can be bettered by at least 4 places. items.h: Walking Notes: Chippenham to Calne 6 Miles.
items.sum: Walking report on the Chippenham to Calne 6 miles, won by George Coleman, with Belgrave narrowly missing third team place, and results.
items.s: Walking Notes: Chippenham to Calne 6 Miles. Walking report on the Chippenham to Calne 6 miles, won by George Coleman, with Belgrave narrowly missing third team place, and results. Not quite the same star-studded field as in previous years tackled this tough course in lovely weather. We had eleven starters but were without Stan Vickers. Wally Emery put a Belgrave vest in front early on, but unfortunately split his heel and had to retire. Belgrave men, it seemed, were everywhere, and if all had been eligible to score we would have won the team event; as it was we missed third place by one point and were only eight points behind Metropolitan Walking Club, the winners. George Coleman added to his list of triumphs and missed the course record held by R. Hardy by only ten seconds. His opposition were disqualified early on and he won by 2m.39s. in 44m.19s. Next came Eric Hall followed by second claim member George Williams in 47m.38s. Ray Hall gained revenge on Ray Switzer, Norman Guilmant smiled his way through and was last seen selling old football jerseys to the timekeepers. Dennis Russell showed us that he will get his seven-mile badge very soon. It was pleasing to see Doug Woods again and we hope that this is the first of many appearances Doug. Ray Switzer got another crafty fourth handicap and Ray Hall crept in at the last with tenth place while Charlie Speechley was only just behind. This shows an improvement on last year so what about next year lads, lets have our share of the pork pies which go with the first team prize. Eric Hall. 1st. G. Coleman H.H. 44.19 27th. N. items.s: St. Dunstans One Hour Walks Report of the St. Dunstans one hour walks at Parliament Hill, where Stan Vickers set a meeting record and Belgrave won the team race. Parliament Hill 22nd. Sept. Quite a good muster of 26 members took part in the various sections. Highlight of "D" section was John Knifton's fine effort in finishing second with a distance of 6 mls. 795 yds. Ben, his father, competing on the same afternoon, must have been pleased with his 17 year-old son's performance. George Webb gained his 6 mile badge, whilst Bob Readman only just missed his 7 mile. Surely Bob has earned the name "Evergreen"- a grand effort. Ray Switzer, ably backed up by Ray Hall, Dave Stevens and Eric Froude gained his 7 mile badge in this section. Peak of this meeting, is the "A" section, and we saw a grand performance by our lads. Stan Vickers led from the start, followed by George Coleman and at the mile they were 6 m.56s. and 7 m. 3s. respectively. Although Coleman got within 60 yds. of Stan, he could get no nearer and Stan went on to a meeting record of 8 mls. 120 yds. With fine efforts from Eric Hall, Ted Smith, George Checkley and Bob Newson, the latter practically killing himself to take Stan over the last couple of laps, we won the team race from Woodford Green. Well done all concerned - a fine show. J. Goswell. Walking report of the match against M.P.A.A. at Wimbledon, won by Belgrave 392 points to 337 with George Checkley first, plus handicap and positions. This event always marks the opening of our winter fixtures and although some of our lads had travelled to Chippenham for the open event, held on the same day, a field of 38 faced the starter. After some early dashes to the front, a group, including Checkley and Newson, settled down in the lead. George Checkley walked really well to win in 40m.12s. with Bob Newson second, Syd James (whom we are pleased to see out again) third and Eric Froude, still improving, fourth. With quite a number of our lads representing M.P.A.A. we expected a close result, and scoring 18 a side we won by 392 points to 337. The handicap was won by our youngest member John Knifton, so "look out the handicapper". George Webb was second and Bert Stevenson third. As this was the first time any of these chaps had won a pot everyone was well pleased. Fred Freeman won the prize for the first M.P.A.A. man home. Handicap. items.s: R.W.A. Junior 5 Miles Report of the R.W.A. Junior 5 miles at Battersea Park, where Belgrave were second team behind Trowbridge A.C. Battersea Park (Road), October 20th. There is always a small field for this championship owing to call up etc., but this year we had a good little team competing. Ray Middleton, home from Ireland, walked well to finish 6th in 41m.21s., Dave Stevens (individual) was 7th, Nick Milsum 9th and Terry Clark, who walked a blinder on the last lap, was 12th and Trevor Luck 13th. Trowbridge A.C., with 1st and 2nd won the team event with 13 points although their third man was 20th. Belgrave were 2nd with 17 points thanks to Terry Clark's effort, as we tied with Metropolitan W.C. and placing depended upon the third man. Our future looks bright with these rapidly improving lads. J. Goswell. items.sum: Report of the pre-Olympic 10 miles walk trial at Brighton, showing Stan Vickers recovered from injury and Eric Hall walking well before the Melbourne Olympics.
items.s: Pre-Olympic Walk 10 Miles - Brighton 3rd.Nov. Report of the pre-Olympic 10 miles walk trial at Brighton, showing Stan Vickers recovered from injury and Eric Hall walking well before the Melbourne Olympics. Although this race was not taken too seriously,everybody was anxious to see how Stan Vickers had recovered from his leg trouble. In the previous weeks,rumours had flown thick and fast concerning him.After watching Stan and Eric Hall in this trial,we feel sure they will be a credit to their Country and Club,at Melbourne. Stan kept with Hardy and Coleman in the lead until 8-8½ mls but then dropped 5 yards or so.He recovered again and was with the leaders when they went off course after being misdirected,and lost at least ½ ml.After retracing their steps,they decided to walk back together to the stadium. K.Matthews,who had been some 500yards behind when the leaders went off course,was only a few yards behind at the stadium,and whilst lapping the track,decided to pass the three men,which really meant nothing;they were content to stroll in chatting together. Their time 77.16 for over 10½mls indicates the early speed of the race.Eric Hall had walked a very well controlled effort and gradually moved through the field to finish as the 1st Kilos man home in 79.47 for 10mls. We can be justly proud of Stan and Eric,who fully justified their selection.Good luck to them both! J. Goswell. items.label: No. 129
items.sum: Note that member John Bromley, a former steeplechaser, won the 17-mile Singapore to Jahore walking race for the second year.
items.s: John Bromley wins big walk. Note that member John Bromley, a former steeplechaser, won the 17-mile Singapore to Jahore walking race for the second year. We are indebted to a member of Thames Valley Harriers for the report of a Walking Race from Singapore to Jahore,a distance of just over 17 miles,which was won by none other than John Bromley former steeplechaser and Brighton Relay runner in the very good time of 2hrs.56mins. This race,which was promoted by the Singapore Free Press,was held on a Sunday morning,when no less than 650 competitors lined up for the start at 6am. According to press cuttings,John won this race last year,but has apparently kept his achievement up his sleeve as this appears to be the first intimation that he has turned to road walking.We do like to hear of the activities of our members who are overseas and hope that any others who are carrying on the good work will let us know about it. Of the 650 starters,430 finished the course,and John received once again the handsome trophy presented for annual competition by Messrs Bata,the shoe people,and the prize of a cinecamera presented by Twentieth Century Fox Films Ltd. Well done John. Bill True is making note of the result in case you continue walking on your return to this country. S.C.R. items.sum: Note from the new Youth and Junior Section secretary on training packs at Wimbledon, with results of a junior 3 mile road race and a 4 lap road relay at Battersea Park.
items.s: For the Attention of all Juniors and Youths Note from the new Youth and Junior Section secretary on training packs at Wimbledon, with results of a junior 3 mile road race and a 4 lap road relay at Battersea Park. This article is primarily for the benefit of the Youth and Junior Section of our club, of which you, the members, have nominated me as Secretary. There are a few points I would like to make which I feel some of you would like to know. ONE. is that I am always ready to listen to any suggestion as regards the functions of our sections. TWO. I am endeavouring to form one, or more training packs during the Winter months; at the moment, we are training from Wimbledon on Tuesday and Thursday nights at 7-0 pm. and Saturday afternoons. I am grading the packs to enable runners of varying ability to enjoy these runs and also to develop each individual without his being run off his legs. This is most important as every Champion will tell you pack running is the foundation of Team running by which we can endeavour to win the Major Events during the Cross Country Season. There are two results which apply to our Section:- 3 Mile Road Race at Wimbledon 29.9.56 K. Miller is a new member and shows every promise. 4 Lap Road Relay at Battersea Park 21.10.56. This race was organised by M. Pyer. and was arranged to give our younger members a chance to show what they could do. Their ages ranged from 12½ to 15½ years. One of our members, E. Penny, recorded second fastest time over the course, which is approximately 1¾ miles. His time was 8 mins. 49secs. which is very good running, but a Mitcham lad did even better- his time being 8 mins. 42 secs. A. W. Penny. (Secretary) Junior Section. 1. A.W.Black - 15.41. 2. K. items.sum: Teasing notes about cross-country runners neglecting club nights at Belgrave Hall, not wearing Belgrave vests and skipping an away road relay.
items.s: Stirrings Teasing notes about cross-country runners neglecting club nights at Belgrave Hall, not wearing Belgrave vests and skipping an away road relay. It is a pity that some Cross-Country Runners (not Night-School Students) who manage the journey to run at Wimbledon some evenings, have apparently forgotten the whereabouts of Belgrave Hall on Club Nights. Members may be assured that if they bring their shampoo on Tuesday or Thursday we can arrange for the extractor fan to be dismantled and converted into a hair dryer. An assurance has been received that in the later cross-country events, runners at present so allergic to their Belgrave vests when representing their Club will wear them. Do they mean when they should be in their County vests? It is heartbreaking to learn that the official reason for not supporting an away road relay where free overnight accommodation had been promised was given as the reluctance of runners to miss their Sunday morning training run!!! Wimbledon Belgrave Hall

items.label: No. 130
items.sum: Editorial asking members to send in regular reports, explaining a plan to post the magazine with the fixture cards, and urging full Belgrave support in all matches for the 1957 season.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial asking members to send in regular reports, explaining a plan to post the magazine with the fixture cards, and urging full Belgrave support in all matches for the 1957 season. Dear Fellow Members, Once upon a time, we used to read this magazine, and we often wondered why it was that the editors were repeatedly asking the officials of each branch of the Club, to send in REGULAR reports of its activities, together with any other items of interest. Now we know! We are not magicians, and cannot be expected to prepare the magazine in the few days immediately before it is due to be printed. To lighten our task therefore, we must ask that reports be sent to us weekly, BY ANYONE, be he spectator, competitor or official. In fact, the wider the field of contribution, the greater the interest of the magazine. What could be more simple than scribbling a report on the way home in the train? Furthermore, in the interests of economy, it is hoped to combine the despatch of the Belgravian with that of the fixture cards, thereby saving approximately £10 per annum. This cannot be achieved unless the magazine can be completed each quarter and sent for printing on time. So let's be hearing from all you budding reporters. We would like to thank those anonymous contributors who have sent us articles for this edition. No doubt they will appreciate that where we receive more than one report on the same event, the contents, as near as possible, are combined, and any loss of style will be understood. By the time this edition is distributed, the track season will be with us, and the programme of long distance road races will have commenced. We want to see full Belgrave support in all the major events, on the Track, in Field Events, and on the Road. Whilst agreeing that athletics is a sport to be enjoyed, win or lose, we feel that the time has come for us to endeavour to assert ourselves as the premier club in the South, and to do this by putting our full strength into all matches. We have an abundance of talent in our ranks, at all ages. Messrs. Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches. Everyone must start at the bottom, and none is so good that he can afford to ignore minor events. The presence of a "Star" in a race is a challenge to the lesser lights to topple him from his pedestal, and he learns that only hard work will keep him there. The unknown having tasted victory will be eagerly looking around for his next "head". Keen competition within the Club for team places is the key to success, but it must be made certain that there are sufficient "B" team matches to enable second string men to gain that experience necessary for promotion to the "A" team. We hope to be reporting the successful commencement of the 1957 season in our next issue. Your coaches can only guide you, you must do the work. Your success will be their well-deserved reward. So go to it and good luck! Your Editors. items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR. 10th. NOV. Report of a poor Belgrave turnout at the South of Thames Junior cross-country race at Brighton, with Charlie Dabbs 8th and the A, B and D team placings. SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR. 10th. NOV. Is the Brighton seaside air not encouraging enough itself or does the thought of a journey frighten many Belgravians? Whatever it was, there was a poor turnout for this event - less in fact, than half those entered. I would add that one of our newer members' worked until midday and then journeyed down by train to compete. The race itself was disappointing from the point of view of Club supporters, who were also few in number. Charlie Dabbs gave of his best again and finished 8th., but I feel much credit should go to J. Dooley, who although entered in the "D" team, finished 54th. to be the third Belgrave man home. As for the other competing members, I am sure they would all admit to having had better runs than this. Once again Arthur Whitehead must be thanked for supplying a very welcome cup of tea to all our runners at the finish. Placings and team positions:- 7th.Belgrave "A" ( 8 C. Dabbs, 50 G. items.sum: Report of Jack Brown winning the City of Rochester 5 mile road race from Salvat of Finchley, with Ray Tooby 12th and Len Bishop 46th.
items.s: CITY OF ROCHESTER 5 mile ROAD RACE 17th NOV. 1956 Report of Jack Brown winning the City of Rochester 5 mile road race from Salvat of Finchley, with Ray Tooby 12th and Len Bishop 46th. CITY OF ROCHESTER 5 mile ROAD RACE 17th NOV. 1956 The usual cold, misty weather greeted the starters for this year's race, but soon warming to his task, Jack Brown set about the opposition in no uncertain manner and was soon in the leading bunch with Salvat of Finchley and Cameron of T.V.H. Jack and Salvat ran neck and neck until approximately 500yds from the finish, when Jack's fine burst of speed proved too much for his opponent. The winning time was only 8sec. outside George Knight's course record. Ray Tooby, continuing his welcome return to form, ran very well to finish 12th, only three seconds behind Haslam (T.V.H.). Len Bishop who arrived only just in time for the start, finished 46th. It was a pity we did not have more support for this event, as no doubt we could have been placed in the team race. 1st J.W. Jack Brown ran very impressively to win by a full minute from Charlie Walker with Ray Tooby half a minute further back in third place. Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap. Second place in the handicap went to Clive Shippen who finished 5th in the actual race - a very good performance. It is very unusual for the scratch man to be placed in a sealed handicap, but in securing third place, Jack Brown achieved this feat. items.s: THE MITCHAM"15" JAN. 12th. Report of Belgrave winning the Mitcham 15 team award, with Jack Brown beating O'Gorman and cutting 41 seconds off Jim Peters' course record; the text places Len Bishop 15th but the result and a later sentence give 14th. THE MITCHAM"15" JAN. 12th. Our road runners notched a further great victory when providing the individual winner of this very popular event and carrying off the team award. Continuing along his road of success Jack Brown sliced off 41 seconds from Jim Peters course record, a most meritorious performance. The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of a dozen, including our own trio, Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop on the other. Jack and O'Gorman, however, had what appeared to be a burning desire to be all alone and with a big effort between 5 and 9 miles (at which point the time was 44m 30s!) they had established a lead of 20 seconds. Any hopes of individual honours cherished by the following group had by now completely vanished. The further these two went, the diminutive O'Gorman and the taller Jack, his hair bouncing with each stride, the greater the gap became, and Keily, who had moved up to third, was soon almost out of sight. Colin, Eric and Len were firmly dug in at 8th, 9th and 15th respectively and Jim Heathfield, confounding everyone, looked very comfortable in 28th place. The wise head of Collis had obviously intervened in Jim's training. Back to the leaders, where, with 400 yds. to go, Jack produced an amazing turn of speed which completely overwhelmed O'Gorman, with the incredible result that Jack ran out the winner by 14 seconds! It is indeed food for thought when one realises that these two had run throughout at approximately 4m.58s. per mile; how about the marathon Jack? With Eric and Colin finishing in good style 8th and 9th, no doubts were felt about the team result. A word of consolation to Len Bishop for finishing 14th in a fast time, yet being denied a team prize. However, let this be a reminder that road-running honours are going to be difficult to come by this season. It was good to see our London to Brighton men, Alan Bishop, MacDonald and Wortley sharpening up early in the season, it is hoped they will soon be starting their long preparation. A special word of praise to Jim Heathfield, whose time of 89m.28s. would open the eyes of many considered road runners. If the Mitcham "15" is any criterion, then the Belgrave vest will be well to the fore in all the leading road events during 1957. items.s: CLUB 10 MILES CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP 26th JAN. 1957 Report and result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship, won by Jack Brown for the eighth successive Macher Shield, with Paget winning the handicap. CLUB 10 MILES CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP 26th JAN. 1957 Although the course was below the stipulated distance (approximately 9¾ miles), the times were nevertheless very fast. In addition the terrain was rather muddy in places and light rain was falling during most of the race. The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind. At eight miles Brown was 1 min. 20 sec. to the good, with Walker 20 sec. in front of Baulch, and Tooby, having pulled away from Gebbett, now running fourth. Over the last couple of miles there were no positional changes amongst the leaders, but the distance between them lengthened, and at the finish Brown came home an easy winner in the excellent time of 50m.27s. Jack must be congratulated on winning the "Macher Shield" for the eighth time in succession, but we must also extend our congratulations to Charlie Walker—for indeed it is no disgrace to be runner-up to Jack—and Dave Baulch for a really splendid performance. items.s: Carnival Dance 26th Jan. 1957 Account of the Social Section's carnival dance, with a comedy sketch, rock n' roll dancing, games and music from the A.T.C. Skiffle Group. Carnival Dance 26th Jan. 1957 Once again the Social Section of the Club did a fine job, and a good time was had by all. Stan Vickers and Ray Hall again acted as Phillip Harbens in the Sausage and Mash Supper Comedy, this time ably assisted by Mrs. Goswell and Mrs. Knifton, who took the part of Mrs. Beatons. Dancing went very well with all the old-timers lowering their dignity to do rock n' roll; it was a treat to watch. The various games and activities (mainly organised by Bill Lucas) proved very pleasant interludes, as well as a source of great enjoyment both to those taking part and to those watching. The A.T.C. Skiffle Group provided some very lively interval music - thanks boys. It only remains for me to ask "When's the next dance?" CHRISTMAS Report and result of the annual half-hour paarlauf at Christmas, poorly supported because of a clash with a Herne Hill fixture and won by the Belgrave pair Charlie Walker and C. Henn. ANNUAL HALF-HOUR PAARLAUF. CHRISTMAS This event would have had much more support had there not been a friendly fixture with Herne Hill on the same day. When it is considered how much work Arthur Whitehead puts in to this race he must find it very discouraging to have his efforts (unwittingly it is hoped) sabotaged in this manner. The race itself, run in very pleasant weather, resolved into a dual between a Belgrave pair, Charlie Walker and C. Henn, and two Hercules runners, who together with four others had been invited to compete. When the signal, indicating three minutes to go, was given, Charlie and D. Cobb of Hercules were running together in the lead. It is a very difficult business to try to estimate just how much time is left but Charlie managed it to a nicety and putting in his effort with about ten seconds to go, drew away to win by several yards. items.sum: Report of a Belgrave team winning an eight-mile cross-country match against Westminster Bank at Epsom by one point, with Flanagan first.
items.s: MATCH V. WESTMINSTER BANK AT EPSOM 28th Dec. Report of a Belgrave team winning an eight-mile cross-country match against Westminster Bank at Epsom by one point, with Flanagan first. MATCH V. WESTMINSTER BANK AT EPSOM 28th Dec. As there was an"A" team match at Wimbledon on the same day we were fortunate in mustering nine runners at Epsom for this pleasant little fixture. The course of eight miles was genuine cross-country, consisting of hills, mud and plough, with a short stretch of road. Flanagan ran very well to finish first, beating Gilham of the Bank by 15 sec. They were followed by three Bank runners but as the next six were all Belgravians, the balance was tipped slightly in our favour and we won by one point - a very fair result. Afterwards we were entertained to tea, for which we were very grateful, and a somewhat strenuous afternoon was brought to a fitting conclusion. Our hosts expressed the wish that we might visit them again next year - fixture committee please take note ! items.s: SOUTH OF THE THAMES SENIOR Report of the South of the Thames senior cross-country race at Maidenhead, where the Belgrave team finished only 15th, complaining that no individual results were sent in. SOUTH OF THE THAMES SENIOR Held at Maidenhead on Feb. 2nd over an extremely heavy course this race proved a big disappointment for the Club when our team could finish only 15th. We do not agree with the view held in some parts of the Club, that reports of races in which the Club is unsuccessful should be withheld from this magazine. This attitude, which we feel is quite wrong, probably explains the almost complete lack of news from the Cross-Country Section. We cannot therefore give any details of individual performances in this race as they are not in our possession. We can only hope that someone will do something to remedy this unsatisfactory state of affairs and see to it that we are regularly supplied with results, be they favourable or otherwise. South of the Thames Senior Maidenhead

items.s: NEW YEAR CELEBRATIONS DEC.29th. Account of the Social Committee's New Year celebrations, with a bangers-and-mash supper, games, a skiffle band and thanks to Bill Lucas as M.C. and Tom Carter. NEW YEAR CELEBRATIONS DEC.29th. It seems an understatement to say the evening was a resounding success, in the light of the gaiety, fun, entertainment and the whole gamut of carefreeness devised by our Social Committee. Bangers, grilled to a turn, potatoes, bashed and pounded to insensibility by a team of master cooks, headed by such International figures as Messieurs Vickers, Hall and Goswell with a posse of Presidents to act as scullions. The resulting "Chef-d'oeuvre", supported by lashings of tea, rolls and butter, etc., was treated with suspicion until the full delicacy of the masterly preparation was appreciated with cries more. This was a prelude to a programme of carnival festivities which for gaiety, fun and whole-hearted co-operation from all, led to an ever-to-be-remembered evening. Nothing appeared forgotten or left to chance. That difficult warming up period was successfully negotiated by a series of games, chief of which was sniffing at mysterious looking bags. The consequent fun soon broke the ice. A "Skiffle Band" performance introduced by Eric Penny thoroughly livened up the interval and the numerous encores were sufficient proof of appreciation. Thank you Eric and your colleagues for their grand show. It is unnecessary to dwell on the lovely and charming ladies present, they were indeed all beautiful, sufficient to thank them for their presence and co-operation; our reward is to see them so thoroughly enjoying themselves. Finally a word of appreciation to our Social Committee for a wonderful evening, particularly to Bill Lucas for his grand job as M.C. to which we were all indebted, and to Tom Carter for all his work so enthusiastically carried out. items.sum: Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Epsom, where the Belgrave senior team finished 3rd behind South London and Thames Valley, led by Jack Brown, with junior and youths race notes and positions.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. EPSOM. FEB.16th. Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Epsom, where the Belgrave senior team finished 3rd behind South London and Thames Valley, led by Jack Brown, with junior and youths race notes and positions. SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. EPSOM. FEB.16th. Senior race. We are back amongst the top Southern clubs again as a result of the fine performance of our team in finishing 3rd. behind South London and Thames Valley. Our six scoring men, led by Jack Brown, were all well placed throughout, and whilst commendably they held those placings, one did not see the spectacle of the claret and gold vests moving up through the field in last desperate attempts to whittle away those points. However, let nothing detract from their performance, it was a welcome and heartening sight, and it should not be overlooked that the course was one mile short. A fast start saw a keen struggle for the lead with our second claim member, Bill Bird of Ranelagh actually leading during the early stages. Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth. Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner. Then came Chas. Walker, Pete Bagnall, Dave Baulch and Eric Gebbett, all running strongly and all four within reach of one another but unable apparently to join forces, a fact which probably cost us second team place. Although still very husky from a heavy cold, Shippen was about the 100 mark with Len Bishop, Eddie Short and Jim Heathfield further back. And so it was, our lads hung on grimly to their early gains and ran out a good third with Jack Brown, a little disappointed perhaps, our first man home. The Bels were ably backed up by the moral and vocal support of many members, and it was good to see Tom Carter, a most decididly active President, whipping 'em up along the line. Many of us know from past experience, especially as juniors, what encouragement is derived from the attendance of Club officials of whatever capacity, at events of this nature. This was brought to mind even more by the presence of Ernie Duffett, whom we were glad to see looking fit and well. Arthur Penny seems to have earned the respect and loyalty of those juniors under his care and it is to be hoped that his efforts will be rewarded next year by some real team running again in those events in which we were once so prominent. Latent talent will not pass Arthur's eye unnoticed. Our sages tell us that we always perform better in the National than in the Southern, so let us look to even better news after the Parliament Hill battlefield on March 9th. Positions :- 10, J.W. items.s: WALKING NOTES. Walking notes congratulating the club's Olympic walkers, welcoming new juniors, and appealing for support for the track season and the Brighton walk. WALKING NOTES. These are, of necessity, brief, but tell of the continued progress of the Club. To others I have left the Olympics, but I am sure I echo the sentiments of all when I say, "Well done Eric and Stan, you were a credit in every way to the Club". With these two, ably backed up, we have great hopes of winning the National 10 again; Sheffield eight years running is too much! Tuesday evenings throughout the Winter have seen good turn-outs at the hall. As a result we lead the Southern clubs in the Winter "Opens" again. We have a fine crowd of up and coming Juniors and welcome Bryan Cormick, George Barratt, M. Small and John Gilbert. May they look back with pride on the day they became "Bels". Coach Don Brown is always pleased to help you, and we start our track season soon. We want a good school at Battersea on Tues. and Thurs.; it is essential to all short distance men, whom we look to, to regain our Inter-Club Track Title this year, whilst we hope the long distance men also retain our hard won titles. I hope to issue dates of fixtures we are supporting this year, along with the R.W.A. 20 and Kilos and the Brighton. We look forward to a grand Summer and to A.A.A. titles for Stan and ....? - who knows? Rally round supporters, your vocal efforts are needed to drive the "Bels" along. Unless we get more support we may have to discontinue the hire of a coach for the Brighton; a nearly empty coach on the journey down is such an expense - the competitors could more cheaply return by train. Let me know early please so that I can see whether a coach is warranted. Training with a happy crowd is great fun. Experiences gained are many. Stan Vickers, back from Melbourne, revealed his prowess in cooking "Bangers". Come along, join in the good fellowship that is to be had. Reap the benefits of FITNESS. In closing, my thanks to all who have helped me in various ways during a busy season. By their ever-ready help and co-operation they enabled the Club to stage another successful Open Walk and the S.R.W.A. Garnet Cup Championship. Thank you, one and all, Yours, Jack Goswell. items.s: CLUB 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP (MURPHY SHIELD) Report and result of the club 10 miles walking championship for the Murphy Shield, won again by Eric Hall, held with a match against the Metropolitan Police. CLUB 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP (MURPHY SHIELD) Chiefly due to a clash with the Stock Exchange 7 miles championships, only 29 walkers started, and we were without Stan Vickers, Ray Hall and Dave Stevens. Eric Hall retained his title, winning by 34 sec. from 2nd claim member George Williams who had travelled up from Worcester (that's enthusiasm). In the champioship Dave McMullen was 2nd and Syd James 3rd. Dave just pipped Williams for the handicap with Bob Readman a popular 3rd. What a pity Bob's new job prevents regular attendance, our youngsters could benefit from him. A match versus Met. Police was held in conjunction with the race which we won by scoring 90 pts. to 192. In true Belgrave style, a tea and social followed the race: in all, a thoroughly enjoyable day. Result of club championship as under:- 1 E.W. Hall 79.38 12 C. Yescombe 91.27 2 G. Williams 80.12 13 J. items.sum: Reports and results of the Surrey, Kent and Middlesex 10 miles walking championships, with Eric Hall winning Surrey, Stan Vickers Kent, and Belgrave walkers placing second for Cadogan A.C. in Middlesex; the Surrey text gives Switzer 9th and Coleman 10th while the table gives 10th and 11th.
items.s: RESULTS OF COUNTY 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIPS 23RD FEBRUARY, 1957 Reports and results of the Surrey, Kent and Middlesex 10 miles walking championships, with Eric Hall winning Surrey, Stan Vickers Kent, and Belgrave walkers placing second for Cadogan A.C. in Middlesex; the Surrey text gives Switzer 9th and Coleman 10th while the table gives 10th and 11th. RESULTS OF COUNTY 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIPS 23RD FEBRUARY, 1957 SURREY AT MITCHAM We started two teams, and 44 walkers faced the started in driving rain. Eric Hall took the lead, closely followed by George Williams. Eric broke away after half-a-mile and thereafter was in no danger of defeat. 63 sec. up at the half distance, he won by 2 min.15sec. from George, who had walked well and always held second place from Dave McMullen who suffered from cramp at 7 miles, but held 3rd place, finishing almost 2 min. ahead of the fourth man. We scored 1,2,3, with Ray Switzer 9th and Joe Coleman 10th. Ray Hall, walking as an individual gained County colours by finishing 6th. Jim Edwards, in his first County 10, performed well. Our "B" team was completed by Joe Wilson, George Webb and Dan Logan, who suffered from the cold. What a distance man Webb would make with regular training! He has obvious potential. Summing up - a grand repeat performance by Eric and a first class team. 43 finished KENT AT BEXLEY Stan Vickers retained his title, winning by the incredible margin of 7m.32s. in 78m.14s. Another new course record (that's three on the trot). Well done Stan! MIDDLESEX AT EASTCOTE Driving rain for a couple of hours or so before the start of this race threatened almost impossible conditions, but fortunately it eased as the competitors started on the hilly course. We had eight walkers competing for Cadogan A.C. and although our chances of a win were slender, we were not without hope. Metropolitan W.C. soon put paid to these by a splendid exhibition of team walking, eventually winning with the absolute mimimum score of 10pts., finishing the first four home. Ted Smith was our great hope for the individual title and at two miles had a lead of afew yards over the field. From the three mile point however, he must have become very tired at the sight of Met vests for he found himself walking with six or seven of their men from then on. Eventually Ted finished sixth, a creditable performance. George Checkley walked strongly in the second half of the race, gaining several places and finishing just in front of Bob Newson who walked evenly throughout. Our fourth man, Hugh McGreechan lost several places in the last two miles but our margin over the third club, Polytechnic H., was always an appreciable one. Of our others, Cyril Yescombe and Harry Shields had their usual social outing, and George Place and Syd Spencer seemed to enjoy their trip round this corner of Middlesex which still has fields and trees to show something remaining of a rural atmosphere. items.s: THE R.W.A. "GARNET CUP" CHAMPIONSHIP Report and result of the R.W.A. Garnet Cup 10 miles walk staged by Belgrave at Belgrave Hall, won by C. Williams of Ilford, with Belgrave 4th team and Ray Middleton their best man in 14th. THE R.W.A. "GARNET CUP" CHAMPIONSHIP At Belgrave Hall 2nd Feb. 1957 Local arrangements for this Southern 10 miles event (which is a "limited" Championship in that many barring clauses operate) were entrusted to us by the Race Walking Association; and we are confident that this trust was not misplaced. Our excellent accommodation at Belgrave Hall is indeed a great foundation to build upon, and with Jack Goswell and Arthur Whitehead working like beavers to ensure faultless arrangements for the planning and conduct of the race, and with Syd Roberts in charge of the scoring and recording details, we had all the ingredients for the perfect promotion. All that was needed in addition was reasonable weather and a good field - and these, too, were forthcoming. Stan Horton, Chairman of the R.W.A. Southern Area, started the field of 114 walkers, and C. Williams of Ilford A.C., the favourite, was soon in the lead and retained this to finish a very worthy winner from A.G. Thomson of Met. W.C. with M. Tadd of Brighton A.C. third. As our winning team of last year was no longer eligible and as many of our other walkers have previously shed their "Junior" status, we realised that our team prospects could not be considered of the brightest; but that they would give of their utmost we were sure, and we could not ask for more than that. The team race was keenly fought out and at one time was very open, but Met. W.C. gradually strengthened their hold to eventually finish easy winners. Woodford Green took second medals, and Brighton A.C., by two points, deprived us of third place. We had expected Trevor Luck to take a forward position in this year's race but he unfortunately broke a wrist a fortnight earlier, thus belying his name, and must wait another year. True he started but it was a forlorn hope with arm in plaster from wrist to elbow and training lost; he did well and revealed great pluck in finishing the race. Our three, Ray Middleton, Nick Milsum and Ray Switzer pursued a steady course together for the first half of the race and then began their advance through the field, with Middleton proving himself our best man on the day, finishing in 14th position. Our team was completed by Cyril Yescombe, and thereafter the Belgrave vests followed in at intervals until we had finished twelve men of the 107 completing the course. When next year's event comes round we are sure that many of our walkers will be showing that they have made progress; and one of our boys who should assuredly make the grade is John Keown. In conclusion, a pat on the back to our team and the assurance that we shall be among the placings again next year; and our renewed sincere thanks to all who helped with the event, with particular reference to the herculean labours of Jack and Arthur. items.sum: Eric Hall's account of the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games, including the athletics highlights and the walks in which he and Stan Vickers competed.
items.s: THE OLYMPIC GAMES Eric Hall's account of the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games, including the athletics highlights and the walks in which he and Stan Vickers competed. THE OLYMPIC GAMES By Eric Hall Our quarters were situated in the Olympic Village, Heidelburg, 10 miles from the Stadium and we reached them at 7a.m. on 12th Nov.1956 after a five day flight from London. The accommodation was pretty good except when it rained - as it did early in our stay - then everything was thick mud. Also excellent was the food, with great variety as well as quantity: indeed if one tackled every meal one couldn't do any training. The Opening Ceremony on Nov. 22nd will always be remembered as the big moment of the Games. We were driven the 10 miles to the stadium in coaches and the streets were lined with cheering crowds. The actual march of ¼ mile into the stadium was used by the crowd for some good-humoured bantering such as:- "Where's the Ashes?" "What about Jim Laker" We managed, however, to hold our own. At last the Games were open and we were greeted with our first spell of warm weather - 84degrees. Soon the athletes were holding the attention of over 100,000 spectators every day and on the Friday the first finals were decided. You know the results by now so I will not dwell on the details, but certain things, however, stick in one's memory at every athletic meeting. First of all, the machine-like running of Kuts - 400m steady, 70 to 100m fast - "steady" being 68s. in the 10,000m and faster still in the 5,000! Then the ease with which Bob Morrow completed the first double sprint victory since Jesse Owens's in 1936. Greg Bell long-jumping 25ft odd with a damaged leg-muscle which finally "went" on his last jump and Derek Johnson so nearly beating Tom Courtney in the 800m. One of the highlights of the Games was the high-jump duel between Dumas of the U.S.A. and unknown Porter of Australia - Dumas who found it too much trouble to convert metres to feet and Porter who peered at the bar before jumping. Bob Richards needed three attempts to qualify in the pole vault and Oerter, who had not seen a discus a year ago, won the Gold Medal, while our own Mark Pharaoh missed third place by five inches. In the javelin, Danielsen never really got loosened up until his last throw when he threw it almost out of the arena to record over 280ft. We had our sad moments also, the last Saturday proving the worst day, with our comparative failure in the 1500m - I do not mean failure in the extreme sense of the word, as a 4m.2s. mile is no flop! At that time I was out on the marathon course and saw Ron Clark and Fred Norris run themselves to a standstill and finally retire, to leave Harry Hicks gamely battling on to the finish, although being attacked with cramp on the track. However, our three relay teams kept the flag flying. The girls track events were shared amongst the Australians with our girls making the 100 & 200 metres finals, while the field events were dominated by the Russians. Perhaps the greatest moment of the Games, for me, was to see two of our men leading an Olympic field - and one of them a Belgravian. I mean of course, the 20km. walk in which Stan Vickers put up such a remarkable performance in holding off the Russians for so long and then giving chase in faultless style. Indeed, by his style, Stan earned for himself the title of "The Walker". I must not overlook the fact that we won a Gold Medal - all praise to Chris Brasher -"the hack who finally became a Champion". So much has been said and written about this event that I do not intend to say anything except that the two steeple-chasers, Rozsnyoi and Larsen, were great sportsmen. The 50km. walk brought us a spot of bother when Don Thompson, who was in fifth position at the time, collapsed from the heat with only 3kms. to go. He was taken to hospital but fortunately made a very quick recovery and now shows no ill effects. The feeding arrangements for this race and for the Marathon were good as was the policing of the courses. The judging in the 20km. walk left much to be desired and Stan should have had at least a bronze medal. However, we should be thankful for the fact that there were no international incidents. Stan was selected for the British Empire versus U.S.A. meeting but owing to the chaos it is not certain where he finished. He apparently had a good time in Sydney and it should be noted that the aforementioned city is now back to normal! We flew home via the United States, so making a round-the-world tour of 27,000 miles, a month's holiday and an unforgetable experience. As Stan says, "roll on 1960". Eric Hall P.S. We would both like to thank all those Club members who gave us their best wishes before we left. We would add that even if we didn't win we at least took part and had a very good try. E.W.H.& S.F.V. items.sum: The Coaching Hon. Secretary lists the club's coaches for the coming season and invites offers of help and attendance at coaching courses.
items.s: COACHING The Coaching Hon. Secretary lists the club's coaches for the coming season and invites offers of help and attendance at coaching courses. COACHING Our coaches these days may not be numerous but we will do all we can to assist anyone who will take the trouble to seek our advice. Frank Simmons will as usual be looking after the sprinters and relay-teams and putting in a tremendous amount of hard work. Stan Davies, Charlie Smart, Arthur Penny and George Isaac can give you assistance in the middle and long distances. Micky Pyer will be continuing his good work with the boys and youths and all our younger members should get to know him. I, myself, can, I hope, help all budding Field Events men and will seek to improve the better performers. Having mentioned that our Coaches are none too numerous, I would welcome any offers of assistance from people who think they are past their best and would like to help the younger members. A number of Coaching Courses are run throughout the season which, if attended, will give anyone a good insight into modern methods of training and technique. Some of these courses are for active athletes too and will benefit anyone who attends and more particularly if he takes his coach along with him. I shall have details of these from time to time and will be only too glad to pass them on to those interested. T.C. Jones, Coaching Hon. items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP Field events notes by T.C. Jones urging members to train and enter championships, aiming to retain the Sward Trophy at Chiswick, and reviewing the club's throwers and jumpers. FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP The Field Events Notes in the last issue were, I'm afraid, rather scanty owing to pressure of space. The Summer Season is fast approaching and I hope all Seniors, Juniors and Youths will be getting down to training in earnest for the coming fixtures. Your Captain, Mal Ash, Vice Captain Dave Ansell and myself want your full support so that we can turn out strong teams. What we want to see more than anything else is the name of Belgrave well represented in County, District and A.A.A. Championships. You may not be good enough to win or get a place but there are standard certificates or medals to be won. The entries of our Youths and Juniors are particularly needed in these events. I will be able to supply all information as to dates and venues of these meetings in due course. Our main effort this Summer will be to retain the Sward Trophy which we won so handsomely last year. This meeting will take place at Chiswick on May 11th and there is no reason why we should not have a very strong team. I remember our first puny efforts in this competition some eight or ten years ago when we only gained half a point - how we gradually built up year by year culminating in success. Go to it lads and retain that Trophy. Just a "by the way" here - in the past our Cross-Country and road-relay teams have had great vocal support. There is no reason why such a meeting as "The Sward" cannot be just as interesting. Throwers and Jumpers will respond to encouragement by Club-Mates and Supporters in the same way as runners and walkers. They'd be glad to see and hear you at Chiswick. Thames Valley Harriers started last year a Winter Field Events Meeting and again this year put on a similar meeting. Roy Liggins, Ted Gaworski and Percy Porter competed. Percy was 2nd in the Hammer and Ted was in the first six in the Discus. We ourselves decided to promote a similar meeting on March 2nd at Battersea. Support from all Club members is essential and I have been promised entries from some of the top performers in the London area. Let's trust the weather will be kind and so help to make this a worthwhile effort. During the season we shall have the usual Club matches. We have received invitations to compete in most of the big trophy matches including the "Kinnaird" and "Brockman". Your efforts last year were all well rewarded and this year we should do even better. Mal Ash assures me he will be making his usual stupendous efforts again and we hope to see him pull off the A.A.A. Decathlon as well as successfully defending his Surrey and Southern titles. John Powell Jones and Dick Harris will, I hope, get nearer that 50 feet with the shot and Ted Gaworski be as consistent as ever with both shot and discus. Our Long-Jumpers are quite strong again with Percy Luxom, Dave Ansell, Charlie Jones, Adjei and Mal Ash all round about or over 22 feet. I hope to see Dave Ansell do 23 feet consistently. Luxom and Jones together with Norman Caves are out main Triple-Jumpers and should do well. Our Javelin men, Roy Liggins and George Edwards, should both improve and get nearer the 200 ft mark. We also have a number of promising Juniors including Reg Chamberlain who got 2nd place in the Surrey Long Jump last year and we hope to see more Youths competing along with Colin Clair and Malcom Draper. In addition to the Club matches we shall, as usual, hold some Handicaps and I would like to see these better supported than in the past. These events are ideal for some of you runners to try out a new event and who knows, some of you may show more potential here than in the distances you have been struggling over in the past. T.C. items.s: THE CHILDREN'S PARTY 6th Jan. 1957 Report of the club children's party, with thanks to the ladies who catered and the helpers who entertained. THE CHILDREN'S PARTY 6th Jan. 1957 Like the dance the week before, this party went off very well, although it was quite noticeable that the adults outnumbered the children easily. The food and drinks were catered for by the ladies of the Club, Mesdames: Carter, Shepherd, Savage, Penny and Morrell, while their better halves thoroughly enjoyed themselves entertaining the "kids". Bob Taylor deserves special mention as he really worked hard keeping the older boys amused with balloon football - well done Bob! Father Christmas gave a very convincing performance and presented each child with a gift, I'm sure some of the grown-ups were jealous - I know I was. Musical songs and games were arranged by Auntie Brenda and Uncle Bill Lucas with Auntie Joan at the piano. On behalf of the children and lookers-on I would like to say - a big thank-you to all the helpers - we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. By the way, Mr. Harry Evans, the cake was delicious - thank you. P.S. I would like to ask the great Mr. Stanley Vickers to look after his hot-dogs in future - one was found on the kitchen floor, exactly a week and a day after it was cooked!!!? items.sum: Letter from Arthur Whitehead thanking those who marked cross-country courses during the winter and the members who supplied equipment.
items.s: Letter from Arthur Whitehead thanking those who marked cross-country courses during the winter and the members who supplied equipment. We are pleased to include the following letter from Arthur Whitehead, to whom the Club owes so much :- Dear Editors, Now that the Cross-country season has unfortunately ended, may I express, through you, my thanks to those who have assisted the Club by marking courses throughout the Winter. This is, whatever the unitiated may think, an extremely difficult and energetic task and our reward is in the knowledge that nobody (perhaps Dooley would prefer me to say no visitor) went off course. It is delightful to think that we have been able to assist such a variety of organisations as our County AAA, the Stock Exchange, the Breweries, Boy Scouts and Catholic Schools and all of these have expressed their deepest appreciation which I would wish to pass on to all concerned in full measure. We are entitled to assume also that the marking of Club Championship courses and inter-club matches is appreciated. Upon the "stores" side may I thank Arthur Penny for the poles which have so much improved and brightened our Finish, George Beecham for a further consignment of flag material, Gordon Biscoe for making the Finish remain upright and Mrs. Edgar for the colourful flags she so kindly made for the starting pens of the County Senior race. The other side? The incessant sabotage of our marks by small boys; false courses laid; flags destroyed and stolen; really frantic last second re-markings. Yes there always problems but don't let's dwell on them too much. Who knows, some of our members other than the odd dozen who have helped this year may next year come along too and we may at length even be able to persuade some of our older runners that it is not asking too much to expect them to take their very serious and important training run round the marks rather than in Richmond Park. But I doubt it. Yours etc. Arthur Whitehead. items.h: THREE NATIONAL TITLES IN ONE YEAR !
items.sum: Editorial celebrating the walkers winning all three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year and members' county championship successes on the track.
items.s: THREE NATIONAL TITLES IN ONE YEAR ! Editorial celebrating the walkers winning all three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year and members' county championship successes on the track. By the magnificent victory of our walkers in the R.W.A. 50 kilometres event at Preston we become the first club ever to have held the three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year - a brilliant achievement! This latest win was accomplished, be it noted, without the assistance of Eric Hall, who was forced to retire from the race owing to the extreme heat. We extend our sympathies to Eric, who, with more favourable weather conditions might easily have completed a superlative double, as he had already won the 20 mile title. Congratulations to those members who showed the Belgrave colours to such fine effect in gaining win and place medals in the track championships of FIVE counties, a remarkable feat! Most notable were the brilliant doubles of Brian Morris (Sussex 220 & 440 yds.), Ivan Mayers (Middlesex 100 & 220 yds.) and Clive Ryan (Surrey Junior 100 & 220 yds.). Another noteworthy performance was that of B. Morris and G. Leroy in finishing 1st and 2nd in the Kinnaird 440 yds. final, both inside 50 sec. Morris followed this up a week later when finishing a very close second in the Southern 440 with a time of 48.6 sec. In view of these splendid efforts our chances of annexing the forthcoming A.A.A. 4 x 440 yds. relay are very bright indeed. It now seems that we have first class performers in almost all the events in which a club of our standing participates, and the days when we lost matches due to our inability to put competitors in certain events are gone. A particular instance springs to mind here, when, a few years back we won almost every track event against L.A.C. and still lost the match. Thanks to Jack Chappell, Bill Merryman and Charlie Jones, the result of such a match now would be quite different.
