items.label: No. 133
items.h: LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY (SOUTHERN CLUBS) OCT.12TH.
items.sum: Stage-by-stage report by "Olympian" of Belgrave's recovery from 18th after the first leg to second place in the London to Brighton relay for southern clubs, won by Thames Valley Harriers.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY (SOUTHERN CLUBS) OCT.12TH. Stage-by-stage report by "Olympian" of Belgrave's recovery from 18th after the first leg to second place in the London to Brighton relay for southern clubs, won by Thames Valley Harriers. Once again we were blessed with the best of weather and no matter what the result our supporters were all set for a good day out. For those who have never followed this race I can fully commend it as the best and most enjoyable in the athletic calendar, both from the competitors and spectators points of view. The changing fortunes of the teams provide a great spirit of friendly rivalry and the quality of the racing gives a piquant spice to a day of many thrills. Those in the know forecast a Thames Valley victory and for once their prognostications proved correct. It would have taken an "Old Moore" to have placed the other teams in the right order. Belgrave were generally considered as being a club with a chance of making the first six with Polytechnic, Woodford Green, Herne Hill, Essex Beagles and St.Albans as the main rivals. Little did we realise the early misfortune that was to befall us and the valiant fight that the rest of the team was to make to recover our prestige. Don MacLean had been given the first leg to Wandsworth Common and the first stroke of ten o'clock sent him on his way with nineteen other runners. At first, all was well, but by the time Chelsea Bridge was reached it was obvious that it was not Don's day and as we have seen so often in the past he fell back and back and our early hopes fell and fell until by the end of the stage we were in eighteenth place and over 1½ mins. behind the leading club (Aylesford P.M.). This was disaster, and a gap which would need a lot of closing. Charlie Walker, however, was spurred on by the responsibility thrown on his shoulders and set out to recover some of the lost ground. By excellent running he passed team after team and the encouraging cheers of the few supporters on this leg kept him at his task. At Mitcham we were up to 9th place but still 1½ mins. behind Poly. who had taken over the lead through a great run by John Evans. Charlie was the second fastest of the day. George Flanagan, one of our youngest team members, had the difficult leg from Mitcham to Purley. His steady start was a wise move, and with the help of Llewellyn of Walton, who caught him after a mile, he made good progress on the field ahead, and by Purley had reduced the overall lead to 69 sec. and had gained a further place - an invaluable effort. Charlie Dabbs took the fourth stage but was obviously not at his best and we were disappointed to see our much improved position slipping away again. Charlie fought hard to keep his place but at Merstham we were back again to 9th and 2¼ min. behind Thames Valley who had gone into what proved to be a winning lead. Jim Masters on the switchback course through Redhill and Earlswood again gave us hope by passing three clubs and taking us up to 6th. Thames Valley, however, were represented by Norris and added 10 more seconds to their lead. Jim produced the second best time and closed up the gap on the intervening clubs - an excellent effort. The next leg was a new one of little more than two miles in length and John Davies, complete with an arm in plaster following a fracture, was entrusted with it. This was John's first experience of this type of racing and he later suffered from an over zealous start which diminished his finishing power. He was forced back to 8th by Portsmouth and Shaftsbury and at this point we were 2¾ min. behind Thames Valley, who were 500 yds. ahead of the second club, Woodford. This run should prove very valuable to John and we shall expect some first class performances from him in future races. Peter Hitchcock had the joy of running over the newly laid stretch of road round Gatwick Airport and although losing ground on the leading clubs he managed to pull us back to 7th with a steady performance which should add to his experience for next year. We were now well over half way to Brighton and no less than 3 min. 10 sec. behind - a poor prospect and we were wondering whether even a place in the first six was to be gained. Pat Newell, taking over Jack Brown's cloak, proved a worthy successor on the hard grind from Crawley to Handcross, and in gaining two places brought us within sight of all but T.V.H. who had widened their lead,through a grand run by Bert Ingles, to 2½ minutes over the second club, Woodford. Pat, despite an unplanned trip under the subway at Crawley level-crossing, which loses at least ten seconds, was credited with the third best time of the day. Eric Gebbett's turn came next on the long undulating leg from Handcross to "The Castle" at Hickstead. This leg is generally reserved for the best runners of each club, and our difficulty, in recent years, has been to find someone of sufficient calibre to keep on equal terms with other teams. Eric gave of his best and ran a good race, but unfortunately he lost a considerable amount of ground on the leaders, and our sixth position, with only three legs to go, was far from favourable with T.V.H. over five minutes ahead and other clubs well away. Len Bishop, on the tenth stage, thought we still had a chance, and with a run which gave him the fastest time of the day, picked up one place which brought us up to fifth, only 12 seconds behind the third and fourth teams. T.V.H., by this time, were in an invincible position with over three minutes to spare on Woodford, who were still holding on to second place. Dave Baulch, again selected to run up Dale Hill, joined in the spirit of the chase and soon moved up to third place and was gaining fast on Woodford, who had by this time run all their best men and were beginning to flag badly. Dave ran to such purpose that he achieved the best time of the day and brought us to within nine seconds of Woodford - a magnificent performance. Our supporters were wild with excitement and were giving our runners every encouragement possible - never have stop-watches worked so hard in taking time checks. Brian Hallowell set about the last leg in a very workmanlike manner, much to the consternation of the Woodford runner only a short distance ahead - never have I seen anyone look so worried. Across Preston Park in similar manner as in April last, Brian took over second place and went clean away from the Woodford man and reached the Aquarium 36 seconds ahead. He also had the distinction of recording the fastest time of the day. It is doubtful if any team, after such a bad start, has ever recovered in so grand a manner to take one of the major awards and keep the Belgrave flag flying so high. Our record in these races is second to none, and the prospects of even greater improvement are considerable, with a batch of first class material available for selection next April coupled with the solid and experienced strength of our seasoned performers. items.sum: Report and result of the Smiths of England 12½ mile road race at Witney, won as a team by Belgrave, with Eric Gebbett third.
items.s: SMITHS OF ENGLAND 12½ MILE ROAD RACE. NOV.2ND AT WITNEY Report and result of the Smiths of England 12½ mile road race at Witney, won as a team by Belgrave, with Eric Gebbett third. Thanks to the efforts of Jack Goswell, a pleasant trip by coach was organised to transport the walkers to Oxford, for their match against the University, and the runners to Witney for the above mentioned race. Our story concerns the latter event, where we were welcomed by Derek Burfitt and Verne Blowfield, two well known ex-members. They had prepared the race with great attention to detail; the result could not be faulted. Excellent showers, good road surfaces, FREE EATS and first rate prizes ensured that our hungry brigade will make every effort to compete next year. For the record book, Eric Gebbett excelled over the distance and the extra two miles enabled him to move away from Chas. Walker and finish third to Haslam of T.V.H. and Thornton of Leeds. Chas. ran well to finish fifth with Len Bishop pipping his brother Eric for third scoring place. items.s: SOUTH OF THE THAMES "JUNIOR" REIGATE PRIORY. NOV.9TH Report and Belgrave results from the South of the Thames junior cross-country at Reigate Priory, where George Flanagan was second. We fielded four teams with a total of twenty-seven runners over a well laid out and sporting course in good conditions. George Flanagan was soon prominent and ran an extremely good race throughout to come through from fifth at the halfway stage to second, only eleven seconds behind the winner Bill Bird of Ranelagh who is a second claim Belgrave member. Our other runners were too far back to secure a place in the team race and they finished 7 th with 130 pts. Robin Weate, in his first big race for us, shewed that he will be a very useful asset by finishing 28th. Charlie Dabbs was disappointing in 44th position but has been unfit and was short of training. Don Stroud ran well to finish 56th and others who performed satisfactorily were S.Boreham,C.Shippen, J.Dooley and M.Robinson. Don McLean came all the way from Oxford by motor-cycle to finish 324th - perhaps the cold got into his bones, or is there some other reason for these continuous lapses from his real form? items.h: MATCH v. HERNE HILL AT ADDINGTON NOV.16TH
items.sum: Report of the cross-country match against Herne Hill at Addington, lost in senior and junior races but won by the youths.
items.s: MATCH v. HERNE HILL AT ADDINGTON NOV.16TH Report of the cross-country match against Herne Hill at Addington, lost in senior and junior races but won by the youths. Probably due to our Club Dinner being on the same evening we could muster only eleven seniors, four juniors and five youths for this fixture but a good run was had by all. In the senior event we were short of our best performers but it was good to see Archie Bedford once more in our midst and even more refreshing to see him running well enough to be our first man home in fourth place. The juniors ran in the same race and Charlie Dabbs and Robin Weate followed Archie round, closely pursued by Eddie Short and Clive Shippen. The brothers Bishop (Alan and Eric) indulged in some good pack running with Jim Heathfield and Bob Glover in attendance. The final reckoning gave Herne Hill a win by 95 pts. to 115 in the senior and 18 to 20 in the junior. In the youths race which had been run earlier young Thresher showed delightful form to win by 15 sec. with Trevor Hart in third place. This good start enabled us to win the team race by the narrow margin of one point - 27 to 28. items.s: BELGRAVE OPEN 7 MILES WALK. NOV.23RD. Report and Belgrave results of the 38th annual Belgrave Open 7 miles walk, a record field of 230, in which Belgrave won the team race with S. Vickers second and E. Hall third. The 38th annual Open Walk, which is the oldest and, we feel, the most popular 7 in the calendar, took place in perfect weather and attracted a record field of 230 starters. With Eric Hall in such fine form and Stan Vickers out for the first time since August and the rest of our team walking well, we were very hopeful of retaining our team title. Right from the start Eric and Stan, in company with K.Matthews of Royal Sutton Coldfield, took the field along at a record-breaking pace, with the result that the first five finishers beat the old course record. Our thanks are due to the Prize Fund Donors without whose generosity we could not maintain our fine display of prizes, also to Arthur Whitehead who, by placing his premises at our disposal, did much to relieve congestion at the hall. items.sum: Report and Belgrave results of the four-club cross-country match at Ruislip, won by Belgrave with Charlie Walker second to Hugh Foord.
items.s: MATCH v. FINCHLEY H., BRIGHTON A.C. AND St.ALBANS CITY A.C.NOV.30TH. at Ruislip Report and Belgrave results of the four-club cross-country match at Ruislip, won by Belgrave with Charlie Walker second to Hugh Foord. Only ten stalwarts attended this away fixture which was most disappointing and does not encourage the arranging of such matches which are provided to give the opportunity of racing over different types of country to that experienced at our own headquarters. Conditions were first class, and a field of about forty faced the starter. Charlie Walker was soon in the first bunch which was headed by Hugh Foord of Brighton and when seen again at the end of the first lap had established himself in second place some distance behimd Foord. Len Orton, our second claim member from Birchfield, was prominent and Robin Weate was also well placed. Eric Gebbett seemed to be taking an easy start but at the next appearance had worked his way through the field. Robin had dropped a little and Orton seemed far from happy. On the last lap Gebbett had made further progress and Orton had recovered from a bad patch. Fred Paget surprised us by apparently gaining twelve places on the last lap but was later adjudged to have cut about one mile off the course by unwittingly following a rival Polytechnic v. Ilford race which coincided with our course for some distance. We eventually took the team honours with 96 pts. for eight scoring men. Brighton were second with 103 and Finchley third with 169. St.Albans could only field four men and won a straight match with Finchley by 16 pts. to 20. items.s: CLUB 7 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP DEC.7TH Report and results of the club 7 miles cross-country championship, won by Eric Gebbett in 36m.47s from Robin Weate, with handicap result. In the absence of Charlie Walker and George Flanagan, the result of this race was very much a matter for speculation. A field of 37 started, including three Essex Beagles men, and a bunch of about twelve runners was soon detached on the first lap, with Eric Gebbett in close attendance. With about two miles to go, J.Masters, who had been forcing the pace for most of the race, fell back rapidly, and was quickly passed by Gebbett, R.Weate and L.Bishop. Once he was in front, a position which always seems to bring out the best in him, Eric quickly established a considerable lead. This he maintained to the end of the race and finished with the highly creditable time of 36m.47s. Our up and coming member Weate, ran extremely well to gain his first place in a Club championship, filling second place, 20 sec. in front of Len Bishop. Good performances came from Steve Charlton, J.Moore and Alan Bishop, whilst new-comer R.Bhatia from Ceylon, astounded most of us by running well to the front and finishing in 8th position. 1 E.Gebbett 36.47 2 R.Weate 37.32 3 L.C.Bishop 37.52 4 J.Moore 38.04 5 E.Short 38.37 6 H.A.Bishop 38.45 7 S.Charlton 38.52 8 R.Bhatia 38.53 9 C.Shippen 39.02 10 J.Masters 39.11 11 J.Heathfield 39.15 12 G.Stevens 39.33 13 J.Edgar 39.56 14 J.Radford 40.11 15 E.M.Bishop 40.14 16 F.Paget 40.15 17 D.Manning 40.27 18 R.Mitchell 40.31 19 R.Glover 40.32 20 D.W.Jones 40.[illegible]0 [?] 21 L.Adams 40.45 22 R.Braine 41.04 23 J.Davies 42.02 24 D.Abbott 42.11 25 C.Dabbs 42.47 26 W.Cousens 42.52 27 G.Davidson 42.57 28 E.S.Stimpson 43.15 29 R.Conway 43.42 30 G.Musselbrook 44.16 31 T.Upperdine 44.16 32 P.Bellenger 46.20 33 J.Baker 46.37 34 R.Hilton 46.48 1st H.A.Bishop (4.15) 34.30 2nd R.Braine (6.30) 34.34 3rd J.Radford (5.15) 34.56 Charlie Walker Charlie Walker absent George Flanagan George Flanagan absent Eric Gebbett Eric Gebbett J. items.sum: Report of the club's 70th anniversary dinner and dance at Barrington House, with presentations to Tom Carter and Stan Vickers.
items.s: CLUB DINNER AND DANCE Report of the club's 70th anniversary dinner and dance at Barrington House, with presentations to Tom Carter and Stan Vickers. Our 70th Anniversary Dinner and Dance, held on 16th November, was undoubtedly a huge success. Due to the hard work of our Social Hon. Secretary, Tom Carter, the function was well supported and the choice of venue, Barrington House, Gresham Street, was a great improvement on last year. Amongst the 230 members and friends who sat down to dinner it was pleasing to see a good number of our younger members. We were pleased to have with us representatives from the governing bodies of Amateur Athletics and after the customary speeches, the President, Syd Roberts, concluded the first half of the evening by presenting a Past President's Plaque to Tom Carter. In the absence of Tommy Green, owing to illness, he also presented the Tommy Green Trophy for the best Club performance to Stan Vickers for his 6th place in the Olympic 20,000 metres walk Dinner was followed by dancing until 11.30p.m. with Bill Lucas, who had earlier carried out the duties of Toastmaster, acting as M.C. items.sum: Field events column reviewing the 1957 season, congratulating Dave Ansell on Maccabia Games selection, welcoming Deszö Audorka and announcing early-season meetings.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP Field events column reviewing the 1957 season, congratulating Dave Ansell on Maccabia Games selection, welcoming Deszö Audorka and announcing early-season meetings. There were no field events notes in the issue of the "Belgravian' just after the track season ended owing to holidays. Normally that contains a review of the season's performances and although a little late we should not forget Percy Porter's fine performances in the hammer, including a 3rd place in the A.A.A. championships and selection as an International reserve.John Powell Jones won the Welsh Shot championship and Charlie (C.R.) Jones put up two fine performances in getting 4th in both Southern and A.A.A. 220 yards hurdles. We had successes in a number of County championships but "Iron Man" Mal Ash had a slightly disappointing season. Those,and one or two others, have a chance of selection for the Empire Games, so we hope they will get down to serious training early, as the team will be chosen immediately after the Southern Championships in June. Congratulations to Dave Ansell, our Captain, on his selection for the British team at the Maccabia Games in Tel-a-Viv. He was 7th in the long jump, 6th in the triple jump and gained a medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay. We should like to extend a special welcome to Deszö Audorka, a very fine International discus thrower from Hungary, and we hope he will be able to show us some of his home form. It was nice to see Malcolm Draper over Christmas. He tells me he has now left hospital and is convalescing - hopes to be home in about two months but unfortunately no athletics for a couple of years. I have already mentioned getting into training early and to help in this Thames Valley Harriers and "The Bels" are putting on meetings on the 8th February and 1st of March respectively for some pre-season competition. The Sward Trophy will be round again on the 10th of May at Chiswick when we hope to turn out our best team to win back the trophy we so narrowly lost last year. The usual Club championships and some handicaps will also be held in the Summer. Details of the Thames Valley meeting can be supplied if anyone is interested. Our own meeting will be held on Saturday 1st March, at Battersea Park, commencing at 1.30 p.m. Events :- Shot Discus Javelin High Jump Long Jump Triple Jump Pole Vault Entries (free) on A.A.A. forms to me not later than 17th Feb. I hope all "Bels" will support our efforts in this meeting. Best wishes to all for the New Year. T.C. Jones. Field Events Honorary Secretary. T.C. Jones T.C. items.sum: Profile of Joseph "Mac" MacDonald, who joined Belgrave in 1938, covering his cross-country, road and London to Brighton record.
items.s: PORTRAIT GALLERY Profile of Joseph "Mac" MacDonald, who joined Belgrave in 1938, covering his cross-country, road and London to Brighton record. Every club has its characters, Belgrave Harriers being no exception. But we don't propose to cover our canvas with the outline of one of those characters whose performances and history are an open book. In 1938, there joined Belgrave, one whom we can only assume was as small, lean and sinewy in those days as he is now. Known to us all as "Mac", Joseph MacDonald has had a dareer as distinguished as many who have been fortunate to be called stars. Under the stern leadership of Footer, Carter and Penny in the immediate post-war years, Mac soon showed he was possessed of great endurance and performed well over the road and country. In 1948 he was in the 3rd team in the Middlesex C.C. championship, 10th in the Kent '20', 3rd team in the Chichester to Portsmouth 16 and 45th in the South of the Thames Junior C.C. race (noted for its large fields). Even better in 1949, he was in our winning South of the Thames Senior team, 59th in the Southern Counties C.C. championship and 5th in the Worthing 5 miles road race. Mac was now established as a road runner and between 1951 and 1953 won the Club Marathon Championship and was placed 2nd and 3rd. But his greatest feats have been in the London to Brighton 52½ miles race where, when twice in dire straits with still a considerable distance to be covered, he has forced himself on in order not to let his team down. Altogether he has been in one third, one second and one winning team in this race in 1952, 1955 and 1956 respectively. His attendance at road and cross-country events and at training sessions has been an example to all. Week after week at the Duke of York's at Sloane Square, he would come tearing in at the last moment on his bicycle (he wasn't such a plutocrat in those days) and oblivious to the abuse hurled at him by those ready to leave, would hastily don his gear and with feet pattering loud enough to disturb half Sloane Square, would join the pack. Good-hearted and generous, it was often barley sugars all round when sweets were rationed; Mac it seemed had relations who didn't indulge. He has been with us years and will still be performing well for many to come. Our London to Brighton team can always rely on him. A true Belgravian, whose performances have so often gone unseen except by the few on the long lonely roads; we are proud to put them on record. items.sum: Letter from the new Track Secretary, D.M. Shepherd, asking members to answer fixture postcards and support the club championships on 14th June.
items.s: FROM THE TRACK SECRETARY Letter from the new Track Secretary, D.M. Shepherd, asking members to answer fixture postcards and support the club championships on 14th June. For the first time I have taken on the task of Track Secretary and I am looking forward to a very successful year for all those members of the Club who are interested in track running We have a very full programme before us, and it should give all of you plenty of racing. Arranging this programme has occasioned us a great deal of hard work, so you will be expected to co-operate by replying immediately to all postcards that may be sent to you, stating whether or not you can take part in a particular fixture. By so doing you will be making our task much easier. Try to make the coming track season a success by doing your best to turn out for the Club, and by remembering that you are part of a team and not just an individual. If I, Bob Taylor, Clive Shippen or Jim Heathfield can help in any way do not hesitate to write to us or see us personally, and we will do our best for you. If you do not help me and the job falls down, through lack of co-operation it will be no good crying about it. Note especially the date of the Club championships. They will be held on Saturday 14th of June in the evening, and will start at approximately 6.00 p.m. We want to make a special effort this year to have a really first class meeting, and once again it will be up to the competitors, that is yourselves, to SUPPORT these championships. I, on my part, will make sure that the track is there, that the officials are there and that the cups and trophies are also there. Make it a real day and bring the family. Yours sincerely. D.M. Shepherd. D.M. Shepherd D.M. Shepherd. Track Secretary Bob Taylor Bob Taylor Clive Shippen Clive Shippen Jim Heathfield Jim Heathfield Club Championships

items.sum: Road running notes by H.A. Bishop urging training and entries for the 1958 long-distance season, with a list of the main events.
items.s: ROAD RUNNING NOTES. Road running notes by H.A. Bishop urging training and entries for the 1958 long-distance season, with a list of the main events. With the long distance road running season barely two months away it is to be hoped that all distance runners are now getting down to serious training. There are numerous events, ranging from 10 to 53 miles, so that all tastes can be catered for. I would particularly like to see a very strong Belgrave entry in each of the two main events, namely the Polytechnic marathon and our own Open 20 miles race, both of which carry a Club championship in conjunction. Scarcely less important is the Finchley 20, which this year incorporates the Southern 20 miles championship. This race presents a good opportunity to secure a Southern standard, as the course is easy and the modest time of 2 hrs. 5 min. should be within everybody's capabilities. There is, of course, no A.A.A. standard for this distance. Southern marathon standard ( 2 hrs.50 mins.) is a trifle more difficult, but on the flat Windsor to Chiswick route it shouldn't present too much trouble provided weather conditions are reasonable. The A.A.A. standard of 2 hrs.35 mins. is a tough proposition on any course. In many distance events, the promotors stipulate that team runners must make individual entries, and I would suggest that this be done in all cases to avoid any possibility of being left out of a team. If you are not one of the recognised distance men and feel that you would like to take part in a certain race or races just drop me a line and I will include you in the team, assuming, of course, that we have a team going to that particular event. Wishing you all a successful season with not too many blisters. H.A. Bishop, 13, Woodside Way, Long Lane, Croydon, Surrey Below is a list of the main long distance events for 1958. items.sum: Editorial on the start of the track and road season, the Battersea Park field events meeting, Fred Stone's police bravery award, a disappointing flu-hit cross country season and the success of the walkers under Jack Goswell.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial on the start of the track and road season, the Battersea Park field events meeting, Fred Stone's police bravery award, a disappointing flu-hit cross country season and the success of the walkers under Jack Goswell. Dear Fellow Members, By the time this edition is published, the track and road season will be with us and it is to be hoped that the Winter has not been spent in idleness by those wishing to do well in these spheres. Our field events men are already hard at it as witness our successful open meeting at Battersea Park on March 2nd. This event does great credit to its organisers and it is a valuable contribution, giving performers competition during the close season. Our old friend, P.C. Fred Stone, was seen by many on a television programme recently when receiving an award in recognition of his bravery during police service. Harry Evans, as sprightly as ever, also appeared on the programme to recount some tales of their younger days. We needn't be too disappointed with the cross country season, for like so many other clubs we were victims of a flu-ridden Winter. It cannot be too strongly emphasized, however, that a season over the country demands both sufficient groundwork and sensible racing. So many seem to forget that the real tests come after Christmas; to feel race-weary when the new year begins is fatal. Likewise it is equally fatal to expect to commence one's season in January with the Southern and National in mind. Under such circumstances it is not possible to produce top performances in both events. Our walkers continue winning in merciless fashion and we must not lose sight of that great driving force behind them, Jack Goswell. He must be the Stampfl of the walking world in his ability to bring out the best in his men. To Eric Hall and Stan Vickers, who have never walked better we offer our congratulations. It may sound fantastic but Eric, now one of our "greats" won a 2 mile walk handicap in 1950, off 650 yards! So go to it, you novices. Fred Stone P.C. items.sum: Report of a four-club cross country match at Banstead won narrowly by Belgrave, led home by John Davies in 8th.
items.s: MATCH v. MITCHAM, MET. POLICE AND GUILDFORD & GODALMING A.C. at BANSTEAD. DEC.28TH Report of a four-club cross country match at Banstead won narrowly by Belgrave, led home by John Davies in 8th. Out of our terrific numerical strength of cross country runners we could only muster thirteen, including three juniors, for this away fixture. The venue is set in the midst of Surrey's grand scenery and provides a complete change to the normal terrain over which we run. I have little doubt that all who took part had an enjoyable afternoon. John Davies, who has been a regular participant in cross country fixtures this year, led home the Belgrave contingent in 8th place, closely followed by a pack of Belgravians in 10th, 11th, 12th, 14th, 15th, 17th and 18th positions. This good bunching enabled us to secure a narrow win in the team race, with Mitcham second, Met. Police third and Guildford fourth. Ken Jones was performing for the Police and ran well to finish fourth in the individual placings. Bob Glover, a strong runner, deserves special mention - he is continually improving and without doubt will greatly assist our teams before many seasons are over - stick to it Bob! 1st Belgrave (8,10,11,12,14,15) 70 pts 2nd Mitcham (1,2,5,19,21,24) 72 " 3rd Met.Police (4,6,9,13,20,28) 80 " 4th Guildford & Godalming (3,7,16,22,23,25) 96 " John Davies John Davies led home the Belgrave contingent in 8th place Ken Jones Ken Jones 4th Bob Glover Bob Glover singled out as a strong, improving runner Banstead Surrey Mitcham Met. items.sum: Report of the Surrey county cross country championship at Reigate, where Belgrave finished fourth behind Herne Hill, South London and Walton, with D. Baulch the first Belgrave man in 11th.
items.s: SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP AT REIGATE. JAN.4TH Report of the Surrey county cross country championship at Reigate, where Belgrave finished fourth behind Herne Hill, South London and Walton, with D. Baulch the first Belgrave man in 11th. This race was held at the same venue as the South of the Thames Junior in November and the course consisted of a mixture of grassland, firm paths and hills, some of which were very steep.It could well be described as a good sporty course.The finishing time indicated a distance well in excess of the scheduled seven miles which produced some grumblings from the competitors, especially those whose training had previously been of a sketchy nature. It would seem that we are doomed to take team positions outside the first three in this race for some years to come unless we can split the strength of South London and Herne Hill and the recent rise to power of Walton A.C. Indeed, we have not won this event since 1952 nor been placed since 1955. Only Baulch and Gebbett ran true to form and finished in positions which deserve any special mention. Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another. Dave was indeed unlucky to miss his selection for the County team but should fare better next year. Eric Gebbett eventually finished 20th after having been up to 15th at one stage - it seems strange to have to report that the extra distance was his downfall.Charlie Walker in 33rd place was very disappointing - perhaps he should not forecast his running before the race - it always seems to be fatal. Len Bishop and Eddie Short should have been at least ten places higher than their 42nd and 43rd, and Peter Hitchcock should also have been better positioned than 52nd. It is obvious that we have the talent but it is not put to the best use when major races are run. Instead of rising to the occasion we fall further and further from grace. Do we do enough training to keep up with modern conditions? 1st Herne Hill H. (4,5,6,8,12,16) 51 pts. 2nd South London H. (1,7,22,23,27,29) 109 " 3rd Walton A.C. ORPINGTON A.C., ISLE OF SHEPPEY AND OLD CROYDONIANS AT ORPINGTON JAN.11TH Report of a poorly supported cross country match at Orpington in which Belgrave, with only four runners, finished second to Orpington. The Cross Country Secretary sent out numerous cards directing runners to this fixture but the nett result was a turnout of four which was extremely disappointing and an insult to our hosts. The race took place over good grassland over a distance of five miles and Robin Weate and J.Dooley ran together to finish second and third. Gerry Lines made one of his rare appearances and showed welcome form to finish 9th. Musselbrook rose to the occasion in answering the card sent to him by appearing in person to complete our team in 17th position. Orpington took the team honours with 22 pts., Bels..were second with 31, Sheppey scored 44 and Old Croydonians amassed 75. On the whole an enjoyable afternoon out for the few stalwarts who supported this fixture. It should of course be mentioned that we had another away race against Westminster Bank on this day which split our forces but nevertheless there were many of our members who stayed away from both. Nic Milsum walked very well to win the race in 28.56 and Bryan Cornish was 8th in 31.18. The same day (Jan.4th) E.A.Smith finished third in the London Business Houses 7 mile championship in 55.52. We also had a match versus Met.Police at "The Warren" Hayes and in a field of eighteen Stan Vickers was first home in 56.05. R.D.McMullen was second and R.C.Hall third. Scoring eight a side we won with 43½ pts. to 93½. On Jan 11th at Imber Court the Metropolitan Police held their open 7 mile walk and in a field of 195 Stan Vickers led for the whole way to win in the record time of 50.14 which was 78 secs. faster than the previous best. With Eric Hall 4th, R.D.McMullen 16th and George Checkley 19th we easily won the team race from Met.W.C. and Highgate. It was very pleasing to see the large number of Club supporters stationed around the course - their presence was well rewarded. items.s: MITCHAM 15 MILES ROAD RACE. JAN.11TH. Report of the Mitcham 15 miles road race, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 7th of 23 and ex-junior member Geoff Goode was 9th for Welwyn. With Jack Brown in Cyprus and Colin Collis (temporarily we hope) retired it was to be expected that we would not retain our team title. Our chances were even further reduced when Eric Gebbett retired at nine miles after unwisely trying to stay with the leaders who were moving at a very hot pace. We eventually finished 7th out of 23 teams. It is of interest that an ex-junior member of the Club, Geoff Goode, now running for Welwyn, finished 9th in the fast time of 84.37. items.sum: Report and result of the club 10 miles cross country championship for the Macher Shield, won by Charlie Walker, with Bob Plummer taking the handicap.
items.s: CLUB 10 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP (MACHER SHIELD) JAN.25TH Report and result of the club 10 miles cross country championship for the Macher Shield, won by Charlie Walker, with Bob Plummer taking the handicap. This year's race,held on a cold damp day, ran true to form with Charlie Walker, who always performs so well over our own courses, the winner by the comfortable margin of 47 seconds. Dave Baulch took second place, 53 seconds ahead of Eric Gebbett who had earlier in the season won the seven miles championship. This was the order which had been maintained almost throughout the race and the fact that, for the second year, the course was inadvertently shortened by missing out the lap of the starting field in the middle of the race, obviously made no difference to the result. The back markers in the handicap could well complain, for if the full distance had been covered there is little doubt that Walker and Moore would have been among the prizes. John Moore (the second), in his first season with us, has made his mark upon us and will soon be taking a leading place in our races and should bolster up our teams both on track and country. His fourth place in this event was well earned, for he has been a keen performer since he joined us. Archie Bedford returned for one of his rare visits and, by finishing fifth, proved he still has the capacity to gain a place in our first teams. Eddie Short ran well to take sixth place and that "little potterer" Joe Dooley followed close on his heels with Jim Heathfield, only a few yards behind. Bob Plummer, better known for his exploits over the marathon distance, took advantage of the handicapper's generosity to win the handicap by a good margin. items.sum: Report and result of the South of the Thames senior cross country championship held from Belgrave Hall, won by Blackheath Harriers, with Belgrave 9th and George Flanagan 13th.
items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP FEB.1ST Report and result of the South of the Thames senior cross country championship held from Belgrave Hall, won by Blackheath Harriers, with Belgrave 9th and George Flanagan 13th. This race was held from Belgrave Hall in honour of Les Cohen who this year is President of the South of the Thames Cross Country Association. He must have been proud of the efficient manner in which this event was organised and our thanks go out to Arthur Whitehead who took all the responsibility for course marking and the provision of starting and finishing pens upon his experienced shoulders. The number of barring clauses in this event precluded the fielding of our strongest team, but on paper our lads, with a mixture of experience and youthful exuberance, appeared to have a chance of a place. Unfortunately we were again to be disappointed as we could finish no better than 9th in the team race with the mammoth score of 461 pts. George Flanagan was the only one of our runners who excelled himself and he should be pleased with thirteenth position. John Moore, by finishing 52nd, gained good experience in a large field and Robin Weate, in his first year with us, showed that he is possessed of more than his fair share of pluck to finish 88th. Robin, still a junior, always gives of his best and is a great asset to us - with regular and correct training he should follow in the footsteps of that courageous little man, Bert Footer, who did so much for Belgrave in the years preceding the last war. Bob Glover, also in his first season, improves with every outing and in finishing 111th can be said to have performed well and should benefit from this experience. Ken Jones, running in the colours of the Metropolitan Police A.C. ran very well to take 33rd place and will be a tower of strength in these races when we have his services. items.h: SOUTHERN COUNTIES SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP at Parliament Hill Feb.15th
items.sum: Report and result of the Southern Counties senior cross country championship at Parliament Hill, won by South London Harriers, with Belgrave a disappointing 9th, plus notes on the Southern youths and junior races where George Flanagan was 5th.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP at Parliament Hill Feb.15th Report and result of the Southern Counties senior cross country championship at Parliament Hill, won by South London Harriers, with Belgrave a disappointing 9th, plus notes on the Southern youths and junior races where George Flanagan was 5th. A return to the course over which the National was held last year saw one of the biggest fields ever set off on the long trek of nine miles over hilly grassland with a fair proportion of mud and slush. Toward the end of the first of the three laps Eric Gebbett was our first scorer way back in 49th place followed closely by Charlie Walker 55th. Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's. Pete Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Len Bishop were next, in the 170's while the rest of our men were back in the 200's. The next view of the field was soon after the first lap had ended, and Walker had moved up to Gebbett and Short and Moore had also progressed about fifteen places and were running well. Masters was making very heavy weather of it and was slipping back steadily, Hitchcock and Shippen were 152nd and 167th respectively with Len Bishop and D.Baulch in close attendance. At the conclusion of the second lap Walker had left Gebbett and was now 44th but was having great difficulty in making any further progress. Although Gebbett was slipping back gradually, Short and Moore were still making up ground and were now 103rd and 104th. Our other men however, were making little or no improvement with the exception of J.Dooley who had started very slowly and was now beginning his late excursion through the field. On the last lap Moore made up another ten places and Hitchcock put in a good run to move up nearly thirty places. Dooley seemed to enjoy himself at this stage and must have passed about fifty runners in the last three miles. The others seemed to have got themselves well bogged down. The final count gave us ninth place with the astronomical score of 591 points, which must have been our lowest place and highest score for a good many years. The impression one gets from this fiasco is that most if not all of our runners are short of the type of training needed to keep pace with the leading performers. On examining the final positions one cannot fail to notice how many athletes, possessed of far less ability than our lads, finished well up the field and assisted their clubs to secure good places - the moral is obvious. Result :- Individuals :- Also held at Parliament Hill on the same day were the Southern Youths and Junior championships. Our juniors ran very well to finish fourth in the team race. An outstanding performance was that of George Flanagan in being placed fifth, a performance which qualifies him for a Junior Honours Badge. Another good run was that of Robin Weate who was 21st. In the youths race Belgrave were 10th.The only other news we have is that C.Thompson was 26th and J.Thresher 48th. 1st South London Harriers 136 pts. 2nd Thames Valley Harriers 142 " 3rd Woodford Green A.C. 206 " 9th Belgrave Harriers 591 " 47 C.W. A feat probably never equalled by any other club was that of ten Belgrave walkers gaining their county colours. Surrey at Walton-on-Thames. items.h: MATCH v. FINCHLEY H. & ORPINGTON A.C. FEB.22ND at Wimbledon
items.sum: Report of a 7½ mile cross-country match at Wimbledon which Belgrave won with 46 points despite moved marking flags sending Clive Shippen off course.
items.s: MATCH v. FINCHLEY H. & ORPINGTON A.C. FEB.22ND at Wimbledon Report of a 7½ mile cross-country match at Wimbledon which Belgrave won with 46 points despite moved marking flags sending Clive Shippen off course. About forty runners faced the starter for a race of 7½ miles in which there was a great preponderance of Belgrave Harriers including a number of old stalwarts. At the end of the first lap Clive Shippen was leading with Moore and Short well in attendance. A quick check showed that we were well in the lead and should have no difficulty in holding our position. Unfortunately a number of small boys on the Common thought otherwise and on the second lap the marking flags were found to have been moved with the result that Clive Shippen went well off course and was left with too much ground to make up to regain his early lead. John Moore and Eddie Short soon discovered their mistake and all was well once more but the whole character of the race had been changed. Nevertheless we gained a comfortable win, scoring seven a side, with 46 points against 82 by Finchley and 103 by Orpington. items.s: GOSPORT OPEN SEVEN MILES WALK.MARCH 1ST Report of the Gosport Open Seven Miles Walk, won by Eric Hall by 14 seconds with Belgrave taking the team award, followed by an account of a Sunday stroll from Croydon the next morning. We sent a small team down for this new venture, and after a rough sea crossing we were not quite so sure we should have bothered. After being "Security Cleared" we changed in a barracks, no autograph hunters were allowed just in case we looked like volunteers. The course itself was flat and Stan Vickers soon showed the way, followed by a large of local lads. Soon the pace began to tell and at two miles Eric Hall had moved through and was breathing very heavily down Stan's neck with Norman Read just behind. Nick Milsum had a bad time, but fought back well to regain lost ground near the finish. At four miles Eric moved away and Stan fell back to third, but not for long however, as over the last mile he closed right up again and Eric just got home by 14 seconds. Ray Hall had a great fight all the way and used bluff to finish 8th. Terry Clark was always handy and he was followed by Joe Coleman who took first veteran's prize. Nick Milsum was third in the handicap and of course we won the team award - a very successful pot hunt. Harry Shields made his mark by leading others astray on the pretext of having tea - result - we had four minutes to swim 200 yards, sprint half a mile and jump six feet. It was a good job we were fit or we'd have missed that train. 1st Belgrave H. 16 pts. 2nd Trowbridge 55 " 3rd Gosport 69 " The following morning six of the above considered themselves fit enough to go strolling. At precisely 0936 we left Croydon led by Harry Shields (shortly to explore Birkenhead) and a steady pace was maintained for six or seven miles by which time we were above the snow line. The leading bunch must have had skis, as they moved away very fast, led by "Sherpa" Clark, followed by Stan and Nick Milsum. The inevitable happened, and when Harry took a sun shot we found that the intrepid trio were hell bent for somewhere about a mile off course. Much signalling resulted and they eventually rejoined the main group in time to buy refreshments. Stan was by now sporting Club colours - he was looking alternately purple and yellow! We ascended the south Col of the downs shortly after this and made good progress to our next camp, where we waited for one straggler, who must remain nameless, then after dropping Terry Clark and Stan, the survivors pushed on over Hayes Common where Harry deviated too much to the right and was lost without trace. The two Halls were left to complete this epic, incident packed march on their own No matter what you have done on the previous day, a Sunday stroll with the Boys is the best tonic you can have. A. items.s: BELGRAVE OPEN FIELD EVENTS MEETING. MARCH 1ST Report of the club's second winter open field events meeting, with 82 individual entrants, noting the discus second place of D[illegible]szo Audorka and thanking the officials. Our second Winter Meeting was better supported than last year and even more successful. There was an entry of 82 individuals and an event entry of 128. This included some of the best performers in the country and a contingent from Cambridge University. The day was not an ideal one perhaps, but after the snowy weather in the early part of the week we were lucky indeed to be able to carry the meeting through. The javelin, perhaps, suffered most from the conditions and we really must try and persuade the L.C.C. to put down a cinder approach. Better support could have come from our own members, although we were represented in all the events except the Shot. It was pleasing to see two of our javelin throwers getting in the first six despite this being our weakest event. Bill Couzens was disappointing, especially after his good performance in the T.V.H. meeting.He is really still a novice as far as the javelin is concerned but is showing promise and must improve during the summer. Our best performer was undoubtedly D[illegible]szo Audorka with a fine throw in the discus for second place after a neck and neck battle with the winner who only widened the margin between them to four feet with his last throw. We hope to see him doing some 160's or more in the summer. Our thanks are due to the Surrey County Judges, Messrs. Reed, Fairfoul and Reeve and to Mr.E.F.Housden, the old pole vault Champion, for their assistance, together with the Club members who came along and particularly to Dick Savage who acted as Referee. items.s: NATIONAL C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS. BIRKENHEAD MARCH 8TH Report of the National cross-country championships at Birkenhead covering Belgrave's youths (12th team), seniors (15th team, Pat Newell 39th) and juniors (16th team). An unusually small band of runners and officials availed themselves of the special transport put on by British Railways for this the premier cross country event of the year. Event one, the youths race over 3 miles started in bright sunshine, most unexpected after the violent snow showers which greeted our arrival.In a large field, Arthur Penny's youngsters performed quite creditably, our first man home being Thresher in 77th place.Having partaken in a schools race the day before, Eric Penny can be said to have run well to finish 127th. Other positions:- C. Thompson 105 T. Hart 108 D. Crooks 124 Team result :- Belgrave H. 12th,414 pts. 53 teams closed in. The senior event, always a race to stir a feeling of awe in the spectator, was soon seen to be an S.L.H. "benefit", for they had three men in six at one stage. What is it about men like Firth, Driver, Pirie and company which enables them always to strike the front within half a mile or so? Pat Newell, running in his first cross country race this season, clung tenaciously to a good start and was always placed around the forty mark. He eventually finished 39th, ahead of international Harry Hicks and many other performers of high rank. Next man was Charlie Walker, 77th, an improvement on recent form, with ever consistant Eric Gebbett 134th. A special mention must be made of Clive Shippen who has been short of training. He put in as much work as possible between the Southern and this race and reaped the benefits. To finish 175th in this field was no mean performance. The rest of our men finished outside the two-hundreds. In the team race we were 15th and the only consolation that can be got from this is that Birchfield were 16th - how are the mighty fallen! To establish a lead of almost 200 yds by two miles and then coast home from a good class field was a meritorious performance. George Flanagan seemed unable to get going. One had the impression that his long-striding action was out of place on this type of going; he faded to 52nd. Whilst Geoff Stevens 118th, and K.Miller 1[illegible]6th improved on their Southern running our other lads found the pace too hot. No one was disgraced, however, and in them we have some good material for the future. items.sum: The cross country secretary laments the club's worst cross-country season since the war, urging harder concerted training, support for club matches and replies to his communications.
items.s: CROSS COUNTRY SECRETARY'S NOTES The cross country secretary laments the club's worst cross-country season since the war, urging harder concerted training, support for club matches and replies to his communications. We have reached the end of another cross country season and I regret that I can raise little or no enthusiasm for our performances. When the results of the major championships are considered it has been our worst year since the war and probably our worst since the early 1930's. Take a look at the following. South of Thames Junior 7th Surrey County 4th South of Thames Senior 9th Southern Counties 9th National 15th I realise that many clubs would be only too pleased to have such a record but it should be remembered that we have one of the largest memberships in the country and should therefore produce a higher standard in our teams. I am convinced that the talent is with us but the spirit to succeed is missing so far as cross country races are concerned. The whole atmosphere changes, however, when the road relay races start. Why can't we carry the enthusiasm shown on the Brighton road into the harder grind of the mud baths. It was a great joy to see us go from 18th to 2nd in the Southern Brighton relay last October; this proves that we have first class performers. This type of performance, however, is not repeated in the large fields of the major cross country races against the very same opposition. Why is this??? I feel that we are neglecting the well balanced training that is necessary to attain the fitness required for good cross country running. Two or three outings each week is not enough - daily training is essential, with a basic amount of really hard work combined with as much speed work as possible. We have all seen the Piries and Drivers at work at Tooting and know that such methods succeed; their followers too, benefiting similarly, even though missing the same limelight, but nevertheless becoming fit enough to bring their clubs into good positions in open races. These lads are no different to any of our members; they are all flesh and blood with the thrill of athletics in their bodies.Perhaps we fail because the concerted training runs in large packs at least three times a week no longer take place. Individual training on Saturday mornings is not necessary - we must all get together and use our efforts for the benefit of our fellow members and the Club as a whole. I am firmly of the opinion that it is quite wrong for an athlete to train continuously for months on end without an occasional race to test his ability. Our Club matches, for the past few years, have been very poorly supported, especially those away from Wimbledon. In our heyday everyone turned out, and it was not necessary for the Secretary to have to remind members to turn up, the fixture card alone was sufficient to guarantee at least thirty runners at every match. These races are planned to fit in with the advance of fitness throughout the winter season and from my own experience they can be very helpful in assessing ones progress. So many of our members fight shy of races on the score that their performances in the championships will suffer but just look at these performances and you can see that this contention is far from justified.I hope we shall all give our training considerable thought in the Summer months with a view to a considerable improvement next Winter. Now I feel that I must attack those members who habitually ignore all the communications I send out. Do they realise the hours spent in writing cards and letters for their benefit and also the cost to the Club for stationery and postage? I have been disgusted with the ignorance shown by many members in taking no notice whatsoever of my cards, especially those regarding the Ilford and Bexley road relays. In the former event we failed to finish a "B" team through the absence of a number of members who failed to give me sufficient notification of their inability to attend. At Bexley we finished only one complete team out of three just because the following failed to write or phone me despite sufficient warning :- R.Linstead, S.Charlton, S.Boreham, G.Lines, D.Manning and R.Braine. In consequence those members who ran in incomplete teams turned out with no object but to finish the course, and spent money on fares unnecessarily. In addition the Club spent 10/- per team on entrance fees. I can only hope that the people concerned have sufficient conscience to avoid a recurrence. Out of this season come a few bright prospects. In John Moore, Ken Jones and Robin Weate we have a acquired runners of high quality and Club Spirit and the improvement of George Flanagan, Peter Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Bob Glover promises well for the future. It is around these boys that our future teams will be built, plus the experience of those diehards who go on for ever. The foregoing remarks may seem rather direct and caustic but they are intended for the good of the Club and I hope you will all take them in the right spirit. It is my ambition that Belgrave should again rise to the top of the cross country world and I want everyone to analyse their approach to Club matters and resolve to do everything in their power to bring the "Claret and Gold" to the fore for many years to come. items.sum: Report of the R.W.A. 10 miles championship at Victoria Park, Hackney, where Belgrave's Stan Vickers and Eric Hall were the first two home.
items.s: R.W.A. 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP MARCH 15TH Report of the R.W.A. 10 miles championship at Victoria Park, Hackney, where Belgrave's Stan Vickers and Eric Hall were the first two home. We were strongly represented in this race, held at Victoria Park, Hackney on March 15th, fielding three teams - a goodly proportion of the 227 starters. Moreover most of our men reported fit and well, although we should have liked to have seen Bob Newson, Syd James and Roy Switzer in the field. The course consisted of five laps of approximately two miles each on level roads within the park and as expected the pace was fast and furious, and many had cause to regret their earlier speed work as they neared the end of the race. Our Stan Vickers, the Championship holder, started at a tremendous pace and at one mile had a lead of about thirty yards over a small group consisting of Eric Hall, Matthews (Sutton Coldfield) and Norman Read(Steyning), the Olympic 50 kms. Champion. At three miles Stan's lead had been reduced by Eric and Matthews, whilst Read had fallen back slightly and already there were some huge intervals between walkers. Gradually Hall and Matthews overhauled Vickers and this trio were together for quite a while, each having his nose in front momentarily. As the last lap was approached Matthews showed signs of his earlier efforts and faded out somewhat, eventually to finish sixth. Our Stan and Eric continued together, lapping numerous competitors in their progress. This passing of other walkers who had been lapped nearly proved Eric's undoing for as our two passed a group of three walkers, one on each side, one of these walkers stepped to one side (presumably to allow the faster men through) but only succeeded in knocking Eric off balance and out of rhythm - and this with less than half a mile to go. But for this the race would have been even closer for the individual title. However, we were delighted to have the first two home, repeating last year's effort. Well done, Stan and Eric! Meanwhile, what of our other team men? Dave McMullen walked a very even race indeed and was always in the first twenty. His 17th position at the finish was one of the soundest pieces of team work he has given us, and they have been many. He was in our winning team in 1947 and it says much for his efforts that he can again score all these years later. We hope to see him emulate some of his Father's performances over 20 miles in the near future. Ted Smith and George Checkley found the start a very fast one indeed and early on they seemed well back, but towards the finish they were gaining many places and claiming their rightful positions. Ray Hall did well on a course that was never to his liking and we look forward to a first class "20" from him soon. The nature of the course and the speed at which the race was walked, combined with very cold conditions towards the end, gave rise to many disqualifications. We lost Nick Milsum and Terry Clark of our first team men, but their turn will come. Nick was particularly unfortunate for he was our fourth man, on the last lap and, in the view of many, walking splendidly as he came through the field. Of our others Ray Middleton, D.J.Stevens and J.Keown show promise for the future and allin all we were well satisfied that all our walkers of A, B and C teams carried the Club colours with great credit on this difficult day. Naturally we were proud indeed to retain our hold on the London Shield and to have the first two men home. They were also first and second in the Inter Counties Race, and Eric Hall, Dave McMullen and Ray Hall were in the Surrey team which was placed third. items.sum: Vice-President Frederick Mark Stone ("Rodney"), decorated Metropolitan Police officer and 1920s club walker, was the subject of the B.B.C. television programme This Is Your Life on March 3rd.
items.s: "THIS IS YOUR LIFE" Vice-President Frederick Mark Stone ("Rodney"), decorated Metropolitan Police officer and 1920s club walker, was the subject of the B.B.C. television programme This Is Your Life on March 3rd. On March 3rd, a popular Belgravian Vice-President, Frederick Mark Stone ("Rodney"), found himself the centre figure of the well established B.B.C. television programme. Rather unwillingly he was persuaded to leave the audience for the platform by Eamonn Andrews, when Paul Bennett V.C., Mrs. Stone, Fred's two sons and many former colleagues and friends from all stations of life (including our own Past President, Harry Evans) outlined those assets of character, courage and sportsmanship which have endeared him to such a wide circle. The programme culminated in the presentation of a testimonial cheque by the Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police, Sir John Nott-Bower on behalf of the members of that great body to "our Rodney", who has been well described as the "bravest Metropolitan Policeman ever". Mention was made during the programme of his winning of the Kings' Police Medal for Bravery in jumping from Westminster Bridge to save life, of the award of the Royal Humane Society Medal for life saving, of supreme courage during an air raid which brought the award of the British Empire Medal, and of his success in preventing a smash and grab raid (when on sick leave and in plain clothes) which resulted in Fred being beaten over the head with an iron bar - but his man did not get away! His courage and devotion to duty gained recognition when he received the George Medal from the hands of Her Majesty the Queen - but his severe injuries unfortunately resulted in his discharge from the Police. Fred was in many of our long distance walking teams in the early 1920's and was a great worker for the Club always, and it was pleasing to see such a combination of many virtues (and many could only be lightly touched upon) on television, exemplifying a life - with many more years yet to run, we trust - which could well serve as a model for the younger man of service, courage and personality. items.label: No. 134
items.sum: Profile of Bill Lucas, the club's cross country secretary, a 1948 Olympic 5000 metres runner and Tommy Green Trophy winner who never won a club championship.
items.s: PORTRAIT GALLERY Profile of Bill Lucas, the club's cross country secretary, a 1948 Olympic 5000 metres runner and Tommy Green Trophy winner who never won a club championship. What stranger than to have represented Great Britain in the Olympic Games, gained international vests for track running and yet be denied a single Club Championship during a distinguished career lasting almost twenty years? Such is the case of Bill Lucas our present cross country secretary. Unlike some stars, who shot into their orbit from the blue, but who faded into obscurity with equal rapidity, Bill progressed steadily in the post war years, representing the Club on every possible occasion and proved that good track running is not adversely affected by cross country racing. 1946 saw Bill win the South of the Thames Junior C.C. race at Cheam and the following January he gained his County vest by finishing fourth in the Surrey C.C. Championship. He also finished well up in the South of the Thames Senior race and in the same year finished second in the Surrey 3 miles track race. Although not listed amongst the probables for the 1948 Olympic Games, Bill sprang a surprise by gaining third place in the A.A.A. 3 miles and earned selection for the 5000 metres in the Games, where he ran well, probably the best of our representatives. Two international races were to come for Bill, when in 1950 he finished second in the 5000 metres in a triangular match at the White City, and at the same venue, versus U.S.A. and Benelux Countries, was third in an event of the same distance won by Ashenfelter of U.S.A. For his great three mile time of 14m.11.6s. in the A.A.A. Championships of the same year Bill received the coveted Tommy Green Trophy for the best performance of the year by a Belgravian. Bill's record in the London to Brighton relay is second to none; he was consistently in the team from 1947 to 1954. Possibly his best performance was in giving Max Jones of Birchfield 31 secs. start on the last stage in 1948 and finishing twenty yards in front of him to give us a great win. On four occasions Bill had the honour of handing the baton to the Mayor of Brighton after finishing first on the last stage of this classic relay race. Although he took a long time to prove he meant it, Bill retired in 1955, only to increase his Club activities even moreso in official capacities. Rather outspoken, but that is what is needed in our Club, Bill has earned the respect of all Belgravians for good work. Perhaps the greatest tribute one can pay him is that he moves with the times and recognises today's runners for what they are worth, one never hears him make unfavourable comparisons between present and past and few know of his distinguished war career when he was decorated for service with the R.A.F. Report and Belgrave placings from a five-club 15 miles walk at Mitcham won easily by Belgrave, plus Ray Hall's win in the Stock Exchange Croydon to Keston walk. Dave McMullen, by finishing second, gave a good indication of his ability over this distance and a newcomer to the distance, J.Keown put up a sterling performance, and with a little more experience should soon be among the top notchers. items.label: No. 134
items.sum: Report and full result of the club 5½ miles road race, the last trial for the London to Brighton relay team, won by Dave Baulch from Eric Gebbett.
items.s: CLUB 5½ MILES ROAD RACE. MARCH 29TH Report and full result of the club 5½ miles road race, the last trial for the London to Brighton relay team, won by Dave Baulch from Eric Gebbett. In perfect conditions a field of thirty-four was started on its way by Past President Tom Morrell. This race is the last chance for London to Brighton relay aspirants to prove their worthiness of being included in the team for this classic race. As a consequence the selectors are given more than a few headaches - this year being no exception. Eric Gebbett was, as usual, quickly in the lead and he, together with Charlie Walker and Dave Baulch, took the field along at a very brisk pace. After about two miles these three became detached from the rest of the struggling mass and it was soon obvious that the winner could only be one of this trio. With about a mile and a half to go, Charlie had a lead of fifty yards and it seemed all over bar the shouting. However, the stiff climb up Pepys Road slowed him down to such an extent that he was quickly passed by his two opponents, Baulch and Gebbett, who went on to finish first and second respectively. The winning time was the third fastest ever accomplished and Dave must be congratulated on a very fine performance. Eric, in beating 29 minutes, can also be said to have run exceptionally well. Another to show much improved form was Clive Shippen. Perhaps the most meritorious performance was that of Charlie Smart, now forty eight years of age, in returning the splendid time of 30.26. But for a mishap with his glasses, which he dropped while cleaning them, his time would have been considerably faster. Congratulations Charlie and may you continue for many more years! items.label: No. 134
items.h: CARSHALTON CORONATION TROPHY MEETING. EASTER MONDAY
items.sum: Report of the Carshalton Coronation Trophy Meeting where Belgrave finished third behind T.V.H. and Mitcham and were presented with a plaque for three successive wins.
items.s: CARSHALTON CORONATION TROPHY MEETING. EASTER MONDAY Report of the Carshalton Coronation Trophy Meeting where Belgrave finished third behind T.V.H. and Mitcham and were presented with a plaque for three successive wins. Held on a cold, blustery afternoon, this event which we have won on three previous occasions, saw us finish third to T.V.H., who fielded almost an international team. We were beaten by Mitcham for second place by one point, a creditable performance considering our sadly depleted field events representation. Charlie Jones was our highest points scorer, finishing 2nd in the 220 yds. to Segal, who won in the fast time of 22.1 s. He also provided our only win of the day by cleverly taking the 440 yds. in 53.2s. Clive Shippen clocked 9m.47.2s., his fastest, in the two miles to enable us to secure third team place. D.Ansell showed good early season form in the long jump, with four jumps over 20 ft; his best, 20'6½" gained him second place. Special mention must be made of S.Boreham, who, recovering from a bad cold reluctantly competed in the mile, finishing 3rd in 4m47s. and having been persuaded to start in the two miles to complete our team, hung on to the end, finishing in a state of collapse. Our other competitors were Holtum, 3rd in the 100yds, and Pepe and Edwards 4th in the 880 yds. and javelin respectively. In recognition of our winning the trophy for three successive years, Carshalton Council made a nice gesture by presenting us with a special plaque. Charlie Jones Charlie Jones 2nd 220 yds.; won 440 yds. in 53.2s. Segal Segal won 220 yds. in 22.1 s. items.label: No. 135
items.sum: Editorial praising the quality of track performances, including Brian Morris and John Davies, but lamenting thin club representation and asking for timely reports.
items.s: Editorial Editorial praising the quality of track performances, including Brian Morris and John Davies, but lamenting thin club representation and asking for timely reports. Dear Fellow Members, From reports so far received, our track performances have been notable for their quality, if Club representation has been lacking in quantity. In the wide sphere in which we compete, we provided champions in six counties; a pretty remarkable achievement. Some great running has come from Brian Morris, with a 48·9s. quarter to his credit when representing the South against the North and Midlands and from John Davies (4m.10·6s.) for Middlesex versus Cambridge. But it is sad to note that in the majority of cases the same old faces turn up, whilst new talent seems to be lacking ( our youth and junior county results bear this out). On paper we have a powerful team at all events, but our inability to muster this strength in matches is poor advertisment and does not show respect for our opponents, let alone for the patient officials. A well meaning anonymous member sends us reports for youths and junior cross country events for which, he states, no reports appeared in the Belgravian. Whilst we appreciate the effort, such items are of doubtful interest after such a lapse of time. This must not be taken to mean that we do not require news, we do! It must be stressed, however, that it should reach us not later than a fortnight after the event occured. Brian Morris Brian Morris 48·9s. quarter for the South against the North and Midlands John Davies John Davies 4m.10·6s. for Middlesex versus Cambridge

items.sum: Report of a poor twelfth place in the Cambridge Harriers Road Relay, and a win for the Belgrave veterans' team.
items.s: Cambridge Harriers Road Relay March 22nd. Report of a poor twelfth place in the Cambridge Harriers Road Relay, and a win for the Belgrave veterans' team. The less said about this event the better,for Bill Lucas looked an extremely harassed man as he juggled with the very inadequate forces at his disposal. The inevitable happened, in that our "B" team was incomplete and that the "A" team contained men, including the writer, of obvious "B" team capacity. Clive Shippen and Len Adams ran quite well on the first leg for the "A" and "B" teams respectively, but apart from a good run by Ken Jones on the third stage there were no outstanding efforts. Twelfth position in this event was not mediocre but downright shameful. In the veterans relay over four stages our team of E. Stimpson, L. Rolls, D. Brickwood and Charlie Smart had a very easy win, with the last named showing great form in returning a lap time of 19.46. items.label: No. 135
items.h: Stock Exchange 25 Miles Walk at Hayes, Kent. March 29th.
items.sum: Appreciation of Ray Hall's record-breaking win in the Stock Exchange 25 miles walk, with Dave Stevens fourth.
items.s: Stock Exchange 25 Miles Walk at Hayes, Kent. March 29th. Appreciation of Ray Hall's record-breaking win in the Stock Exchange 25 miles walk, with Dave Stevens fourth. Reminiscences hardly have a part in club life, yet who can say what part "Footerisms", "Harleyisms" and all the other "isms" have in creating the spirit of comradeship, sportsmanship and will to achieve that which is such a part of a true Belgravian. What luck I had in attending to Ray Hall on what I am sure is only the first of his many victories in "Claret and Gold". With pride I watched him breast the tedious climb out of Westerham and shatter the opposition,and saw the tenacity with which he stuck to his task when in the doldrums and the whole world looked black and unsmiling. With pride I witnessed the comeback of a true champion as his strength returned and he started that fight against the watch, as not only victory but one of the most difficult records of the walking calender came within grasp. Such was my fortune and pleasure in witnessing one of our younger school display such fine characteristics and have his name added to the long list of champions this Club has produced. Congratulations also to Dave Stevens for his performance in finishing fourth. Result:- 1st R.C. Hall 3hr.39m.08s. 4th D.J. Stevens 4 " 02" 28" Previous record 3hr.41m.51s. H.W.S. items.label: No. 135
items.h: Match v. Hercules A.C. & S.L.H. at Tooting. April 23rd.
items.sum: Report of the mid-week track match against Hercules A.C. and S.L.H. at Tooting, with Belgrave second in the senior match and third in the junior match.
items.s: Match v. Hercules A.C. & S.L.H. at Tooting. April 23rd. Report of the mid-week track match against Hercules A.C. and S.L.H. at Tooting, with Belgrave second in the senior match and third in the junior match. Our first mid-week fixture of the season, although blessed with fine weather and excellent conditions, did not produce results quite in the same category. However, our performances were not entirely displeasing. Brian Morris, in serious preparation for a coveted place at Cardiff and Stockholm, sharpened his speed by running in both the 100 and 220 yds. events; comfortably winning the latter by a yard from Gerry Leroy in 23.2s. This event produced our only points maximum of the evening. Henry Martin produced a promising early season effort in the quarter when running a close second to Woodland of Hercules(52.0) and, although only placed fifth, it was good to see Jim Heathfield running quarters once more after his third retirement from the event! Apparently he hasn't yet decided between the 440 yds. and the Mitcham '15' !! Although we had four representatives in the mile they had to fill the last four places behind P.Driver(4m.19.8s.), E.Earl (4.23.1), J.Edgar and C.Wilson. Our first(?) man home was Len Orton, our second claim member from Birchfield, who recorded 4m.30.2s. Mal Ash collected his usual quota of points with a win in the High Jump (5'7") and a second in the pole vault(11'6"). Three Bels supported Mal in the high jump with 5'6", 5'4" and 5'0"; the latter performance by Roach, still only a boy. Dave Ansell(19'8") was beaten on the last jump by one inch for second place, and finished third, four inches behind the winner. Coleman collected a point here for his fourth place and a further two in the shot, which was won by Rasey, our 3rd(!) claim member from Southgate and Barnet. In the junior match our best performance was by Stan Black who ran third in the half mile to Jones of S.L.H.(2m.1.2s.) and Hamilton of Hercules(2m.3.2s.); the latter just pipping Stan on the line. This was a fine run only two weeks after the London to Brighton relay and a busy winter season. Dave Taylor earned a point for his fourth place as did D. Crookes in the mile, but with no entry in either of the sprints our points total reached a mere six. Surely we have some junior sprinters somewhere! items.s: Finchley '20'. April 26th — Great run by Eric Gebbett Report of the Finchley 20 miles road race, where Eric Gebbett was 8th and Belgrave placed 4th team in both the open and Southern Counties races. This event was favoured by its usual warm weather, but a strong wind prevailed throughout and made hard going of the first two miles of each five mile lap. A good class field emphasised the fact that this is now the top 20 of the year. At five miles, Eric Gebbett was placed 6th with Len and Eric Bishop 28th and 43 rd respectively. Our fourth man at this stage was Alan Bishop in 55th place but he didn't stay there for long, and at nine miles was overtaken by Geoff Pearson. The impetuous were soon feeling the effects of the fast first ten miles and our scoring men were steadily moving through. Eric Gebbett, although slowing somewhat on his last lap, ended up in 8th place, returning the very fast time of 1hr.50m.29s.The Bishop brothers, less Alan, who was having a rough time due to the after effects of a heavy cold, had moved up to 22nd and 25th positions. With Geoff Pearson, now a veteran, gaining 49th place, we were placed 4th team in both the open and Southern Counties race held in conjunction. Also started:- R. Bolem, A. Penstone, R.Conway, L.
