items.sum: History of Belgrave's performances in the News of the World London to Brighton relay (later the National Relay) and the Southern Relay from 1924 to 1959, signed A.A.H.
items.s: BELGRAVE AND BRIGHTON RELAYS - 1924 to 1959 History of Belgrave's performances in the News of the World London to Brighton relay (later the National Relay) and the Southern Relay from 1924 to 1959, signed A.A.H. The first relay race on the Brighton road organised by the "News of the World" took place in 1924. Belgrave did not merit an invitation to compete on this occasion and sixteen clubs, all Southern, took part with Surrey A.C. proving the winners in 4hrs. 50min.0·2s. Each competing club fielded a team of ten men. In the following year, Belgrave were still absentees, but Birchfield Harriers entered for the first time and proved equal to their great reputation by winning from a field of seventeen teams. In 1926 we received an invitation to compete, following a qualifying race, and Hallamshire Harriers from the North were also in the field for the first time. We were never conspicuous at any time; seventh position at Merstham was our best, and at Brighton we were 14th. On the ninth stage (then 5 miles 486 yds. up Dale Hill) Bert Footer returned second fastest time. In 1927 we again qualified, but in the relay itself we suffered grave disappointment for we were never nearer than ninth, and eventually finished 17th. Our one small mead of satisfaction was the running of A.E. Smith whose time on the Mitcham to Purley stage was third fastest. In 1928 we were (not unexpectedly!) called on to qualify in a trial race once again, and this we did in emphatic fashion, winning the trial by over two minutes. In the Brighton Relay itself we managed to improve by 11½ minutes on our time of the previous year and finished 12th in the race. We were never higher than 10th and never lower than 14th throughout; and derived satisfaction from our evident solidarity even if brilliance was lacking. 1929 marked a turning-point and gave us our first set of medals in this race. For the first time we included in our team Arthur Allum and Arthur Penny (both to win International cross-country honours later) and the brothers Jack and Joe Flower. Our seventh position earned us the special award medals. Joe Flower excelled himself in running the second fastest over stage 2, and placed us second at Mitcham. Even more improvement was shewn in 1930, when we finished fourth and earned a set of place medals. Our star runners were Allum, who did fastest time over his stretch and Syd Warboys, running for the first time who was second fastest on the long fifth stage of those days of 6 miles 352 yards. In the following year we actually finished fifth, but many thought our performance had more merit than that of the previous year. We suffered a bitter blow when Arthur Allum, having made four places in 2½ miles and seeming all set to peg back more, sustained an ankle injury and had to concede two of the places gained. Arthur had great difficulty in finishing and had to be carried away once the change-over had been effected. In this race another of our future Internationals, Tom Carter, made his debut. In 1932 the sporting papers advised the public that the Belgrave team had deteriorated and would not be in the first half-dozen - whereat we were secretly very pleased! The strongest field ever was promised; for all the leading clubs in the country were to be represented. Over the first eight stages we were either fourth or fifth - remarkable consistency. On the ninth relay yet another of our Internationals, that great character Bert Footer, showed his teeth and took us into third place, which was well held to the end by our Captain, Bill Webb. The two clubs to finish in front of us were Salford Harriers and Birchfield Harriers. Behind us were Aldershot Command A.C., South London Harriers and Surrey A.C. in that order, with fourteen other clubs following on. Every one of our runners set up a new Club record over his stage. Obviously the conditions must have been favourable, but here were ten magnificent performances. In those days we had on the road a double-decker bus, which served as grandstand and dressing room. The inside was curtained off and we actually dropped our man at his relay point, picked up our finishing runner and then passed through the field to the next change-over point and so on throughout the race. What a hopeless task it would be these days! Needless to say a very happy bus load of Belgravians returned to London on that day in April 1932. In 1933 third position was again ours, and Salford Harriers, from Manchester, and Birchfield Harriers were again in front of us.But once again we were the first Southern club home, and the future hope of the South to win a sporting victory over the Midlands and North. That came in 1934 - and how excited we were! April 14th was the date and the late Bill Rice was entrusted with the first stretch from Westminster and handed over third. Tom Carter held the position and next Harry Shields set about the opposition to some purpose. He quickly took the lead and also the baton carried by the leading team (the first Belgrave man to carry it). He still gripped it firmly and defiantly at Purley even though the Polytechnic Harriers runner got his nose in front in the last yard! Jack Flower (4th stage) had a three seconds lead over the Poly when handing over and 2 min. 2 sec. lead over Birchfield. Arthur Penny ran our fifth leg and finished 61 sec. ahead of the Poly with Birchfield nearly three minutes away; we were well on our way to our first victory! Syd Warboys increased our lead over the next stretch, and then we ran over successive stages two newcomers, Bert Shaw and Alf Taylor. Both ran well but nevertheless at Hickstead, Polytechnic and Birchfield had made some inroads into our lead. Bert Footer, on the Dale Hill stretch that he new so well, ran brilliantly, recording second best time over the stage to hand over nearly two minutes in front of Poly with Birchfield four minutes further back. Our great little International handed over to another of that gallant band, Arthur Allum, who sped on his way over the last stretch of 6 miles 904 yards to return the fastest for the stage, and gave us a winning margin of 2 mins. 6 sec. over Polytechnic Harriers, and 4 mins 9 secs. over Birchfield. Great was our delight! 1935 - we were now English Cross-country champions and holders of the Relay Trophy, the challenged, no longer the challengers. Birchfield Harriers tried all they knew to give us a beating and at the commencement of the last stage were only 17 seconds behind, but we ran out winners by 37 seconds. Newcomers to our team were Jim Ginty (one of our finest runners ever), Dan Patience and Syd Ring. Our hat-trick of wins was accomplished in 1936 and we were the first club to have three wins in a row, even though Birchfield could boast five wins in all. Two new boys in our team were Pat Parker and Ted Stimpson - both destined to become Cross-country Internationals. Our winning margin on this occasion was 13 seconds only from Birchfield - a most exciting race, marred only by the death of C. Young of Queens Park Harriers who was killed on the road. This was the first of the races to start from Mitcham and teams still consisted of ten men. 1937 was our Jubilee Year and naturally we wished to excel, but as so often happens at such times, we were doomed to disappointment. After taking the lead on the second relay (Pat Parker gained eight places) we held it all the way to Brighton and to within half a dozen yards of the tape, when Mitcham A.C. (represented by Dennis Brickwood, now well known as one of our members) managed to gain an inches win in almost the last stride! Birchfield were a mere 12 seconds behind us - what a race! Our team newcomers were Les Cohen and Bill Lucas, then a junior, but destined later to win Olympic and International honours. In 1938 we slipped back to third position, Mitcham A.C. again winning, with Birchfield second. Those were the days of mass unemployment, and many Welsh International runners were finding their way on to the nursing staff of a certain mental hospital in S.W. London, whence they became members of Mitcham A.C. Much high feeling was caused at the time, but one thing is certain, and that is that there were some grand runners and sportsmen among these Welsh runners. In our team for the first time were Len Herbert, due to become an International later, Harry Verney and Charlie Smart. Mitcham's hat-trick of wins was recorded in 1939 when we were second and Birchfield third. All our runners on this occasion had previous relay experience and one of the best performances was by Charlie Smart on the fifth leg. Then came War and it was "good-bye" to Brighton Relays until 1947. In our Diamond Jubilee Year we were again the winners, and in no uncertain manner, for we led on every stage except the eighth when we were second for a short while, but Len Herbert quickly took us to the fore again. Blackheath Harriers were second and Coventry Godiva third. Rather naturally there were new names in our team in Vic Blowfield, George Lucas, Stan Eales, Eric Herbert and Albert Frost. It is interesting to note that of our ten runners, six were past or future Internationals. Our 1948 win owed much to Bill Lucas who started the last lap 31 seconds behind Birchfield and passed the finishing line twenty seconds to the good! Newcomers to the team were Tom Clinton, Ken Stimpson, Martin Williamson and Eddie Short. Twenty-five clubs competed in 1949 and we accomplished our second hat-trick of wins, thus achieving more wins in the nineteen races held than any other club. Birchfield, Tipton and Reading A.C. finished 2nd, 3rd and 4th in that order. On April 1st 1950, old friends of ours for many years past on track and country, Thames Valley Harriers, scored their first win. It was definately not our day although we took the fourth set of medals, for Blackheath and Reading also anticipated us into Brighton. The first of the National Relays was staged in April 1951 over the Mitcham to Brighton course, and we were the winners from Thames Valley H. by nearly three minutes. Our team ran in this order:- C.W. Walker, L.W. Herbert, A. Bedford, W.E. Lucas, J.C. Smart, E. Herbert, J.W. Brown, J. Bromley, E. Short and L. Adams. The Southern Relay held later in the year provided us with another win - our fifth win in the last six races - and the minor places were filled by Blackheath H. and Polytechnic H. In 1952 Birchfield Harriers gained their first Relay win since 1931, beating us by 25 seconds with the Scottish Club, Victoria Park A.A.C. in third place. In this race Pete Newell made his debut, coming in as reserve on the fifth stage. He took us from tenth to fourth position and accomplished fastest time - what a reserve to have up one's sleeve! In the Southern Relay held later in the year we had yet another win by almost a minute from T.V.H.; Essex Beagles were third. Jack Brown, Arthur Bruce, Len Adams and Ray Tooby all broke stage records, with Eddie Short also doing so but finding one better runner on the day in Ken Norris of Thames Valley. The National Relay of 1953 found us slipping back to fourth place behind Thames Valley H., Birchfield H. and South London H. Bill Lucas recorded fastest time over the eighth stage. In the Southern Relay held in October we finished second to Essex Beagles with T.V.H. third. In 1954 the National Relay reverted to the old pre 1936 full length course from Westminster to Brighton (54¾). Our position was a meritorious second to South London Harriers with Essex Beagles third. Teams comprised eleven men and our team did exceedingly well although we were very conscious of the fact that five of our members were over 35 years of age, and of the need for some young replacements. The Southern Relay in October gave Herne Hill their first win with Thames Valley H. and ourselves second and third. We move more into the days of recent history and 1955 found us fourth in the National Relay behind S.L.H., Poly and Sheffield. The Southern Relay gave us a real shock - we were sixth! From 1932 onwards we had always won a set of medals in this event and now we were turned away empty. In 21 consecutive races we had been inside the first four places (on nine occasions, winners) and this is a record any club would be glad to have; but this fall from grace was all the harder! In 1956 we were fifth in the National event, S.L.H. winning for the third time in succession. We were happy to see two of our younger members Charlie Dabbs and George Flanagan performing so well. The Southern race gave us the chance of being in the "placings" once again, and we were third to Thames Valley H. and Herne Hill H. Jack Brown, as so often, ran splendidly for us. The 1957 National race also found us in third place, with S.L.H. winning once again. Ours was a satisfying performance. The Southern relay in October had added distance due to the re-laying of the road round Gatwick Airport, and twelve runners constituted a team. Thames Valley H. had an easy win but we took second place with Woodford Green A.C. third. As we were 18th at the end of the first relay we did well to come through to second at the end of the race. Last year we dropped to 11th in the National race and 6th in the Southern Relay. This year, as recorded elsewhere, we were placed 11th again in the National Relay; and in October we shall be able to try ourselves out once again with the other chosen clubs in the South. Our form in the last two years has borne no comparison with that of earlier days. It is true that many of our younger runners who by now should be establishing reputations in these relays have been prevented by injuries from turning out as regularly as we would have wished, but time is still on their side. In addition we have some excellent junior runners maturing and there can be little doubt that those golden days we enjoyed for so long can soon come back. But they will not return without plenty of purposeful hard work added to great enthusiasm and solid mutual team support in training, as well as in racing. These, we may be certain, will be forthcoming, and may we see their results soon! A.A.H. items.s: FINCHLEY H. 20 MILES ROAD RACE - APRIL 18TH Report of the Finchley 20 miles road race, with Belgrave winning the team race and the Belgrave finishers' positions and times. This very popular event again attracted a large entry and there were actually 163 starters. Some tremendously fast running ensued and the winner (O'Gorman of St. Albans) covered the course in 1h.43m.26s.- 3m.25s. faster than the previous record. With such a fast winning time many meritorious performances "down the field" are apt to be overlooked, but Colin Collis deserves special mention for his 11th place in 1h.50m.50s as does Bob Plummer for his best ever time of 1h.52m.54s. In the team race we scored the same number of points as T.V.H. but our fourth scoring man finished ahead of two of their scoring members and so clinched first place. items.s: MATCH v. HERCULES A.C. 13TH MAY. Report of the evening match against Hercules A.C., which began with the club 7 miles walk championship for the Frank Elson Cup, with the walk result. The evening commenced with the Club 7 miles walk Championship for the Frank Elson Cup. Notable absentees were Stan Vickers, the holder, and Eric Hall, last year's runner up. However, form had altered very little for Ray Hall, Hugh McGreechan and George Beecham, 3rd, 4th and 5th last year, filled the first three places this time in the same order! Although the turnout of Seniors and Juniors for the match with Hercules was quite good, they were outnumbered by the boys and youths present. Les Stokell and Tom Carter have a most enthusiastic bunch of youngsters under their wings; it gladdened one's heart to see so much promising young talent in Belgrave vests. A most exciting Senior 100 yds. was won by the versatile Charlie Jones in the good time of 10·2; Ron Holtum and S. Deane each clocked 10·3. The half-mile was notable for the last lap performance of John Thresher. With just over 500 yds. to go John was boxed in by a group of runners 12 yds. behind the leaders. Entering the back straight for the second time he made his effort to catch the leaders. Rubbery legs in the last 40 yds. prevented his doing so and Malcolm Robinson passed him on the line . However, he was undoubtedly the fastest over the second lap and its good to see him consistantly breaking 2 minutes these days. In the mile Derek Crookes gave a most welcome show of form by finishing third in a time of 4m.25·1s. Don Maclean also running well again did 4m.21s. and Alan Black 4m.25·7s. The standard in the long-jump was also high. Dave Ansell, runner up in the Sward Trophy a few days earlier could only manage 4th place this time with a similar distance! Jim McGrath, our new member from Northern Ireland who seems to be another Mal Ash, jumped a most creditable 21'0" to finish 5th. The junior sprints illustrated our sad lack of young sprinters but this was offset to some extent by the promising debut of Linley in the 440 yds. His time of 52·6s. should be cut considerably under the guidance of Frank Simmons, as he has the stamp of a class runner. Our junior Captain, Brian Kolbe performed creditably in both the 220 and 440 and is improving each time out. Eric Penny ran a very well judged race to win the mile in 4m.45·7s., an encouraging early season time. Result of 7 miles walk. 1, R.C. Hall 55.47; 2, R. Middleton 56.10; 3, G.S. items.sum: Report of the rushed evening match against H.H.H. and Q.P.H., with senior, junior and youths match scores.
items.s: MATCH v. H.H.H. & Q.P.H. MAY 20TH. Report of the rushed evening match against H.H.H. and Q.P.H., with senior, junior and youths match scores. Owing to a late start, and an already overcrowded programme for an evening meeting, the events had to be rushed through in double quick time; giving the appearance of some hybrid relay meeting. However this did not stop the athletes from putting up some good performances. Sylvan Deane won both the sprints in 10·5 and 22·8 and a now free from injury Gerry Leroy made a welcome comeback to win both second string sprints in 10·4 and 23·5 . Brian Morris and John Davies showed their class by cantering home in the 440 and 880 respectively and virtually clinched the match for us. An excellent start to the season was made by Norman Caves in the triple jump with 45'4", only 13" less than his highly ranked best of last year. Jim McGrath showed his versatility by adding the discus to his list of events, and continued his battle of the "half-inch" with Dave Ansell in the long jump. Jim and Dave seem to be inseparable in their long-jumping performances. In the junior match Brian Kolbe (2m.4·5s.) was our only winner although Eric Penny was narrowly beaten in the mile. The junior section must be hungrily awaiting the arrival of some of our promising youths. Les Stokell's lads did their duty in the youths match by beating Herne Hill. A few personalities will no doubt soon arise from their ranks and their progress watched with growing interest. Keep at it boys! items.label: No. 139
items.h: VANCOUVER TROPHY MEETING AT WOODFORD MAY 23RD
items.sum: Report of Belgrave's under-strength team at the Vancouver Trophy meeting staged by Woodford Green A.C. in a fierce wind.
items.s: VANCOUVER TROPHY MEETING AT WOODFORD MAY 23RD Report of Belgrave's under-strength team at the Vancouver Trophy meeting staged by Woodford Green A.C. in a fierce wind. This meeting was inaugurated in 1955 by Woodford Green A.C. to commemorate the performances of Elliott and Johnson in the previous year's Empire Games at Vancouver. The home club were virtually at full strength, but many athletes from some of the other clubs were conspicuous by their absence. Our own John Davies, Brian Morris, Clive Ryan, Frank Wright and D. McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave. Nevertheless, the lads who did carry our colours performed with considerable credit and had no small portion of bad luck. Conditions would have been ideal but for a fierce wind which affected almost every performance. Ron Holtum just failed to qualify for the final of the 100 m. recording 11·8 in his battle against both wind and competitors. In the 200m. we were out of luck again when S.Deane, who clocked 22·7s. was also unable to qualify. However, Dave Carter joined the finalists with a workmanlike performance a provided us with a very valuable point. In the 400m. C.Lindsay of Q.P.H. showed considerable speed and strength in negotiating the antics of the wind to record a phenomenal 47·7! How Brian Morris would have liked to have been there! Our own Alan Jackson (51·9) was also unable to reach the final but ran a sound race. When he has the courage to make his first 220 a little faster his times will undoubtedly improve. Dave Mitchell and John Thresher, both of whom are new arrivals to the senior ranks, each narrowly missed qualifying for the 800m final. They both ran very spirited races and in a couple of seasons time should prove to be outstanding performers. In the 1500m. Malcolm Robinson, our only entrant, found himself up against opponents such as Earl, Linford, Chapman and Ellis, but with his usual show of determination and ever-improving ability he secured a point with a time of 4m.2·4s., another best performance. In many events we were unable to field two competitors, which meant a possible wastage of points before we started. The 5000m. appeared to be another such event when a call was put out for the runners to assemble. Simultaneously, a certain Irishman, red-faced and panting, burst upon the scene having, seemingly, run a four minute mile from Woodford Station. Having had his clothes virtually dragged from him John Moore was ushered over to the starting line where he just had time to take a deep breath before travelling a further 5000 metres. John must be congratulated on his running although his performance, of course, was not one of his best. Don Maclean ran well in the first half of the race but when it became obvious that he wouldn't score he eased down to save himself for the steeplechase, in which he had volunteered to run. In the high hurdles Jim McGrath showed his prowess by qualifying for the final. Charlie did likewise in the 400m. hurdles and was a creditable fourth in 57·9s. Both Percy Porter and John Ware did well in finishing 3rd and 2nd in the hammer and javelin respectively. Jim McGrath led in the long jump until the final round where two competitors"pulled one out of the bag". Only 2¾" separated the first four! Both Jim and Dave Ansell, who was fourth, recorded 20'3", the wind accounting for a good two feet. Dave went on to a fourth place in the triple jump while Jim completed a "Mal Ash" type performance by finishing third in the pole vault, narrowly failing at 12'0", an excellent days work. Stan and Eric were sadly missed in the 3000m. walk, although Ted Smith and John Knifton gleaned a valuable three points between them. Prior to the 3000m steeplechase Clive Shippen paid the penalty of insufficient warming-up by pulling a thigh muscle when negotiating a hurdle. Thus Don Maclean faced yet another race as our sole competitor as this time there was no late arrival to join him. In doing 10.21 Don left behind several fresher opponents. As far as the match result was concerned Woodford Green were in an unassailable position quite early on. Of Belgrave's 32 points, 23 were obtained on the field and 9 on the track, from which you may form your own conclusions. C.S. items.s: R.W.A. 20 MILES ROAD WALK CHAMPIONSHIP - MAY 9TH Report of the R.W.A. 20 miles road walk championship at Imber Court, where Belgrave were second team and retained the Nijmegen Cup, with Belgrave positions and times. Held on a very hot day at Imber Court this race was notable for the way in which Tom Missen and Don Thompson, both of Metropolitan Walking Club, absolutely slaughtered the opposition. It was also notable for the performance of George Williams who came in at the last minute to replace Eric Hall, who had leg trouble. To finish fifth in such a class field at his first attempt over the distance deserves great praise. Credit must also be accorded to Terry Clark, only just out of the junior stage, for his very fine effort in finishing ninth. Although we lost the team race we did retain the Nijmegen Cup for the first club to finish eight men, indeed this is the fifth time in succession that we have won it. Teams:- 1st Met. items.sum: Report of the Surrey Championships at Motspur Park, at which Belgrave were represented in every event and swept the two miles walk, signed C.S.
items.s: SURREY CHAMPIONSHIPS - 29/30TH MAY. Report of the Surrey Championships at Motspur Park, at which Belgrave were represented in every event and swept the two miles walk, signed C.S. Without doubt Motspur Park has an atmosphere all of its own. A fast track in a pleasant, well-sheltered setting, together with a large appreciative crowd of spectators reclining on the grassy banks and the usually fine weather, make this meeting a rather special occasion for competitor and onlooker alike. A large proportion of the crowd consists of semi-retired athletes, still dabbling, who have not yet managed to resist the lure of an athletic meeting. At one time they would have returned home determined to make a "come back", but now, alas, the County Junior and Youth performances are sufficient cause to not only turn this group to full retirement but to swell their ranks by the addition of many more disillusioned Seniors. At Whitsun, Surrey's athletes allowed the Inter-County Trophy to slip across the river to their Middlesex rivals. But on thisday they made it quite clear that it had gone for no more than a year's holiday. Performances were improving all round but most noticeably amongst the younger competitors. Mitcham A.C. and Hercules A.C. were the most prominent but Belgrave were unique in being represented in every event - that is if one is allowed to count the announcer! Yes, Bill Lucas was on duty once more. Bill's announcing is second to none and he must be congratulated on the way he carried this marathon task. Highlights of the meeting were, a 1m.49·6s. "half" from Brian Hewson, a 48·7s. 440 by junior John Strachan of Hercules and a 13m.49·6s. conquest by his clubmate Ernie Earl over the redoubtable Mike Maynard in the three miles. For many this meeting started and finished on Friday evening, and no less dramatically than in the Senior mile heats. County standard is 4m.24s., yet Giddings of Deptford Park failed to qualify for the final with a time of 4m.13·7s.! and our own Malcolm Robinson likewise with a personal best of 4m.19s. In the two miles walk Belgrave swept to victory by filling the first three places; George Williams winning from Ray Middleton with John Knifton a good third in his first year of senior competition. On Saturday Clive Ryan and Charlie Jones comfortably qualified for the 440 final despite being drawn against each other in their heat and having to fill first two places. Clive recorded 49·9 and Charlie 51·0. In the final Clive was drawn on the outside lane, while the holder, Woodland of Hercules, was blessed with the inside. However, Woodland had to put up a Best Championship Performance of 48·4 in beating Clive's 49·4. Charlie was fifth in 51·3. Eric Penny ran well on Friday evening to qualify for the Junior mile final but found the opposition too strong next day. The first four broke the Best Championship Performance and the first seven were inside 4m.23s.! Harvey of Mitcham (4.16·8) led from start to finish to win from Harper of S.L.H. (4.19·1) Eric Shirley made his first appearance at the Championships and won the senior mile from A.S.Rogers of Mitcham in 4m.11s. - sixth man here clocked 4.14·4! Sylvan Deane (10·4) was narrowly beaten in his 100 yds. heat, being passed in the last ten yards in a blanket finish. The leading white-vested runner in the second heat of the 880 went by unrecognised as Belgravians cheered on Malcolm Robinson in the main bunch. When the first lap time of 54·8 was announced eyebrows were raised and on closer inspection it was seen to be Frank Wright. A barrage of voices carried Frank down the back straight and although caught in the final straight he qualified through second place in 1m.57·2s. - a good solo run. In the third heat John Thresher ran a personal best of 1.58·5. Belgrave's only representative in the three miles was Don Maclean who recorded 14m.57·8s., and as the crowd left was seen to be reclining against a post in the centre of the arena in a rather deflated state - a fitting end to the day. Eldridge, in his first season back from overseas performed a most creditable treble in the Beds. and Hunts. Championships at Luton, winning the 100 in 10·2, the 220 in 22·8 and the 440 in 51·7. items.sum: The new editors introduce themselves, explain this 28-page issue, and pick out Ray Hall, Peter Eldridge, Gerry LeRoy and Charlie Dabbs as performers to watch in Olympic year.
items.s: EDITORIAL The new editors introduce themselves, explain this 28-page issue, and pick out Ray Hall, Peter Eldridge, Gerry LeRoy and Charlie Dabbs as performers to watch in Olympic year. Dear Fellow Members, This issue marks the arrival of a new Belgrave year, a new President, and as you can see from the head of this page - new Editors. We thank the Bishop brothers for helping to establish our journal as a regular, healthy and expressive organ of Club activity, and we will endeavour to maintain the high standards they have set. We hope to introduce new ideas in future issues and are quite prepared to face adverse criticism. A big post-bag indicates a lively readership, so let us have your ideas too. The Autumn issue of the Belgravian always has plenty of news to cover. This,together with a back-log of results to last June, has enabled us to produce the biggest issue for many years - 28 pages. We should hastily point out however, that for ecconomic reasons it is not possible to continue publishing more than 20 pages, so the accent will be on quality rather than quantity. Although the summer season was not one of our most succesful there emerged several performers who could well gain higher honours next year. In the forefront of these is Ray Hall who has been outstandingly consistent in his walking, and whose quest for Olympic honours will be followed with great interest. Peter Eldridge and Gerry LeRoy, in their first fully active season for some time, showed that very little lies between them and representative honours of high note, and Charlie Dabbs, who at long last triumphed over persistent injury and established himself as one of the country's leading distance runners by his magnificent performance in the R.R.C. 25km event. Success leads to success and as a result many other stars are likely to be swept along in the wake of these athletes. We are firmly of the opinion that Belgrave is now equipped with the right sort of material to commence a succession of highly successful seasons- and what better year to start than Olympic year, 1960! items.label: No. 140
items.sum: Profile of the newly elected President T.C. "Charlie" Jones, a member since 1926, covering his hurdling, field events, walking and administrative work.
items.s: THE PRESIDENT - 1959/60 Profile of the newly elected President T.C. "Charlie" Jones, a member since 1926, covering his hurdling, field events, walking and administrative work. Our newly-elected President, T.C."Charlie" Jones, has certainly grown-up with the Club for he became a member as far back as October,1926, and has been very much in evidence ever since in all our activities. His early interest in our sport was derived from his father who became a member on the Club's formation in 1887, and could tell many an interesting story of the early days; and of the matches Bels v Bats (the long-since defunct Battersea A.C.) on the roads over the Chelsea Bridge—Battersea Bridge circuit. Charlie was also a cricketer of some skill, and as junior and youth athletic events were infrequently held at the time, he spent most week-ends in perfecting his fast bowling. Despite his activities on the cricket pitch he was at all other times to be found at Battersea Park Track- the focal point of all our Summer interest in those days. The hurdles always fascinated Charlie and his first club award was for the event. Later he was to win the Surrey County 440 yards Hurdles Championships, and later still to gain Surrey County place medals in the Hop Step & Jump and Javelin Championships. He competed in our Junior Cross-country teams, and in later years established himself as one of our best runners at 440 and 880 yards. His long-striding action was a delight to watch, and only inability to translate that terrific stride into a sprint over the last thirty yards or so prevented him from carrying off many Championships. His interest has always been extended over the full range of field events, and he became a Club Champion at the triple jump and was responsible for many excellent performances in this event and the long-jump. To add to this story of athletic versatility must be added the fact that Charlie was always (and still is) a most accomplished stroller both at home and abroad; and had he decided to try himself out as a race-walker it is certain he would have achieved further successes. Charlie had the good fortune, shared with many others, to be part of that tremendous enthusiasm which permeated the Club in the late 1920's and 1930's, when our star was in the ascendant, when each month saw more battle honours won, more athletic history made. Even the slowest man in the Club felt he was pushing the man in front of him, who was forcing the man ahead of him to give of his best, and so up to Club team level when the reserves compelled the selected team men to run every inch of the way. Charlie epitomised this intense Club spirit and was at every Championship urging and working for our successes. On the administrative side Charlie has done yeoman work and served in a variety of offices and been in on higher councils for the greater part of his Club life. His legal knowledge has been of the greatest help to us, his especial work for Field Events and Coaching within the Club still continues; and his work in the administrative field has been almost as versatile as his active career in our colours. We may be sure that Charlie Jones will serve us well as President. Let us resolve to serve him and the Club equally as well. A.A.Harley. T.C. "Charlie" Jones T.C."Charlie" Jones newly elected President 1959/60; member since October 1926; won Surrey County 440 yards Hurdles Championship Charlie Jones Charlie Jones President A.A. items.label: No. 140
items.sum: The new President thanks members for his election and calls for full teams and club spirit across all branches of the sport.
items.s: THE PRESIDENT SPEAKS The new President thanks members for his election and calls for full teams and club spirit across all branches of the sport. I view the bestowing upon me of the Presidency of this famous Club as the crowning glory of what seems almost a lifetime as a member. It comes to comparatively few and so is sure to be a treasured memory for the rest of my days. It came as the greatest surprise to know that I had even been considered for this honour. However having had it conferred upon me I would offer my sincere thanks and express my regrets that I was far away on holiday in Switzerland when the election took place. The latter however saved me the qualms of opening my mouth to verbally express my thanks. Enough of thanks, which I hope I have adequately expressed, and on to our aims as true Belgravians. We have a fine crowd of athletes in all branches of the sport in which we participate. We have our Internationals, and good,mediocre, and indifferent performers - rabbits as well. That is what a Club such as ours should have, it helps to make Athletics what it is. The burning spirit behind all and each should be "The Club" - to keep, to make and enhance its name and reputation. All can help in this - team spirit is what will achieve it. The turning out of full teams in all Championships,Competitions and even Club Matches should be the aim of everyone, even if it be only for the sake of not letting your Club mates down. We have had our successes in the past, but it is to the future we look, to repeat successes, achieve new ones and so to keep this great Club ever in the forefront of our sport. Being one of the few Clubs in the country which is so numerically strong in all its Branches -Track, Field, Cross-country, Road-running, Track and Road-walking - we have great opportunities and with your efforts doubled and re-doubled in the name of Belgrave successes must come. T.C.Jones The President. T.C. Jones T.C.Jones President Switzerland

items.s: KINNAIRD TROPHY - CHISWICK - JUNE 13th. Report of the Kinnaird Trophy at Chiswick, where Belgrave finished last of nine teams despite good track running. Although the final result proved to be our worst performance ever - last out of nine teams, our track men ran particularly well and were quite justified in feeling they had all the bad luck it was possible to have. The field event section were extremely weak and failed to collect a single point; most of the star performers being injured or committed elswhere. In the heats of the 100 yds. both Charle Jones and Sylvan Dean narrowly failed to qualify for the final with 10.1 and 10.4 secs respectively. Charlie, however, succeeded in the longer sprint with 22.3, whilst Peter Eldridge was eliminated with 22.2! Peter had previously missed qualifying for the 440 final by the finest of hairs breadths. With 50.2 Clive Ryan qualified for the final, but was unable to reproduce a similar time. With three to qualify in the 880 yards heats both John Thresher and Bob Taylor (Capt) finished fourth in their respective heats. John's time of 1:57.5 is a personal best . He is obviously a great prospect for the future. John Davies showed a most welcome return to form in the 1 mile turning the tables on Mal Robinson - his victor in the Club Champs., with 4:13.7 for 4th place, as against Mal's 4:19 for 9th. Yet another 4th place was recorded in the 3 miles where Pat Newell ran a creditable 14:23.8. Don Maclean was 12th in 15:23. 1.L.A.C. 50 pts. 2.T.V.H. 41 .. 3.WOODFORD GRN. A.C. 35 .. 9.BELGRAVE 9 .. items.s: MATCH v S.L.H. & ST.MARY'S COLLEGE TOOTING 17th JUNE. Report of a track match at Tooting against S.L.H., St. Mary's College and Ranelagh/Hermes, with Belgrave third among seniors and second among juniors. Brian Morris won the senior 'A' 220 in 23.8 whilst Alan Jackson secured second place in the 'B' with 23.6 - a grand start to the meeting. Dave Mitchell won a well judged quarter in the good time of 52.1 and Alan Black obtained further points by finishing 4th in the 880. Mal Robinson won an exciting mile in 4:23.2 after a ding-dong last lap struggle with Colin Wilson (S.L.H.). Ken Miller, making his first track apperance after foot trouble, did his fastest time to date finishing 4th in 4:32.6. As can be seen from the results, lack of depth in the team cost us the victory. However, an entertaining evening was concluded with Belgrave scoring their customary win in the relay. K.Blair and Bob Grant were 3rd and 5th respectively in the junior 100 yds. The former also did well in the 220, finishing 2nd ably supported by Dereck Wade, 4th, who is still a Youth. Bernard Linley, a great prospect, won the 440 in a canter from Mike Smithers, whilst our Junior Capt. Brian Kolbe was third in the 880 with 2:7.0 and Eric Penny 4th in the mile with 4:46.4. items.s: SOUTHERN SENIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS MOTSPUR PARK - JUNE 20th Belgrave performances at the Southern Senior Championships at Motspur Park, with a note on Peter Eldridge at the Midland Championships the same day. Brian Morris ran one of his best races of the season to record 48.4 secs to finish 3rd, behind Ted Sampson and Chris Lindsey who both clocked 47.7 secs. Pat Newell ran as consistently as ever to record a noteworthy 14:20 in the three miles. That time must now be Pat's average. Other good performances were made during the heats on Friday evening by Alan Jackson, with a 51.8 quarter and by Dave Mitchell (another fine prospect) who did a personal best of 1:56.6 in his 880 yds heat. John Davies was not at his best on this occasion and had to be content with a mile time of 4:16.8. The Midland Champs. were held on the same day with Peter Eldridge performing excellently in both the 220 and 440 yards. In the former event he finished 2nd to Robbie Brightwell of Birchfield in 22.0 secs and followed up with 3rd place in the 440, recording 50.7 secs - Well done, Peter! items.s: BROCKMAN TROPHY - CROYDON JUNE 27th Report of the Brockman Trophy at Croydon; the text says Belgrave finished seventh of twelve clubs, while the printed result lists Belgrave 4th. Although below strength we managed to finish seventh out of the twelve clubs competing, and several creditable performances were put up. Ron Holtum was first past the post in the 220 yds, with 22.8 whilst Brian Morris reversed the "Southern" result by winning the quarter in 49.3 from Ted Sampson of Blackheath. Once again John Thresher just failed to reach the final of the 880, this time recording 1:59.7. Eric Gebbett finished 8th in the 6 miles with 33:9.6 . In the field events D.MacCorquindale won the shot with a putt of 48'4½" , and Percy Porter was 2nd in the hammer with a throw of 157'0". items.sum: Report of the Cecil Fry Trophy at Woodford, where a weakened Belgrave team finished eighth, with Gerry LeRoy winning the quarter.
items.s: CECIL FRY TROPHY - WOODFORD - 4th JULY Report of the Cecil Fry Trophy at Woodford, where a weakened Belgrave team finished eighth, with Gerry LeRoy winning the quarter. Despite a strong wind to counter the 80 deg. temperature, the high humidity coupled with the loose state of the track made fast times impossible. This was not the only set-back, for we were minus all sprinters;they doing their best to record 2nd place behind the Valley, in the Southern 4 x 110 yards relay. It was therefore left to Gerry LeRoy to open our scoring. This he did with a vengance winning the quarter in a scintillating 49.4 secs. Alan Jackson was unable to reproduce the 51.8 he did in his heat and finished 6th, in 53.9 secs. Dereck Johnson ran as he liked to win the 880 yards, moving away from the field at 660, at which point our Dave Mitchell was lying second only to fade badly over the last furlong, and record 2:01 for 6th place. It was undoubtedly the heat which upset him, for as he said afterwards,"At 220 to go the heat hit me, and I folded up." Running his first track race this season for the Club, Ranjit Bhatia did well to close in at 9th with 4;23, in a good class mile. This was some three seconds faster and three places higher than Mal Robinson, who was however, running with a heavy cold. Our last track man Ray Middleton walked well to close-in fourth with 15:31.2 in the 2 mile walk. It was annoying to see only one field-events man but John Ware threw well to record fourth in the Javelin with 158'2½". 1. Ilford A.C. 47½ pts 2. Essex Beagles 40 .. =3. Cambridge/Woodford Grn. items.label: No. 140
items.sum: Report of the Central Road Services Sports at Langley Park, with a close medley relay and Belgrave winning the 3 miles team award.
items.s: CEN. ROAD SERVICES SPORTS - 12th JULY Report of the Central Road Services Sports at Langley Park, with a close medley relay and Belgrave winning the 3 miles team award. We received an invitation to send a medley relay and a three mile team to this fixture, held on a grass track at Langley Park. In the medley relay only three teams turned out - T.V.H., Met. Police & Bels, so the boys were assured of ' a pot'. The first leg, an 880, was run by Dave Mitchell and he handed over to Alan Jackson some twenty yards behind Linford (T.V.H.) and Frank Wright, running for the Police. We lost a little further ground by the time Charlie Jones received the baton, and try as he could he was unable to make any impression on Dave Segal. With the quarter to go the Valley had some forty yards lead,with the Police twenty yards up on the Bels. It looked as if we were booked for third place. But Gerry LeRoy had other ideas! Running like a man inspired he had caught Brian Morris, running for the Police, by the 220 and was hareing after the Valley. With forty yards to go Gerry had caught and passed the Valley, but Morris with his customary last burst, moved up to pass on the line. A wonderful run Gerry!. Rangit Bhatia and Mal Robinson finished equal second in the 3 miles, after a desperate last 80 yards sprint. With half-a mile to go Anderson, the Police Champion, and Rangit moved away from Mal after the three had interchanged the lead all the way. When 300 yards out Mal began to sprint and had caught and had his nose in front by the home straight. But Rangit was not to be beaten and they crossed the line to-gether, with a time of 14:52.5, a personal best for each. Don Maclean and Charlie Walker finished 6th & 7th, for the team to take the team award. items.h: MATCH v VICTORIA PARK - BATTERSEA - 15 JULY
items.sum: Report of a small July match against Victoria Park at Battersea, which Belgrave won in the senior match and lost narrowly in the junior match.
items.s: MATCH v VICTORIA PARK - BATTERSEA - 15 JULY Report of a small July match against Victoria Park at Battersea, which Belgrave won in the senior match and lost narrowly in the junior match. July fixtures are not generally well supported, and this was by no means an exception. However, those present were equally divided between Vic.Pk. and ourselves, and a four-man field was found for most events; giving the match an International flavour! Victoria Park, noted for their middle-distance runners duly won the 880 and mile events, whereas the Bels scooped the 100, 220 and 440 yards. Gerry LeRoy won a sparkling 440 running in the out-side lane, and the ever versatile Jimmy Heathfield returned to the distance over which he was winning 12 years ago, to win the quarter in 54.6 secs. Following his now customary warm-up from dressing room to starting line Don Maclean duly took third place in the mile (after having borrowed some spikes) with a creditable 4:26.6. Norman Caves was in excellent form winning the high-jump with 584" and the hop-step & jump with 44'10". The ever present Jim McGrath was second to Norman in the high-jump, and also the shot, and it was most pleaseing to see Andorka competing once more after examinations, to win the shot with a putt of 43'1½". In the junior match Douglas Crosbie, our most promising sprinter who is but a youth, was narrowly beaten in the short sprint with 11.4, but ran a perfectly judged 220 to snatch victory in 24.2. Under the watchful eye of Frank Simmons he should become a most valuable addition to our senior sprint ranks. Bernard Linley, who will soon be knocking at the door of our senior teams, finished second in his first half-mile with 2:2.1, and soon after, over his favourite distance of 440 yards ran out a creditable winner in 54 .5 secs. The steadily improving Eric Penny was second in the mile with 4:38.1 followed by Brian Kolbe in 4:47.8. 1.BELGRAVE 37 pts 2.Vic.Pk. 23 .. Vic.Pk. 28 pts BELGRAVE 25 .. items.sum: Report of the T.V.H. track inter-club at Alperton, highlighted by Gerry LeRoy's 440 win; Belgrave finished fourth.
items.s: T.V.H. TRACK INTER-CLUB - ALPERTON - 18th JULY Report of the T.V.H. track inter-club at Alperton, highlighted by Gerry LeRoy's 440 win; Belgrave finished fourth. With two to run per event, we started the day with one entrant in the 100, Dave Carter. He, however, was quickly out of his blocks and qualified for the final quite comfortably. In the final he ran with plenty of fire and determination to come 4th in a good class field; Omagbi[illegible]i of T.V.H., being the winner. In the 220 Dave was again our only entrant, but Jimmy Heathfield filled the breach, and although he failed to qualify was by no means outclassed. Dave reached the final once more where he ran exceptionally well to finish a very good third behind Lindsey of Q.P.H. Both Gerry LeRoy and Charlie Jones qualified for the final of the quarter, despite Charlie feeling unwell owing to an attack of hay-fever. In the final, Gerry was drawn on the outside and Charlie in lane three;with Futter of University of London A.C., an AAA finalist the week previous. After two false starts the field got away particularly fast, with the wind behind them. At 220 Futter appeared to be slightly leading from Charlie with Gerry a close third. But with 220 to go Gerry made his effort which took him into the final straight level with Futter. Showing great fighting spirit into the powerful wind he gradually forged ahead to complete the most notable victory of the afternoon, in 49.4. Dave Mitchell and Dudley Gordon both reached the final of the 880 where Dave was narrowly beaten by Haith of the Valley. In the mile John Thresher ran particularly well to gain third place in 4:26.0 behind Pegley and Darchambaud (S.L.H.) 4:23.0 and finish in front of Mal Robinson. Don Maclean was our only scorer in the three miles, finishing fifth after gaining two places in the last lap; thus gaining two valuable points. Jimmy Heathfield had sportingly agreed to run but was forced to drop out after a mile. It was a pity we were unable to field a full relay for under the scoring of 12,10,8 etc., we were deprived of a second and possible first place in the Match. 1.T.V.H. 39 pts. 3.Q.P.H. 29 pts 2.S.L.H. 37 .. 4.BELGRAVE 28 .. items.s: BELGRAVE CLOSED MEETING - BATTERSEA - 22nd JULY Report of the club's closed meeting at Battersea, with Norman Caves winning the Charlie Cook Cup triple jump and Mal Robinson edging Pat Newell for the Griffen Cup three miles. Two Club Championships were included in the meeting and two worthy Champions emerged. In the "Charlie Cook Cup", Norman Caves was successful with a Triple Jump of 44'11½". Second was Charlie Jones (43'0½") whilst a newcomer of very great promise in A.Underwood jumped 42 ft. We shall watch his progress with the greatest of interest. The three mile Championships for the "Griffen Cup" brought out a full crop and a great race resulted. For lap after lap, Pat Newell, the holder, Mal Robinson, our Mile Champion, and Jim Radford ran together; neither giving nor expecting quarter. From the bell the first two named managed to struggle away from Jim; then Pat seemed to have the race well won when he opened up a lead of ten yards or so with only a furlong to go, but in the last few strides Mal got on terms and won by six inches both runners returning a time of 14:2 5. Well done both, and an especial word of congratulations to Jim Radford on an eye-opening performance which gives clear evidence that our younger element are going to take us right back where we belong. items.sum: Lap-by-lap report of the club's 8th annual 20-mile road race, won by W. 'Digger' Pawsey, with Len Bishop first Belgrave man in 6th and Belgrave second team to T.V.H. Results list two runners at 28th as printed.
items.s: THE 8th ANNUAL BELGRAVE '20' - 15th AUG. Lap-by-lap report of the club's 8th annual 20-mile road race, won by W. 'Digger' Pawsey, with Len Bishop first Belgrave man in 6th and Belgrave second team to T.V.H. Results list two runners at 28th as printed. This was another event to suffer through fixture congestion - the Liverpool marathon and the Enschide event being held the same day. Despite this, a good field of 73 competitors faced the Deputy Mayor of Wimbledon (Councillor A.E.Ayres) to await the start in conditions summarised on the result sheet as "fine and warm, with a cooling breeze." After the first of the four 5 mile laps W.'Digger' Pawsey, of Mitcham A.C. and Brian Cooke of Haltemprice R.R.C., were almost a minute clear of the field. Then came Len Bishop in 3rd. place Eric 9th, Bob Glover (coerced into running by Ken Stimpson) 10th!, with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer running well together in 14th position - 1 min.49 secs. down on the leaders. At the end of the second lap it was clear that the first two places had been booked by Pawsey and Cooke, but Lennie was hanging onto third place despite nagging attention from Hopcroft (TVH) and Shave (HHH), whilst brother Eric had moved up to 8th. Bob Glover was back to 12th with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Reg Plummer hard on his heels. At this stage the Bels. and the Valley were neck and neck in the team race and excitement was mounting. Necks were craned to watch the runners approach 15 miles in the hope that Len had established third place, but unfortunately he had not had a good time this lap for Hopcroft and Shave had well and truly dropped him, whilst Elderfield (TVH) had also moved ahead by some 23 secs. Eric was still 8th and Alan now 12th fighting it out with Davies (TVH) and Paxton (HHH). Bob Glover was fading badly and was now a further 1½ mins. down, having been caught by Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer. Ken Stimpson, Geoff Pearson and Pete Mathews were 23rd, 25th and 26th. when the fifty-six competitors remaining went out for the final lap. Pawsey was a comfortable winner in the 2nd. fastest time ever recorded, 1hr 51:06 and Cooke's 1hr 52:12 had been bettered on only three occasions. Len Bishop was first man home for the Bels. finishing 6th, the same 23 secs behind Elderfield as he was with 5 miles to go. Eric Bishop had a most uncomfortable last lap owing to stomach trouble and dropped five places, however, the team result wasn't affected and the Bishop brothers were still our first three men home. Thus enabling Sam Ferris to write "Equally popular were the performances of the amazing Bishop brothers (Bishop A.C.) who placed Belgrave 2nd......" Joe Dooley finished strongly to finish 14th, two up on Bob Plummer and six up on Geoff Pearson, who had moved through from 35th with the most even-paced run of the day recording lap times of 31:20, 31:29, 31:46 and 31:51. Ken Stimpson also ran exceptionally well to finish 21st. Bob Glover came almost to a standstill on his last lap (37:02!), but still recorded 2hr 07:57 and took 2nd place in the handicap for good measure. Pete Mathews also had an encouraging run while Arthur Penstone was another last lap sufferer. T.V.H., won on superior staying power but with 10 in 29 the Bels. could be justly proud of their performance. The expert organisation of Bill Bird, and the assistance of Arthur Whitehead were most successfull and greatly appreciated in making this event a milestone in the road-running calendar. 1.W.Pawsey (Mitcham) 1.51:06 2.B.Cooke (Haltemprice) 1.52:12 3.G.Hopcroft (T.V.H.) 1.55:42 ......... 6.L.C.Bishop 1.58:27 11.H.A.Bishop 2.00:34 13.E.M.Bishop 2.01:59 14.J.Dooley 2.03:00 16.R.G.Plummer 2.04:16 20.G.Pearson 2.06:26 23.K.Stimpson 2.06:45 28.R.Glover 2.07:57 28.P.Mathews 2.11:32 29.J.McDonald 2.13:17 31.A.Penstone 2.17:28 39.W.Fairfield 2.23:22 46.R.A.Conway 2.32:27 1.T.V.H. items.sum: Tribute to Colin Collis on his retirement from competition after a comeback that ended with eighth place in the Polytechnic Marathon.
items.s: COLIN COLLIS Tribute to Colin Collis on his retirement from competition after a comeback that ended with eighth place in the Polytechnic Marathon. Colin has finally decided to call it a day! This great-hearted club-man who fought so hard to reach the top has now had to give way to the effects of further injury, a new home and the calls of family life. He had already retired once but the lure of athletics proved too great to resist so he began the the long trek back to fitness culminating in a Polytechnic Marathon performance which brought him home in eighth place, ahead of many better known rivals. Colin was no natural athlete. In his early days he was frequently seen amongst the tailenders, but eventually made the grade by sheer hard work. Many of our members would do well to follow his example. We have lost a valuable competitor but are sure to have retained a keen supporter, whose constant contact with the young might well reap dividends for Belgrave. Colin Collis COLIN COLLIS retired; 8th in Polytechnic Marathon Polytechnic Marathon

CLUB 6 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP - 19th AUG.
The "TOM CARTER" Cup
items.sum: Report and results of the club 6-mile championship for the Tom Carter Cup, won by Pat Newell in 30:46, with results of a 300 yards handicap and a junior 880 yards held the same evening.
items.s: CLUB 6 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP - 19th AUG. The "TOM CARTER" Cup Report and results of the club 6-mile championship for the Tom Carter Cup, won by Pat Newell in 30:46, with results of a 300 yards handicap and a junior 880 yards held the same evening. On a hot summer evening, and on a bone hard track Pat Newell the defending champion, and fifteen challengers faced the starter. After only one lap 'Glimpy' Jones and Dereck Crooks were a good twenty yards up on Pat and going as though they were after an international vest! Their lead was, however, gradually cut down and on the third lap the leading bunch was comprised of Newell, Walker, Moore and Bedford. During the second mile Pat broke away and was never again headed, while Don Maclean made one of his typical surges through the field to join the battle for 2nd. place with the other three. At three miles Charlie, only just recovering from injury, found the pace too hot while Mac had the opposite view and gradually pulled clear to isolate himself in 2nd place. Meanwhile John Moore and Archie Bedford were battling it out shoulder to shoulder and remained that way til the last half-mile, when John, who had almost been dropped a couple of minutes earlier, drew away to take 3rd. place. Pat, with no one to trouble him, slowed up appreciably in the latter stages but ran out a comfortable winner in 30min 46secs. Don Maclean was untroubled for the greater part and ran a very well-judged race. It was very good to see Gordan Biscoe and Mike Stearman out again, as it was to see such an encouraging performance from John Hilton. RESULT: The first two were inside first-class standard, with third and fourth inside second-class. Other events held during the evening were a 300 yards handicap in which Charlie Jones,off 2 yards, narrowly failed to run right through the field. items.s: MATCH v CAMBRIDGE H. v ILFORD A.C. v DEPTFORD A.C. CHARLTON PARK - 22nd. AUG. Report of a four-club match at Charlton Park in which Belgrave finished last in the senior and junior matches and third in the youths; the heading names Deptford A.C. but the results table prints Dartford. Apart from a full strength home team that won all three matches, the other teams were quite closely matched and although we were last in the Senior and Junior matches and third in the Youths, our lads performed very well. Jim Heathfield ran his fastest half of the season finishing 3rd in 2:02.2, while John Ware finished 2nd, 3rd and 5th in the shot, discus and Javelin events. Mike Stearman, now turning out regularly for us was 5th in a classy 3 mile field. Young D.Cocks showed his class once more by taking the Youths 880 yards in 2:07.8, with his comrade-in-arms, Pottinger setting about the field events with an excellent 36ft 7½inch H.S.J., followed by a 35'11" shot-putt. Bernard Linley was runner-up in both the Junior 100 and 880 yds with 10.8 secs and 2:09.2 respectively, and also had a fine 440 yds win in 51.9 secs. - an outstanding time for this track. Quite a treat to see so many 'claret and gold's' out for this match. Carter streets ahead of the apposition in a 10.2 hundred, and B.Linley yet another win in the quarter with 52.0 secs. Jim McGrath did his usual quota of events, missing out the long-jump this time, with second place in the discus, third in the high-jump and fifth in the shot. Jim's long-jump twin Dave Ansell did his duty with a winning jump of 20feet 10½inches. Alan Black was a close runner-up in the 1500 metres s/chase to Barry Collins (Surrey) who is the country's leading junior performer at this event. Alan's time of 4:23.8 probably ranks in the best dozen performances of the year. Mal Robinson,4:22.0 and John Thresher,4:24.5, scooped the points in the mile from a field of nearly thirty, while Dave Carter made it a double for himself with a 23.3 secs furlong dash; Sylvan Deane winning the other furlong event in a snappy 22.8 secs. The ever-consistent Jim Heathfield secured third place in the half with a time of 2:03.4 in a blanket finish, while Dave Ansell did an eye-opening 10.7 sec dash, in the 'B' event. items.s: LONDON CHAMPIONSHIPS - HURLINGHAM 5th SEPT. Report of Belgrave performances at the London Championships at Hurlingham, led by Gerry LeRoy's 440 win, and the loss of the W.J. Pepper Memorial Trophy. Outstanding performance of the day was undoubtedly the quarter victory of tenacious Gerry LeRoy over his international opponent Chris Lindsey, both recording 48.7 secs. An A.A.A. vest should soon come Gerry's way and could well be followed by even higher honours. Pat Newell and Charlie Dabbs produced two personal best performances in the three miles, finishing 3rd and 5th with 14:14.4 and 14:22.4 respectively. These times become first and second in the Club's season's rankings - an excellent performance. Dereck McCorquindale won the shot with a putt of 46ft 4½ins, whilest Dave Ansell secured third place in the long-jump with 21'4¾". In a very close 100 yds finish Sylvan Deane was 4th in 10.5 secs; and to complete the picture Eric Smith was sixth in the 2 mile walk. Despite our outstanding performances we relinquished our hold on the "W.J.PEPPER" Memorial Trophy, partly due no doubt to our having no Junior performers, and Eric Hall being unable to defend his 2 mile walk title, through injury. items.sum: Review, signed T.C.J., of Belgrave's 1959 field events season, naming the leading jumpers and throwers and appealing for fuller teams; it starts on page 27 and ends at the foot of page 12.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS REVIEW. Review, signed T.C.J., of Belgrave's 1959 field events season, naming the leading jumpers and throwers and appealing for fuller teams; it starts on page 27 and ends at the foot of page 12. The past season has been but a moderate one for whilst we have some good performers we have insufficient depth even up to a moderate standard. The main event for our men "The Sward", has been fully reported in an earlier edition. Injuries and illness beset us then and we have had a recurrence throughout the season, and more often than not have not turned out full teams in Trophy matches or even, to our disgrace, in our own home inter-club matches. Derek McCorquindale has no doubt been our best class performer. His new Club Championship best with the Shot of 49'9" and later the same day a 51'4" to win the Bucks Championships were two of his best efforts; he was also selected for A.A.A. teams. Dave Ansell has had quite a good season, attaining a place in the Middlesex Championships and winning the Maccabi European Championship with 22ft odd. He, Jim McGrath,and in the late season Reg Chamberlain (just back from the Forces) represented us in most of the Long Jumps. Jim McGrath is another "Iron Man" of the calibre of Mal Ash. His efforts in two, three or even four events at matches has been of inestimable help and in true Belgrave Spirit. He tells me that he has not been so fit as in some years,but gave a creditable show in finsihing 10th in the A.A.A. Decathlon with 4,405 points; just missing Standard. Pole Vault is really perhaps his best event, although he has run well over the 120 yards Hurdles. It was unfortunate that in this event Robin Tolson was unable to overcome an early season injury, and was never able to race. John Sams has done virtually nothing hurdlewise, except the Sward, but Pat Fox ran one or two reasonable 440's as second string to Charlie Jones. Norman Caves's early effort of 46'5" in the Triple Jump gave promise of great things but he suffered injury and it was not until late in the season that he came back with performances nearing his best. He again won the Beds and Hunts Championship. Dave Ansell has supported well in this event and Brian Jones, a new member, shows promise. Charlie Jones has also performed creditably in the triple and long-jump, but his hurdling seems to have gone to pieces; although in the Fulham Borough meeting a win in the 220 lows with 25.7 secs showed something nearer his true standard. In the High-Jump we have been really weak but perhaps Alan Stanborough will get back to his true 6 ft plus form next year. Jim McGrath, Dave Rasey and Norman Caves have all reached 5'6". The Javelin and Discus were weak events. John Ware has shown small improvement with a personal best of 169'10½" gaining second place in the Vancover Trophy, but is inconsistent. Bill Couzens found that Army life does not make for much improvement, more particularly perhaps because he has not been able to compete regularly; although he has thrown 169 ft and over in practice. Deszo Andorka has virtually had no Discus competition owing to examinations but we hope next year he will be able to get back his true form. Our other performers are all below 120 feet. Percy Porter, in the Hammer, has not reached his best but it is good to see Jock Whyte improving, winning the Middlesex only to have a bad day in the Scottish Championships. Ted Arnold has also shown a small improvement. Our Juniors seem non-existent, although Mike Smithers and Alan Blackett have appeared in the Jumps- but where are the throwers? The same might be said for the Youths, except for Dereck Wade in the Jumps. Norman Dewberry has now taken over as Secretary and I hope you will all give him your earnest support to make the Club what it should be and ensure we turn out full teams next year. We can win or help to win most matches and Trophies just by turning out a full team. We hold our Open Winter Field Events on 5th March 1960, when I hope all will turn out. /cont foot P.12 P.27. Field Events contd. Generally a disappointing season. Even the Club Championships' entries were sparse, and for Handicaps worse. One last note. I would like to thank everyone for their support particularly those who acted as Judges and Marksmen. T.C.J. items.h: SURREY COUNTY ROAD RELAYS - WOKING - 12th SEPT
items.sum: Report of the Surrey County Road Relays at Woking, where Belgrave were sixth in the new youths' relay and fifth in the senior 6 x 3 miles, with a closing note signed W.E.L. and an editor's reply.
items.s: SURREY COUNTY ROAD RELAYS - WOKING - 12th SEPT Report of the Surrey County Road Relays at Woking, where Belgrave were sixth in the new youths' relay and fifth in the senior 6 x 3 miles, with a closing note signed W.E.L. and an editor's reply. The afternoon's proceedings opened with the newly instituted relay for Youths, over a two mile course. Our four runners were Roy Bagley, Mike Smithers, Eddie Gaze and Eric Penny in that order. Seven teams faced the starter and at the end of the first leg we were fifth with Mitcham A.C. in the lead nearly half a minute ahead - Roy had run well but seemed to finish with too much in hand probably through lack of experience of this type of racing. Mike Smithers was unfortunate to get an attack of stomach cramp on the second leg and fell back to the last position. Eddie Gaze took over seventy seconds behind the team in front and over 2½ minutes from the leaders - a hopeless position; but,Eddie was not deterred and succeeded in almost catching up with Epsom & Ewell, who at this point ceased to function. Eric Penny could make no further progress although running steadily and well, and we eventually took sixth place. RESULT: (Bagley 11:11; Smithers 12:45; Gaze 11:58; Penny 11:43) The Senior race (6 x 3 miles) attracted fourteen teams. Charlie Walker took our first leg but could do no better than finish tenth with a deficit of 58secs. from Surrey A.C. Charlie Dabbs returning to racing of this type after a long series of injuries ran an exceptionally good leg to take us up to third place, only 22secs behind the leaders. Jim Heathfield could not hold this place under heavy pressure and dropped back to sixth and handed over to Clive Shippen forty seven seconds in arrears. Clive had come into the team at the last moment,although by no means fit, but managed to retain sixth place but with a margin of 72 secs from Herne Hill who were leading at this stage. Jim Masters took the fifth leg and remained in the same position, although losing ground on the teams ahead. Don Maclean who is in great form these days, went off last and with a good effort gained one place to bring us into fifth place. With a fit team we could have done better but in the circumstances the team ran well. RESULT: (Walker 15:07; Dabbs 14:16; Heathfield 15:30; Shippen 15:13; Masters 15:23; Maclean 14:44) Note; I can remember the day many years ago when all our team beat fifteen minutes - we won on that occasion - Heigho, for a return to such times!! items.s: L.A.C.RELAYS - HURLINGHAM - 19th SEPT. Report, signed C.J., of the L.A.C. Relays at Hurlingham, where Belgrave won the 4 x 440 yards in a meeting and club record 3min 20.7secs and the 4 x 110 yards, finishing sixth of eleven teams overall; with a photo of the 4 x 440 handover. Owing to the coincidence of the Poly Road Relay with this meeting, we could not field teams in the 4 x 1 mile and 4 x 880 yds steeplechase; we were also missing in the 4 x 220 yds hurdles, and the High-Jump. Our boys made amends in the remaining events however. Undoubtedly the best performance of the day was that of the victorious 4 x 440 yds team of Bernard Linley (still a junior!), Charlie Jones, Peter Eldridge and London Champion Gerry LeRoy. The main feature of this race was the really strong finishes of all lads, with Peter and Gerry both doing split times of 49.5 for their stints. Our time of 3min 20.7secs. set up a new meeting and Club record and put Birchfield, that great club of quarter-milers, into second place. We also beat Birchfield in the 4 x 110yds relay, winning in 43.2secs. With better baton-changing we would have beaten 43.0secs. The team was Peter Eldridge, Sylvan Deane, Charlie Jones and Ron Holtum,who showed a most welcome return to form in this race. An inch meant the difference between 1st and 2nd place in the Long Jump, where Dave Ansell (21'10") and Jim McGrath were squeezed out of their winner's medals. In the hammer Percy Porter and Jock Whyte gained 3rd place and John Ware, with the ever-versatile Jim McGrath,picked up 6th place in the Javelin. items.sum: Report of the Polytechnic Harriers Road Relay at Chiswick, where Belgrave's A team finished fourth with all eight men under 14 minutes, despite many absences.
items.s: POLYTECHNIC H. ROAD RELAY - CHISWICK - 19th SEPT. Report of the Polytechnic Harriers Road Relay at Chiswick, where Belgrave's A team finished fourth with all eight men under 14 minutes, despite many absences. It was regrettable that a fixture of this importance should clash with the L.A.C. Relays. Normally our middle-distance men could have split forces but on this occasion we had Newell, Robinson, Dabbs and Radford on holiday, Davies injured and Bhatia a 'flu victim; so it was decided to concentrate our remaining forces on the only major road-relay event we tackle before the "Brighton". In view of the unavailability list our less-than-usual turn-out of twenty was not unreasonable and enabled us to close an 'A' and 'B' team, and at least start a 'C'. Most of the 'A' team had done little to indicate their current form so the team was something of an unknown quantity. Len Bishop, with a season of distance running behind him, was given first leg to sharpen up his speed - as were Dennis Jones and Ken Stimpson, for the 'B' and 'C' teams. This opportunity they were duly given by Roath (Walton), who was first to the change-over, with 13:10 - fastest of the day and second fastest ever! Len ran remarkably well to finish 9th of the thirty runners, with 13:45. Charlie Walker took over five seconds down on the Valley man and in the course of chasing and catching his quarry he passed three others to give 'Jumbo' Masters the baton, in fifth spot. Our Jim got stuck into the battle with his usual spirit but had to give way to that promising Valley star, Hicks. John Moore showed that he was back on form once again, pegging back two more positions on the fourth leg to place us 4th at halfway, only 68secs behind the leaders. Alan Black held our position in the next circuit to exactly the same distance behind the third team (T.V.H.) as before - 28secs, although Woodford Green were moving up on our heels. Newly married Eric Gebbett, whose current running form was unknown, ran very well in his first race for some time, but Woodford in the shape of Eric Major (13:10) swept past both ourselves and T.V.H., to take third position. Clive Shippen, now almost fit again, held fifth place without losing ground on Woodford and handed over to Don Maclean for the final leg fifty seconds down on T.V.H. and thirty-three down on Woodford Green A.C. Don set about the latter in his most devastating style and turned the deficit into a lead of 28 secs, restoring us to a well-earned fourth place. Although we did not qualify for medals we were the only team to have run all eight men under 14mins each - consistency which should serve us well in the London-Brighton Relay - and our aggregate time was sufficent to have placed us second last year and to have won in any previous year! Brian Johnston ran exceptionally well in the 'B' team. It should not be long before he is a regular first team choice. items.s: 5¾ MILE ROAD RACE - WIMBLEDON - 26th SEPT. Report, signed W.E.L., of a club 5¾-mile road race at Wimbledon won by John Moore in 29:39, with full results and the handicap won by Chris Fairfield. Nearly thirty runners faced the starter on a fine afternoon, some with the prospect of being chosen to represent the Club in the forthcoming Brighton Relay; others with an eye to a handicap award and the remainder out to enjoy their saturday run. Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman. After leaving the common Don increased his lead and the field began to string out, but Ranjit had moved up and was profitting from a steady start. Down Copse Hill and turning into Cambridge Road the position remained much the same. But, no sooner were the hills reached than the sting went from Don and John Moore took over the lead. Before the Common was regained Clive Shippen and Charlie Walker had also passed the struggling Don and it was obvious that this was not to be his day. John went on to record a fairly comfortable win with Clive showing a welcome return to form taking second place and Charlie Walker,once again, placed in a Club race. Eric Gebbett, short of training, fell away after being prominent early on but Ranjit Bhatia and Len Bishop ran well. It was good to see Mike Stearman getting going again and we hope he will once more be a regular performer in our teams. Chris Fairfield, who has improved to the extent of four minutes since joing us last year, took the handicap with Arthur Penstone second and George Piddington a very keen lad who had also improved considerably over the past few months, in third place. The times generally were disappointing,due I was told to a troublesome wind, but more likely through general lack of training and the prospects of a win in the Brighton Relay on October 10th seem remote. items.s: FULHAM BOROUGH TROPHY - HURLINGHAM - 26th SEPT Report of the Fulham Borough Trophy meeting at Hurlingham, which Belgrave won without their middle-distance runners. This was yet another fixture to clash with a Road-Relay, or Race - this time the Club 5¾. We were therfore minus all middle-distance runners. Charlie Jones opened our quest for points recording 3rd in the 100 yrds - he later in the afternoon easily took the 220 yds hurdles, with a respectable 25.7 secs. Despite the presence of International Adrian Breacker the 220 yards was won by Peter Eldridge in a smart 22.0secs. Cruising home to a 49.8secs quarter win, Gerry LeRoy maintained his record of the last eight weeks - always passing the post first. Making a valuable contribution to our points, D.McCorquindale scored a double in the shot and discus, with 47 and 120 ft respectively. After dropping out of the 5¾ at Wimbledon, Trevor Hart dashed down to Hurlingham to win the mile, with 4:48 - running in bare feet! A second in the sprint-relay and we had won the trophy. A good show! (By some Irish thinking the Trophy winners received prizes, whilst the 'open' winners -run in conjunction - collected medals!) items.s: LONDON CLUBS - WHITE CITY - 30th SEPT Report of the London Clubs' Continental Relay at White City, where Belgrave lost the cup to Southgate after a muddle over stations. Inserted at the end of the London-Stockholm meeting, the London Clubs' Continental Relay, 440 x 330 x 220 x 110yds. Under the fierce glare of the floodlights Gerry LeRoy stepped on to the track and settled himself into his 'blocks'. With the 'Gun' and he was away very fast, in the outside lane. Level at half-way he drew away to hand over at the quarter to Peter Eldridge, a foot ahead of International Peter Higgins. Peter, taking advantage of the 'breaking-lane after first leg' rule, tucked behind Wrighton (Southgate) but found him just a little too strong at the finish. Unbeknown to him the officials had allowed stage three to break stations, but Peter was not to know and we lost many valuable yards sorting out the tangle. Charlie Jones sped after Southgate and pulled to within two yards, but last stage officials insisted on drawn stations and a further muddle ensued. When Sylvan Deane at last got away it was too late to catch Southgate. We therefore lost our hold on this Cup. For once not entirely our own fault! 1.Southgate 1:57.0 2.BELGRAVE H. 1:57.8 3.Achilles.
