items.sum: Walking-section notes by Jack Goswell covering the London-Brighton walk, winter plans, new members, the club's Open 7 Miles, and news of members including Stan Vickers' 20km win in Varese.
items.s: JACK GOSWELL REPORTS Walking-section notes by Jack Goswell covering the London-Brighton walk, winter plans, new members, the club's Open 7 Miles, and news of members including Stan Vickers' 20km win in Varese. The distance season finished with a first class performance by all the lads in the London-Brighton walk. And there emerged a new Club long-distance champion, in Ray Hall. He capped a grand season by finishing 3rd, followed by George Beecham fifth and Hugh McGreechan tenth. These three occupying the first three places in the Club Championships, held in conjunction. We now start on a new Winter Season and look forward to a good crowd out pack training, from the Hall. Steady work through the winter always pays dividends when the Championships come along. We should try and start the season by annexing the Southern "Garnet Cup" race once again (it's a few years since we won this) at Trowbridge. So all you 'Junior' walkers set your target on the first week in February, for this ten mile event - and then progress on to the major Championships. We welcome new members, J.Levison, Peter Tyson, John Unwin Peter Grant and John Taylor, and look forward to their steady progress. Our Junior team needs recruits so never lose the opportunity of enrolling likely lads! We hope to have a first class muster of club men for our own Open 7 Miles, on Nov 21st. Forty years old, and the oldest open seven in the Calender, make it a "must" in the walking-world. Prizes for this event have always been of the highest standard and every help is needed to enable us to meet the high cost involved. Our thanks are due to all those stalwarts who have supported us in this endeavour. Donations would be gratefully received by the Treasurer, or Walking Hon.Sec. We are pleased to learn that George Checkley is recovering from his illness, and hopes to start training again. Congratulations to Terry Clark on his recent wedding to Janet. Several Club members attended the ceremony. Terry, who is an R.A.F. Technician, is due for Australia and we offer him the best of luck and a resumption of his brilliant walking career when he returns. Bernard Eglinton has found another sister! This time in, of all places, Cyprus where he is to stay for two years. Best wishes Bernard may your family grow, we will miss you on the Road. Stan Vickers won a very good twenty kilometer walk in Varese, Italy on Sunday 27th September, when he beat his arch rival Ken Mathews by over two minutes. He certainly pulls out the stops on his trips abroad. After a four month lay off, due to leg-injury, Eric Hall is doing that steady work which is so necessary to reach peak. May a good winter season reach a climax in the Championships, with all those improving walkers making their presence felt. And doing their best to topple those at the top. All the Best, Jack. items.label: No. 140
items.sum: Report, signed E.W.H., of the London to Brighton walk, where Ray Hall was third and Belgrave lost the team race and the Edward Knott Memorial Shield to Metropolitan by a point.
items.s: LONDON TO BRIGHTON WALK - 12th SEPT Report, signed E.W.H., of the London to Brighton walk, where Ray Hall was third and Belgrave lost the team race and the Edward Knott Memorial Shield to Metropolitan by a point. The Brighton this year again dissolved into two distinct races, the two Metropolitan men, Thompson and Misson were locked together until just after Crawley, but Belgrave supporters were more interested in the third place and team race. Met. have relieved us of several long distance trophies this season and although they have provided more individual winners than any other club they had yet to win the Edward Knott Memorial Shield. George Beecham was more restrained than in other years and did not attempt to lead early on but as the leaders were doing over 7½ m.p.h. it was not surprising. The lads soon settled down and forgot all about the two wee men in front who were already burning up the road - someone said that as the morning was coolish they were keen to get to the seaside before sun-up! At Croydon Hugh McGreecgan was the leading Bel. in third place and as the field passed it was obvious that this year the team event would be a close thing. Several of the lads were not as fit as we had hoped and I heard one wife remark that her husband only turned out so that she and the children could have a day out! The gaps were appearing and with the forecast of a warm day now being fulfilled there was much speculation about times. By 20 miles Ray Hall was third in the cracking time of 3:3:00 he was being whipped along by "Digger" Clark who returned from his honeymoon to attend Ray. George was bashing along with brother Eric shedding a few stone on the bike, it is a question each year of which gives up first - the bike or Eric, but somehow they both survive. As for George I believe he smells the sea air at Streatham, Mac had eased up for a while and was developing a blister but with only 34 miles to go was not worried. Harry Shields was intent on time and motion study earlier in the year but this was not evident at this stage. However, you can always rely on the "old man" giving of his best when it is most needed. Newcomer, Jack Keown was making hay before the sun shone and Bernard Eglinton, the enigma, had begun to move through to his real place. Cyril Yescombe was very short of training but was having a go for several reasons. Percy Wilson was this year representing the Wilson clan and the other Bel. was Fred Rolfe who unfortunately had to give it best at Crawley. The race dosn't really get under way until Crawley and although Met. led in the team race all the way it was a close thing as only Don Thompson had a trouble free race; and we always felt we had a chance. Ray really consolidated his third place and George was not very keen on the idea of relinquishing his Club title, so he tore along in hot pursuit and with Don was the only one to record a faster time than last year. Mac was really in a bad way but with Fred Denny attending was able to peg back the vital place here and there. Harry closed in as fourth man, 'pot-hunter' Shields the veteran award winner; Bernard made a good recovery after a bad patch on Dale Hill and he just pipped Jack Keown by two seconds, Jack walked very well for a first-timer and was heard to say that it was easier than an Open 7. Cyril and Percy walked steadily from Crawley and gained several points but Met. with first and second were just too good, and won by a point! The attendants had the worst time, this year for instance one was given a bottle of stuff he couldn't open, somewhere around Gatwick he asked "How the hell do I open this", to which the walker gave the obvious, "Jam it in a door." Next year the attendant swears he'll take a door with him. Our attendants performed excellently and are to be congratulated! Well done Met. - but, keep the shield clean it's only on loan! Congratulations to: Don, on a great performance with the weather against you; Ray, for gaining perhaps another International vest for Belgrave and also on winning the Club Champs., and finally to Harry for the first Belgrave vets award since 1934. items.sum: Stage-by-stage report, signed W.E.L., of the London to Brighton road relay for southern clubs, won easily by Portsmouth A.C. with Belgrave sixth, with the team result.
items.s: LONDON to BRIGHTON (SOUTHERN CLUBS) -10th OCT Stage-by-stage report, signed W.E.L., of the London to Brighton road relay for southern clubs, won easily by Portsmouth A.C. with Belgrave sixth, with the team result. It seems to have been a foregone conclusion that Portsmouth A.C., with the help of Hyman and Tulloh (with or without shoes) would win this race. And so it proved, for in no uncertain manner this 'minor' club ran away from the rest of the field to come home easy winners, nearly three minutes to spare. It seemed a travesty of justice that after months of excellent weather this should be the day for the break to occur - the rain started soon after the start and continued without a let up for the full distance. We can be satisfied that we have qualified for the next National, but much work must be put in before we can hope to close the gap between us and Portsmouth, even supposing that this club can annex the April race. At least thirty seconds must be knocked off every runners time -no easy matter but by no means improbable. 1st Stage. Ranjit Bhatia (21.17). The usual dash along the embankment did not deter this runner from India, who had endeared himself to all with whom he has come into contact. Using his head in experienced manner he dogged the leaders and moved up at Cedars Road Hill, where he proved to be better fitted than most of his opponents. Briault of Brighton, romped away to a fourteen seconds lead and our lad came in third to give us a good start. 2nd Stage. Charlie Walker (26.22). No lack of experience here although everyone crosses their fingers when 'What do you think' Charlie sets off. When the Pompey runner moved away it seemed Chas. was to have one of those days , but when Haith (T.V.H.)and later White (Woodford) caught up it seemed to act as a tonic and he stayed with them to the end, where with a typical final flourish he kept us in third place, only thirty secs. down on Pompey. 3rd Stage. Pat Newell (29.49). Pat was switched from his usual leg to this stage as he had to return to work. He held his position by steady running, until half-way up the aerodrome stretch of Purley Way when Foord of Brighton, running in fine style, sailed past. Just before reaching Purley cross-roads Herring (Blackheath) caught Pat, and on the run in John Thorpe (St.Albans) also took him, so we were back to sixth and the gap between us and the leaders, still Portsmouth, was now forty-eight seconds. 4th Stage. Clive Shippen (26.24). Our new cross-county captain running in his usual reliable fashion set about his task in steady style. Unfortunately the runners ahead with the exception of St.Albans were in better form and the gap was widened. On this stage 'Dippy' Richards of Poly brought his club into the picture for the first time with the fastest run of the day. Belgrave still sixth but 75 secs behind T.V.H. now a short lead on Pompey. 5th Stage. Jim Masters (23.05). Jim must know every inch of this section of the road and we hoped that his knowledge would help us. But although maintaining his position by passing Brighton,by losing a place to Woodford he lost considerable ground on all the other runners ahead and we finished this stage over two minutes in arrears. 6th Stage. Alan Black (13.56). Alan did the fifth fastest time of the day, and set up a new Club record, but it must have been discouraging to him to find that three of those who beat his performance were ahead of him, with the result that we remained in sixth place. 7th Stage. Mal Robinson (19.10). Our three mile track champion also set up a new Club record for this stage, and gained on three of the five teams ahead, but was unable to do more than maintain our 2min 24sec deficit. Walton, with Judd as their representative had, however, passed Malcolm who in turn had moved ahead of Blackheath. In passing Gatwick Airport, how Mal must have wished for some jet propulsion!! 8th Stage. Charlie Dabbs (31.00). On the approaches to what is probably the most difficult, and longest stage, Charlie must have felt a little overwhelmed by the company in his coach - Hyman, Peter Cl[illegible]rk, Brian Fernee, Chapman, Roath, Perkins, Mike Barratt, George Brown, Maynard, Palmer and Sando just to mention a few are not designed to rouse one's confidence. Nevertheless Chas. was not upset by these "Names" and only four were able to better his magnificent run of 31mins (yet another Belgrave best). By the time Handcross was reached we still were in sixth place but had been put in touch of the three clubs immediately ahead. Portsmouth by virtue of a record breaking run by Hyman (29.14 and 26 secs off the previous best) had gone into a 2 min lead from Thames Valley. 9th Stage. John Moore(31.35) Despite the perils of dashing down Handcross Hill rapidly, John could not resist the urge, but paid for his folly by getting cramp and having to give ground on all the runners ahead. He did recover on the latter part of the leg but the damage was done. Tulloh was taking Portsmouth into an even greater lead and T.V.H. were consolidating their second place. We were now five minutes thirty seven seconds behind. 10 Stage.Len Bishop(21.16) If Len could have kept up the pace he showed over the first mile we would have wiped out Jim Peters' name from the book, and Belgrave would have moved out of sixth place. After making up some lost ground we fell further behind at the foot of Dale Hill. 11th Stage.Jim Radford (21.25) This was Jim's first taste of the Brighton road and although his time of 21mins25secs was not outstanding he can be well pleased with his initial run in bad conditions. It compared favourably with the runners ahead and a slight gain on the leaders was made for the first time during the whole race. The fastest time of the day was less than 30 secs better than Jim's, and the experience he gained will be invaluable. 12th Stage. Don Maclean (17.55) Don was given this stage as a result of his fine last-leg efforts in the Poly and Surrey Road Relays. Although the task on this occasion was far more difficult as Woodford and Walton were 95 and 82 secs ahead, respectivly; the latter setting fastest time of the day. However , Mac set off fully determined to overcome our disadvantage but had to give best and noticeably eased up in the last mile. But for this he would have set up the fastest time of the day, his 17.55 being only 6 secs slower than Walton's Avery - thus finishing in the sixth position we had held since Purley. To sum up - a moderate performance with a few bright spots in the shape of Bhatia, Black, Dabbs, Radford and Maclean. We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable). T.V.H. gave the chance to five 'first timers' and how well they responded. We have the talent but it tends to lie dormant. items.sum: Review by Les Stokell of the club's boys' and youths' section, praising its spirit and naming promising young runners, jumpers and throwers.
items.s: BOY'S AND YOUTH'S SECTION Review by Les Stokell of the club's boys' and youths' section, praising its spirit and naming promising young runners, jumpers and throwers. It was obvious to officials chiefly concerned with these sections at the beginning of the year, that the development of the 'Belgrave spirit' amongst the newcomers was the first most important essential. A group of youngsters had to be gathered who could be depended upon to train enthusiastically, to turn out for the Club when required and in whom could be inculcated some of the traditions and 'esprit de corps' which made Belgrave such a power in the athletics world until a few years ago. I think the course is proving a correct one, and because so much importance is attached to the 'morale' side of the lads' training, the development of the physical side i.e. fitness, strength, techniques etc., is proving so much simpler. When such keeness is shown it seems almost invidious to select particular names, but I think a few must be mentioned. David Cocks appears likely to prove a very bright star in the not too distant future; if his 4:43 mile and 2:06 half mean anything. Middle distance talent is almost in abundance so with challengers like Hampshire,Jarvis, Alan Mead, Hammond, Wiseman, Brown, Yeo, Redwood and Satchell not very far behind, David cannot afford to flag in his efforts. Our field events future is beginning to look equally bright and here I must pause to congratulate the winners of the boy's and youth's all-rounders medal competitions. Pottinger won the boy's with a score of 23 pts out of a possible 24, and J.Williams won the youth's. Pottinger,incidentally, has done twenty feet in the long-jump - Not too bad for a lad just fifteen years old. Young Wade, too, is beginning to make a name for himself, particularly in the jumps, and with Paddy Fyman,shot, Tony Moritz, discus 137 feet, and Chris Page,javelin, it appears that this side of athletics is being well taken care of. Our outstanding sprinter is undoubtedly Crosbie, who runs remarkably well every time he turns out for the club. Last, but by no means least, the youngest members of the Club; boys like Berry, Pymont (a very promising hurdler) and Nelson, having reached the ripe old age of thirteen or thereabouts have apparently made up their minds to "throw away their childish things" and to get down to serious training. Fine, but don't make it too serious yet. Remember there are still footballs to be kicked, trees to be climbed and,(dare I mention it!) exams to be passed. Les Stokell. items.s: MEDAL COMPETITION. Report, signed A.D.P., on the boys' and youths' all-round medal competitions won by D. Pottinger and J. Williams. It is encouraging to see more turning out for these competitions, though not everyone competed in each event, which is the purpose of the competition. D.Pottinger won the Boy's taking maximum points in the Shot, high-jump and long-jump; just failing by 1 point,in the 100 yds, to obtain a maximum aggregate for four events. Wiseman took 2nd place, with 3rd hotly disputed between E.Hawkins and N.Berry both with 14 pts, Hawkins taking it on highest position, although N.Berry had competed in every event. Hard lines! The youth's was won by J.Williams, who beat Dereck Wade by one point. (Dereck was last years boy's winner.) A.Mead was third, another who competed in each event, with a solid performance. In the 'boy's' it is interesting to note that D.Wiseman, who competed in all events won both the 880 yds and the 100; the 880 off 15 yds in 2:14.7, from a field of eleven, and the 100 off two yards in 11.5 secs. The corresponding times in the Youth's being, 2:16.4 and 11.9 secs. We shall be hearing more of D.Wiseman in the near future, no doubt. A.D.P. D. items.sum: Report, signed H.W.S., of the 1959 Annual General Meeting, at which T.C. Jones was elected President and Stan Vickers received a presentation.
items.s: ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING - 1959 BELGRAVE HALL -18thSEPT Report, signed H.W.S., of the 1959 Annual General Meeting, at which T.C. Jones was elected President and Stan Vickers received a presentation. The attendance of the A.G.Meeting was a little below that of recent years but even so, it was pleasing to see the goodly array of faces representing the various Club interests; especially the Youth's,Junior's and new members'. This is the one occasion when democratic priveliges can be exercised to the full, in order to ensure that those members elected to office continue to steer the Club on a progressively expanding course. Generally there were no fireworks; rather the opposite. The feeling was that the major offices should remain unchanged, and it was hoped that their re-election was a vote of confidence backed by the firm intention of giving them even more support in their many duties. The high-light of the meeting was the election of T.C.Jones as President of Belgrave Harriers. He was charmingly introduced by the retiring president F.R.Webb, who spoke of the great service that Charlie has given the Club during his membership as an athlete and official of over 30 years. A presentation to Stan Vickers to mark his European Games victory, and to commemmorate his English Native Record for the 1 hour and 8 miles walks was made amid acclamations from all. Stan expressed his appreciation of the gift and gave an amusing and most interesting account of his experience in Moscow and Helsinki. H.W.S. T.C. items.sum: Hon. Secretary's notes, signed A.A.H., on members' marriages, appeals for coaches, officials and schoolboy members, Stan Vickers' presentation and the change of magazine editors.
items.s: From the Hon.Secretary. Hon. Secretary's notes, signed A.A.H., on members' marriages, appeals for coaches, officials and schoolboy members, Stan Vickers' presentation and the change of magazine editors. We should like to express our congratulations and good wishes to Eric Hall and Mavis on their recent marriage. Mavis, as befits the only daughter of hard-working Past President Tom Morrell, has been handing out the pins and numbers for us for quite a while (and taking the money!), and our good wishes go to them both. Our good wishes also go to Eric Gebbett on his marriage, and Terry Clark who has also taken a wife unto himself. We hope to welcome Jack Brown back from Cyprus in Mar/April of next year, and it will be pleasing indeed to see him in our teams once again. In my Annual Report circulated to all members I tried to give an appraisal of our present position in the world of Athletics, and to indicate those departments in which greater strength would be a decided asset. May I again appeal to experienced Club members to come forward and assist as Coaches and as Officials? If advice or instruction is required we will try and fill the need. We are particularly anxious to build up our School-boy strength (thinking in terms of 12 years to 19!) and your help in introducing such members, and of assisting them to make the most of their talents once they are members, will be much appreciated. The presentation award made to Stan Vickers at the A.G.M., was an etched action study of Stan himself worked into the back of a mirror. An engraved tablet gave details of the wonderful records he acomplished a year ago and also referred to his winning of an European Games title last year. Stan has written expressing his sincere appreciation to the Club. We express our profound thanks to the Bishop Brothers for their great services as Joint Hon Editors, positions they now relinquish; and offer our good wishes to Malcolm Robinson and Clive Shippen who have taken over. May I ask for your full support to be given to our new Joint Hon.Editors? Our Gazette calls for team-spirit at its highest. It can breathe our hopes and aspirations, chronicle our disappointments, lead us to even greater things than we have yet known - but only if we will it to be so, and work for it to be so. As in so many other spheres of activity, if we lack enthusiasm, we lack everything. A.A.H. items.h: A Word from your CROSS-COUNTRY CAPTAIN.
items.sum: The cross-country captain's call to members for regular Tuesday and Saturday training and his hopes for the coming championship season.
items.s: A Word from your CROSS-COUNTRY CAPTAIN. The cross-country captain's call to members for regular Tuesday and Saturday training and his hopes for the coming championship season. Many of you will have already read my circular letter regarding the season now upon us. If so, read it once more and ask yourself whether you are supporting the training and racing programme as well as you might. It is most important that you keep Mal Robinson or myself informed of any developments likely to affect your immediate availability; many wasted entries and cards can thus be avoided. I shall always be pleased to hear from you and can be contacted at PAD 9281 (day) or SHE 0534 (evening). To recapitulate on points previously made. Tuesday evenings and Saturday afternoons are to be treated as "Club days" and I want you to appear on at least one of these occasions per week. No one in Belgrave is good enough or bad enough to necessitate solo training at these times and it will be considered sacrilegeous to the "new" Club Spirit to do so. No one is asked to race each week but everyone is expected to meet each week. To finish umpteenth in an inter-club match matters not one iota, it's where you come in the Championship event that really counts. So let us see everyone every Saturday, and if injured let us have your vocal support instead. The season's prospects are good, but depend entirely upon your support. Charlie Dabbs and Pat Newell could both get their County colours, we have a new three mile champion, and John Moore should be a real force this winter. I therefore hope to see Belgrave win the South of Thames Junior and the L.C.C. Championships, improve a further place in the Southern and finish in the first two in the Surrey County. With the return of George Flannagan to active training, the hope of a 'come-back' by Dave Baulch and the prospect of an active season from Ron Linstead our potential is indeed great. So get to it Belgravians and step up that training! items.sum: Report of Charlie Dabbs' win in the R.R.C. and Walton 25 km track race, setting club records en route and ranking fourth in the world best-ever list.
items.s: GREAT RUN BY CHARLIE DABBS. Report of Charlie Dabbs' win in the R.R.C. and Walton 25 km track race, setting club records en route and ranking fourth in the world best-ever list. "Charlie Dabbs Causes a Surprise". This was the masterpiece of understatement in Athletics Weekly with which Sam Ferris headed his report on the R.R.C. and Walton 25KM. Track race, on 17th Oct. After his fine effort in the London-Brighton Relay 7 days earlier, Our Chas. was reported to be feeling in even greater condition, and keen to undergo an even more exacting test on his newly acquired fitness. Ivor Edmonds (Bristol A.C.) was favourite for the title with J.Heywood (H.H.H.) probable runner-up. At 5 miles Dabbs and Edmonds had a clear 44 secs. lead and a mile later were timed at 31.11 (this would have placed Chas. second in the Club 6!). After 7 miles Charlie dropped his rival and was never again troubled. En Route, Tom Carter's 10 mile Club Record of 20 odd years standing went by the board, with 52.06,and 11½ miles were covered in the hour; bettering Dave Baulch's hour record by no less than 450 yards! New Club marks were almost certainly set for 7 miles and upwards. The 15 miles was covered in 78:29.4, and although Fred Norris's English Native Record was set en route to a longer distance, Charlie was only 65 secs. outside the official mark. His 25 KM. performance ranks him fourth in the World Best-ever, behind Zatopek, Popov and Norris! His 3 mile split times were 15.37; 15.34; 15.40; 15.48 and 15.50 - remarkable consistency for an athlete who had never previously raced further than 10 miles. 1.C.Dabbs (Belgrave H.) 1.18.29.4 (15) 1.21.16.6 (25 Km) 2.I.Edmonds (Bristol A.C) 1.19.03 1.21.50 3.J.Heywood (H.H.H.) 1.23.52 1.27.07 Charlie Dabbs Charlie Dabbs won R.R.C. and Walton 25 km track race; club records for 10 miles (52.06) and the hour (11½ miles) Sam Ferris Sam Ferris wrote the Athletics Weekly report Ivor Edmonds Ivor Edmonds favourite for the title J.
